My umbilical cord is buried here – Bagbin pledges continued support for Sombo development
items.description: Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin says he will never stop facilitating development in Sombo, stating that “my umbilical cord is buried here.” Speaking at the commissioning of a new administration block for Sombo Senior High School on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, the Speaker said neglecting his hometown would be like “breaking the umbilical cord” that ties him to his people. “A woman whose child cries of hunger while she is distributing funeral food is an irresponsible mother,” he told chiefs, teachers and students. “In other words, every child has the right to eat to its fill, the funeral food prepared by its mother. That is why I am duty-bound to visit Sombo ever so often.” Mr Bagbin said the new block was built to correct a long-standing wrong. Since its establishment, Sombo SHS had operated without a proper administration block. He described school administrators as the “hubs around which academic work revolves” and said they cannot perform when forced to work “under trees” or in “small, stuffy, dilapidated offices.” “When school staff sit in offices that do not befit their status, their self-esteem, and by extension that of the children they train, is greatly bruised,” he said. “When administrators and teachers cannot have comfortable spaces to do their work, they become demotivated.” The Speaker revealed the facility was built with resources he personally mobilised. “Woe betide you if you don’t maintain it” the former Nadowli-Kaleo legislature charged the school management to maintain the building, warning that he will be back to inspect it. “Each time I visit the Region, I will be here to inspect the use of this building. And woe betide you if I find cobwebs, cracks, peeled paint, broken furniture,” he warned, drawing laughter from students. He urged staff to build systems that foster collaboration, teamwork, and a positive school culture to improve student achievement. Chiefs, the Nadowli-Kaleo DCE, and the District Director of Education who attended the ceremony praised the Speaker for his continued support to education in the district.

items.title: La commune Tchaoudjo 2 lance l’élaboration de son PDC
items.description: Sokodé, 6 août (ATOP) – La commune Tchaoudjo 2 a amorcé, officiellement, le processus d’élaboration de son Plan de développement communal (PDC) lors d’un atelier réunissant les parties prenantes le mercredi 5 août à Lama-Téssi. Le PDC servira de boussole pour le développement communal sur une période de 5 ans, visant le bien-être social, économique, culturel, spatial et le développement harmonieux durable et résilient de la commune. Il permettra de faire de la commune Tchaoudjo 2, un exemple inspirant de planification territoriale intégrée, conciliant développement économique et préservation de l’environnement. Le document sera élaboré grâce à l’appui du programme « Restauration des paysages forestiers et bonne gouvernance dans le secteur forestier » (Forests4furure). Ce programme est cofinancé par l’Allemagne et le Luxembourg et mis en œuvre par la GIZ. L’élaboration de ce document s’appuiera sur un processus structuré permettant d’identifier les besoins réels des habitants, de concevoir des projets adaptés et de déterminer les sources de financement nécessaires à sa mise en œuvre. Afin d’assurer une prise en compte exhaustive des attentes locales, les citoyens seront consultés à chaque étape du projet. Le travail s’organisera en cinq phases, chacune comportant plusieurs étapes méthodologiques. Ces phases portent sur la préparation, la définition de la vision, des orientations stratégiques, des objectifs et des résultats attendus. Elles incluent également la programmation, la rédaction et la validation du plan puis son adoption par le Conseil municipal et son approbation par le préfet. Au cours de l’atelier, les parties prenantes ont suivi les grandes étapes du processus d’élaboration du PDC ainsi que la présentation des membres du comité de pilotage et du cabinet d’appui. Elles ont été éclairées sur le contexte de mise en œuvre du programme Forests4Future en lien avec la planification du développement. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Tchaoudjo, Bawo Moukadassi, l’administratrice des collectivités locales, Mme Pindra Samiya et le directeur régional de l’Environnement, Lt-Col Aledi Palakyèm ont invité chaque acteur à apporter sa contribution afin que le futur PDC de Tchaoudjo 2 reflète les aspirations des populations et constitue un référentiel pour les actions de développement des prochaines années. Le maire de la commune Tchaoudjo 2, Kiliou Kokolou a confirmé l’engagement de l’exécutif communal à accompagner et à œuvrer pour la bonne réussite de ce processus qui va définir la bonne trajectoire d’un développement inclusif et durable pour leur municipalité. Le conseiller technique de Forests4Future/GIZ, Dr Koumantiga Dabitora a réitéré l’engagement des partenaires à continuer d’accompagner le Togo dans ses efforts pour restaurer ses paysages forestiers, renforcer la gouvernance locale et améliorer les moyens de subsistance des populations. La rencontre a pris fin par une opération de mise en terre de plants. ATOP/MEK/JK/BV

items.title: Our deeds and sacrifices speak after we are gone – Sheikh Aremeyaw at helicopter crash memorial
items.description: The spokesperson for the National Chief Imam, Sheikh Aremeyaw Shaibu, has called on Ghanaians to reflect deeply on the purpose of life, the certainty of death and the importance of leaving behind enduring legacies of service, as the nation marked the first anniversary of the tragic military helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight distinguished Ghanaians. Speaking during the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service held in Accra on Thursday, August 6, Sheikh Shaibu said the solemn gathering was not only to mourn the departed but also to inspire the living to embrace lives of purpose, sacrifice and accountability before God. Addressing a congregation of government officials, religious leaders, bereaved families and members of the public, he described the occasion as one of silence, reflection and renewed commitment to national service. “We meet this morning in the stillness, silence and the momentous nature of this occasion to remember those whom we lost through a plane crash exactly a year ago,” he said. “But as we do so, we also do so with a sense of equanimity and mission.” The memorial honoured eight prominent Ghanaians whose lives were cut short in the air crash while they were undertaking official national duties. Their sudden deaths plunged the nation into mourning, prompting an outpouring of grief from citizens across the country and tributes from the international community. The victims were Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah , Minister for Defence; Alhaji Dr Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed , Minister for Environment, Science and Technology and Member of Parliament for Tamale Central; Alhaji Muniru Mohammed Limuna , Acting Deputy National Security Coordinator; Samuel Sarpong , Vice-Chairman of the National Democratic Congress; Samuel Aboagye , Deputy Director-General of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO); Squadron Leader Peter Baafemi Anala ; Flying Officer Manaen Twum Ampadu ; and Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah of the Ghana Air Force. The eight lost their lives when the military helicopter crashed in the Adansi area of the Ashanti Region while en route to Obuasi on official government business. Their passing was regarded as a significant national loss, not only because of the positions they occupied but also because of their commitment to duty, leadership and national development. One year after the tragedy, the inter-faith service brought together people of different faiths to honour their memory under the theme “Lives of Service, Legacies of Sacrifice.” Drawing on Islamic teachings, Sheikh Shaibu reminded mourners that while death often comes unexpectedly and remains difficult for human beings to comprehend, it ultimately occurs according to the will of God. He said the departed neither chose the manner nor the timing of their deaths, emphasising that every life unfolds according to God’s divine plan. “In our belief, God’s will continues every moment to unfold in different aspects of our lives, including the circumstances under which we die,” he said. “Talented heroes did not choose to die the way they did. Nor did they consult their families before their passing. It happened because God’s will unfolded, and in surrender to Him we declare: ‘Indeed, from Allah we came, and unto Him is our return.'” READ ALSO: Defence Minister, Environment Minister, 6 others confirmed dead in military helicopter crash He noted that death remains one of life’s greatest mysteries, arriving without warning and sparing no one regardless of status, age or achievement. “Every human being has a destiny that is undeniable and irresistible,” he said. “When God’s appointed time comes, no soul can delay it.” According to him, life should never be regarded as accidental or meaningless, but rather as a divine assignment entrusted to each person. “God has a purpose for our creation,” he stated. “We are here not merely to exist but to accomplish a mission and fulfil the purpose for which we were created.” Quoting passages from the Holy Qur’an, Sheikh Shaibu challenged the congregation to consider whether human beings believed they had been created simply for amusement. “Do you imagine that God granted you this life without purpose?” he asked. “Every success, every failure and every accomplishment will ultimately be examined by the Creator.” He explained that accountability before God remains one of the central principles of Islamic teaching, stressing that individuals would one day answer for how they used the opportunities and responsibilities entrusted to them during their earthly lives. Sheikh Shaibu spoke about how expressions of public grief often diminish with time, even after tragedies that profoundly affect the nation. Recalling the period immediately after the crash, he said he frequently drove past the area near the funeral venue where wreaths had been laid in honour of the deceased. The sight of countless floral tributes and portraits, he said, reflected the nation’s collective sorrow. However, only weeks later, the wreaths had disappeared. “I asked myself, ‘Where are they?'” he recounted. “Those wreaths represented our emotions and how deeply we were affected by their deaths. Yet within a short period, that memory gradually faded from our minds.” He said commemorative occasions such as the national memorial were essential because they renewed remembrance and ensured that the sacrifices of those who died in service to the nation were not forgotten. Quoting further from the Qur’an, Sheikh Shaibu assured mourners that God never allows the righteous deeds of faithful believers to be lost. He said every act of service, sacrifice and devotion is permanently recorded by God and will receive its due reward. “The Qur’an tells us that those who believe and perform righteous deeds will never have their efforts reduced to nothing,” he said. He urged those in attendance to think beyond material achievements and instead consider the lasting impact they would leave on society. “My dear brothers and sisters, this is where those of us who are alive must reflect on the traces we want to leave behind,” he said. “Our deeds, our service and our sacrifices are what will continue to speak for us after we are gone.” Sheikh Shaibu reflected to the theme of the memorial service, saying the lives of the eight departed public servants demonstrated the enduring value of commitment to duty and sacrifice for the nation. He encouraged Ghanaians to honour their memory not only through annual commemorations but also by embracing lives characterised by integrity, compassion, service and accountability. “The theme, ‘Lives of Service, Legacies of Sacrifice,’ should not merely describe those we have lost,” he said. “It should become the guiding principle for those of us who remain.”

Bribery cases decline as more Ghanaians feel included in governance – GSS report
items.description: The Government Statistician, Dr Alhassan Iddrisu, has said the nation is making measurable progress in improving governance, with fewer citizens paying bribes and more people feeling included in public decision-making, but warned that the gains remain fragile and must be sustained. Launching the Governance Series Wave 3 Report in Accra last Tuesday, Dr Iddrisu said the findings reflected the everyday experiences of Ghanaians in accessing public services and underscored the need for stronger institutions to promote transparency, accountability, and inclusive governance. He said the report tracked the experiences of the same respondents across all 16 regions and measured whether they were asked to pay unofficial fees for public services and whether they felt their voices influenced decisions affecting their lives. Dr Iddrisu said 69 out of every 100 Ghanaians who interacted with public officials during the second half of 2025 reported being asked to pay something extra for services to which they were already entitled. He described the finding as more than a statistic, saying it represented the experiences of citizens at health facilities, police checkpoints, passport offices, and other public service delivery points. “The Governance Series is more than a report. It is a mirror of how citizens are treated, a compass for reform and a catalyst for stronger institutions and better governance,” he said. Mixed picture Despite that finding, the Government Statistician said the overall trend for 2025 was encouraging. He explained that the proportion of Ghanaians who had contact with public officials increased from 56 per cent in 2024 to 72 per cent in 2025, representing about 1.6 million additional interactions, yet the proportion that paid bribes declined from 18.4 per cent to 16.8 per cent. He added that payments exceeding GH¢1,000 fell by almost half, from 14.7 per cent to 7.6 per cent. Dr Iddrisu also said repeated bribery was becoming less common, with the proportion of respondents who paid bribes five or more times falling sharply from 24 percent in Wave 2 to less than four percent in Wave 3. He said more citizens were refusing to pay bribes, with refusals increasing from 3.0 per cent to 4.9 per cent, indicating growing public confidence to reject illegal demands. Although the police, particularly the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), remained the institution with the highest reported bribery incidence, he said the rate improved from 61 percent in 2024 to 53.6 percent in 2025, showing that targeted interventions could make a difference. Citizen voice Dr Iddrisu said the report also recorded significant progress in citizen participation. He said the proportion of Ghanaians who felt they had no say in decisions affecting their lives declined from 42 percent in 2024 to 30 percent in 2025, although young people, the elderly, and the unemployed still felt least heard. He explained that the findings showed that governance reforms were producing results, but progress remained vulnerable to reversal, making it necessary to continue measuring governance indicators every six months. Call Dr Iddrisu said findings from the previous report had already prompted engagements with public institutions identified as high-risk, leading to commitments to strengthen integrity systems. He urged the government to digitise public services, publish official fees, protect citizens who refuse to pay bribes, improve transparency in public decision-making, and deliberately include vulnerable groups in governance. Dr Iddrisu further urged the government to integrate the findings into national planning and budgeting. He also called on businesses to insist on official payment channels while urging citizens to report bribery. He further encouraged civil society organisations and the media to use the report to promote accountability and strengthen democratic governance.

items.title: Dunenyo Za 2026 : Des rites de libation annoncent la fête à Sagbado
items.description: Lomé, 6 août (ATOP) – Les autorités traditionnelles de Sagbado, dans la commune Golfe 7, ont organisé, une cérémonie de libation pour annoncer la célébration de la fête traditionnelle Dunenyo Za le jeudi 6 août au palais royal de Semekonawo. Cette cérémonie rituelle a été marquée par des invocations adressées aux mânes des ancêtres afin de solliciter leur protection, leur bénédiction et leur bienveillance pour le bon déroulement des festivités. Les officiants ont également formulé des prières en faveur de l’unité, de la paix et du renforcement de la cohésion sociale entre les fils et filles d’Aflao, en particulier ceux de Sagbado. Ils ont aussi imploré la grâce divine sur le Président du Conseil, les membres du gouvernement ainsi que sur l’ensemble des autorités du pays, afin que règnent la paix, la stabilité au Togo. Le représentant du trône de Semekonawo, Togbui Alley-Fiago, a rappelé que Dunenyo Za est une fête de rassemblement qui offre aux fils et filles de la localité un cadre privilégié de retrouvailles entre les générations. Selon lui, cette célébration favorise le raffermissement des liens entre les communautés et contribue à la transmission des valeurs ancestrales aux jeunes. Il a souligné que cette fête constitue également un important levier de promotion du patrimoine culturel local et a encouragé la jeunesse à s’approprier les us et coutumes hérités des ancêtres, afin d’en assurer la préservation et la transmission aux générations futures. L’apothéose est prévue pour le 15 août prochain. ATOP/AO/MD

items.title: L'Iran et Oman avancent sur une nouvelle route maritime dans le détroit d'Ormuz
items.description: L'Iran et Oman ont trouve dans la soiree du 5 août un accord de principe sur le trace d'un nouvel itineraire de transit pour les navires dans le detroit d'Ormuz, selon Teheran. Sa mise en œuvre reste cependant conditionnee a l'evolution des tensions avec les etats-Unis, qui ont impose un blocus des ports iraniens. « Les coordonnees geographiques du trace envisage par les deux parties ont ete approuvees », a declare Esmaïl Baghaï, porte-parole de la diplomatie iranienne. Les deux pays travaillent desormais a une declaration commune, sous reserve qu'« aucune partie tierce ne vienne entrer dans le processus ». Un accord dependant de Washington Le detroit d'Ormuz, par lequel transitait avant la guerre pres d'un cinquieme du commerce mondial des hydrocarbures, est redevenu un point de confrontation majeur depuis la reprise des hostilites entre Washington et Teheran debut juillet. L'Iran affirme vouloir organiser la reouverture avec Oman, autre pays riverain, plutot qu'avec les etats-Unis. Le president americain, Donald Trump, assure pourtant que Teheran souhaite parvenir a un accord avec Washington pour retablir la circulation maritime. Son vice-president, J.D. Vance, a reconnu mercredi 5 août que les negociations etaient difficiles, evoquant des « avancees et des revers » dans les discussions. « ca va etre complique et ca va prendre du temps pour y parvenir », a-t-il declare. Pour Teheran , un eventuel accord avec Mascate ne signifierait pas automatiquement un retour a la libre circulation d'avant-guerre. Esmaïl Baghaï accuse les etats-Unis de maintenir des « actions agressives et menacantes » autour du detroit, notamment via leur blocus naval. La situation reste tendue dans la region : une agence maritime britannique a signale jeudi 6 août qu'un petrolier avait entendu des explosions pres des cotes omanaises, illustrant les risques persistants autour de cette voie maritime strategique.

items.title: 8è édition de Dunenyo Za : Les communautés de Djidjolé sollicitent la bénédiction des ancêtres
items.description: Lomé, 6 août (ATOP) – Le chef du canton de Djidjolé, Togbui Dzidzoli Awounor Détu X, a présidé une cérémonie de libation marquant le lancement des activités de la 8 è édition de Dunenyo Za, le jeudi 6 août à Lomé. Cette édition est placée sous le thème « Avec Dunenyo Za, valorisons la jeunesse et la femme, acteurs du développement durable ». Les organisateurs entendent promouvoir les valeurs culturelles tout en mettant en lumière le rôle de la jeunesse et des femmes dans le développement de la communauté. Séance de danse Le chef du canton de Djidjolé a fait savoir que cette cérémonie de libation a pour objectif d’informer les ancêtres de la tenue de la fête et de solliciter leur protection ainsi que leurs bénédictions pour le bon déroulement des manifestations. « Ce jeudi est un jour sacré consacré aux rituels et à nos divinités. Nous devons informer nos ancêtres de la célébration de cette fête afin qu’ils nous accordent leur grâce et leur bénédiction. C’est dans cet esprit que nous avons organisé cette cérémonie de libation et de sacrifice, afin que Dunenyo Za soit une réussite », a expliqué Togbui Dzidzoli Awounor Détu X. Les activités de cette 8 è édition se poursuivront jusqu’au 15 août, date de l’apothéose. Des jeux traditionnels, des conférences-débats, des journées dédiées à la jeunesse et aux femmes sont prévus. ATOP/MD/AO

items.title: Tivaouane : « Ensemble, penser et agir par le verbe de l’Unicité », thème du Gamou 2026
items.description: Le Comité scientifique du Gamou a publié un document d’orientation destiné à éclairer le thème central de l’édition 1448 H/2026, retenu par le Khalife général des Tidianes, Serigne Babacar Sy Mansour : « Ensemble, penser et agir par le verbe de l’Unicité (Tawhid) ». Ce texte met en avant le Tawhid comme fondement de la foi musulmane, mais aussi comme socle de l’unité, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble. Selon le document, la parole de l’Unicité (Lâ ilâha illa Allah) ne se réduit pas à une simple profession de foi. Elle constitue un engagement invitant chaque croyant à faire preuve de sincérité, de justice, de fraternité, de solidarité et de respect d’autrui, en accord avec les enseignements du Saint Coran et de la Sunna. Pour le Comité scientifique, une communauté durablement unie repose sur une croyance authentique, une parole véridique et des comportements exemplaires. Le texte rappelle également que les enseignements de Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy (RTA) s’inscrivent pleinement dans cette vision. Son œuvre a constamment mis l’accent sur la purification des cœurs, l’éducation spirituelle, la quête du savoir et le renforcement des liens fraternels comme conditions de l’épanouissement de la communauté musulmane. Face aux défis sociaux, culturels et numériques, le Comité scientifique appelle les fidèles à faire de la parole un instrument de rapprochement plutôt que de division. Il les invite à privilégier le dialogue, la bienveillance et la responsabilité dans les échanges, y compris sur les espaces numériques, afin de préserver l’unité et la paix sociale. Ce document de référence servira de cadre aux conférences, causeries religieuses et autres activités prévues durant le Gamou 2026. L’ambition est de permettre aux fidèles de s’approprier le message de cette édition et d’en faire un levier de renouveau spirituel, de cohésion communautaire et de promotion du bien commun. Salla GUEYE

items.title: Highlife to the World campaign for Black Star Experience 2027 launched in Barcelona
items.description: Highlife to the World: The Black Star Experience 2027 was officially launched in Barcelona on Sunday, 2nd August 2026, marking the start of a global campaign to promote Ghana’s iconic music genre ahead of the country’s 70th anniversary celebrations. The launch took place at Seasea Club and was led by Ghana’s Ambassador to the Kingdom of Spain, H.E. Kalsoume Sinare Baffoe, and the Executive Secretary of the Creative Arts Agency, Gideon Aryeequaye, in the presence of dignitaries and music legends. The campaign will feature workshops, masterclasses and major concerts in selected cities across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas as part of activities marking Ghana’s 70th anniversary in 2027. “The Creative Arts Agency sees this partnership as the best platform to put talented Ghanaian creatives on international platforms, with the key goal of promoting and preserving Highlife for future generations,” said Gideon Aryeequaye, Executive Secretary of the Creative Arts Agency. Presidential Aide and Coordinator of the Black Star Experience Rex Omar, H.E. Meredith Naakai Lamptey, Ghana’s Permanent Delegate to UNESCO in Paris, and H.E. Kalsoume Sinare Baffoe also pledged their support to ensure Highlife receives greater global recognition as Ghana prepares to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The launch featured performances by Jupitar, Bessa Simons, Obrafour, Stonebwoy and the Lucky Star Band, with opening sets by DJ Logs, DJ Demo, DJ King Solo and Nigerian guest DJ Enny. “We are so excited to support a brand as big as the one that birthed Afrobeat. We hope to host H2TW every year for our audience,” said Lara Torres, Events Lead at Seasea Club. H2TW is organised by Showbiz Africa, the Musicians Union of Ghana, the Black Star Experience, Benayacon and the Ghana Embassy in Madrid, in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Creative Arts Agency, the Ghana Tourism Authority and the National Folklore Board. The full roadmap for H2TW 2027 will be unveiled at the maiden Highlife Festival, which will be hosted later this year at Laboma Beach Resort in Accra. The Black Star Experience is Ghana’s flagship culture, arts and tourism initiative, aimed at promoting the country’s creative industries and cultural heritage on the global stage.

items.title: China’s Ambassador Cong Song says people-to-people exchanges are key to strengthening Ghana-China relations
items.description: China’s Ambassador to Ghana, Cong Song, has underscored the importance of strengthening people-to-people relations to deepen mutual understanding and enhance long-term cooperation between Ghana and China. He said the future of Ghana-China relations depended not only on trade, investment, and infrastructure development but also on stronger human connections fostered through education, culture, and professional exchanges. Mr Song made the remarks during the 2026 Ghana-China Media Fellowship organised by the Africa-China Centre for Policy and Advisory (ACCPA) in Accra. Speaking on the importance of dialogue among civilisations, he said mutual respect and engagement were essential for promoting peaceful coexistence and sustainable cooperation. He noted that differences in history, culture, and levels of development should be viewed as opportunities for learning and collaboration rather than sources of division. “No civilisation is superior to another,” he said, adding that countries could achieve greater progress by appreciating one another’s experiences and development paths. The Ambassador observed that exchanges between Ghana and China had expanded significantly in recent years, particularly in the areas of education, culture, and professional development. He said many Ghanaian students continued to pursue higher education and professional training in China, while Chinese language education and cultural programmes were witnessing increasing growth in Ghanaian universities and other institutions. Mr Song also noted that journalists, researchers, artists, and young professionals from both countries were increasingly participating in cross-cultural initiatives aimed at promoting understanding and cooperation. Touching on the designation of 2026 as the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, he described the initiative as an important platform for expanding collaboration in education, tourism, media, youth development, and cultural dialogue across the continent. According to him, such exchanges complemented economic and diplomatic engagements by fostering stronger interpersonal relationships between Africans and Chinese. Mr Song, however, stressed that genuine mutual understanding required exchanges to move in both directions. He said Ghanaian and African histories, cultures, and perspectives should receive greater visibility in China, just as Chinese culture and development experiences continue to attract growing interest in Ghana. The Ambassador identified language barriers, inadequate public knowledge, and lingering stereotypes as some of the challenges that needed to be addressed to strengthen people-to-people relations. He said the media had a crucial role to play in bridging those gaps through balanced, accurate, and informed reporting that highlighted both the opportunities and challenges in Ghana-China relations. Mr Song urged journalists to uphold objective reporting standards to foster trust, dispel misconceptions, and encourage constructive dialogue between the peoples of the two countries. Looking ahead, he said the long-term strength of Ghana-China relations would depend not only on government agreements, trade volumes, and infrastructure projects, but also on the ability of ordinary Ghanaians and Chinese citizens to interact, learn from one another, and build lasting friendships. He expressed confidence that sustained cultural and educational exchanges would further strengthen the comprehensive strategic partnership between Ghana and China while contributing to closer China-Africa cooperation.

items.title: Ken Ashigbe questions commitment of MMDCEs, police commanders in fight against galamsey
items.description: Anti-galamsey campaigner, Ing. Ken Ashigbe, has criticised the lack of commitment from some local government and security officials, arguing that the leadership required to eliminate illegal mining is not forthcoming. According to him, some Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) and local Police Commanders are not showing enough interest in the fight against illegal mining, making efforts to tackle the menace at the grassroots level more difficult. Speaking on the state of the fight against galamsey as Ghana marked one year since the tragic helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight state officials while they were travelling to support the anti-illegal mining campaign, Ing. Ashigbe said local leadership remains a major gap in the fight. READ ALSO: Ghana’s Defence Minister, 7 others die in tragic helicopter crash “For me, the big thing is that the leadership that we need to be able to deal with this, we are not seeing it, especially at local level,” he said. “I will plead with His Excellency the President; he has mentioned that galamsey was going to be a KPI for the MCEs, so how come none of these MCEs, where galamsey is happening right close to them, and nobody is caught and held accountable? For me, that is the slippery slope that we are on, and all of us need to wake up and find a way of supporting our country so that these people who have lost their lives in carrying out national duty, at least, their lives should mean something; otherwise, we would have failed,” he added. Ing. Ashigbe stressed that MMDCEs and security commanders operating within affected communities play a critical role in enforcing mining regulations and ensuring that illegal miners do not return to reclaimed areas. His comments add to growing concerns from environmental advocates that a coordinated approach involving central government, local authorities, traditional leaders and security agencies is needed to achieve lasting results in the fight against illegal mining.

items.title: NANS dismisses claims of Northern marginalisation over passport reform
items.description: By Joseph Erunke The National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, Northern Caucus, has dismissed claims that the Federal Government’s ongoing passport centralisation reform is designed to sideline or disenfranchise Northern Nigeria, describing such allegations as false, misleading and politically motivated. The students’ body said the passport centralisation programme being implemented by the Nigeria Immigration Service, NIS, is a nationwide operational reform aimed at improving security, efficiency and service delivery, rather than a regional agenda. Speaking at a press conference in Abuja on Thursday, the caucus urged Nigerians, particularly residents of the North-East and North-West, to ignore what it described as “deliberate falsehood, propaganda and misinformation” surrounding the exercise. The National Vice President (External Affairs) of NANS, Comrade Sadiq Zango, who read a prepared text of the conference,said the group was compelled to address growing public concerns following enquiries from passport applicants and stakeholders across the affected northern states. According to NANS, the migration of passport production to the Central Personalisation Centre in Abuja does not stop passport processing or issuance at any passport office across the country or at Nigerian embassies and consulates abroad. Instead, it explained, the initiative forms part of a comprehensive modernisation programme designed to strengthen the security, integrity and efficiency of Nigeria’s passport issuance system. The association disclosed that the NIS had adopted a phased implementation strategy, with phases one to three already completed between February 2025 and 2026, covering passport offices in the North-Central, South-East and South-West regions, except Lagos, as well as 41 Nigerian missions across Africa, Europe, the Americas, Asia, the Middle East and Oceania. It added that phase four, scheduled for August 2026, will onboard the remaining passport offices in the South-South, North-East and North-West, including Calabar, Port Harcourt, Uyo, Yenagoa, Bauchi, Gombe, Jalingo, Yola, Farm Centre Kano and Dawakin Kudu Kano. “It is therefore far from the truth to suggest that the Federal Government is attempting to disenfranchise the North or any part of the country through this process,” the statement said. NANS further revealed that under the new operational framework, passport booklet printing and security personalisation have been consolidated into a secure, high-capacity production hub in Abuja to ensure passport production is completed within two weeks. It stressed that passport offices nationwide would continue to receive applications, process requests and issue passports as before. The students’ body also noted that the reform would eliminate manual interference in passport personalisation, curb document fraud, strengthen accountability and ensure uniform quality and advanced security features in Nigerian passports. Expressing confidence in the Nigeria Immigration Service, NANS said the agency remains committed to deploying technology-driven solutions that align Nigeria’s passport system with global best practices. The association appealed to Northerners to remain calm and disregard rumours capable of creating tension. items.title: Daech: l’Afrique au cœur de la menace
items.description: Malgré les revers militaires infligés à son commandement central ces dernières années, le groupe terroriste État islamique en Iraq et au Levant (EIIL), plus connu sous le nom de Daech, continue de représenter une menace sérieuse pour la paix et la sécurité internationales, en particulier en Afrique et en Asie du Sud, ont averti mercredi des hautes responsables des Nations Unies devant le Conseil de sécurité. Présentant le dernier rapport du Secrétaire général sur la menace posée par Daech, Oguljeren Niyazberdiyeva, du Bureau des Nations Unies de lutte contre le terrorisme (UNOCT), a souligné que le groupe terroriste avait profondément transformé son mode de fonctionnement pour survivre aux campagnes militaires menées contre lui. « Malgré les efforts internationaux, Daech continue de poser une grave menace à la paix et à la sécurité internationales », a-t-elle déclaré au nom du chef par intérim de l’UNOCT, Alexandre Zouev. UN Photo/Eskinder Debebe Oguljeren Niyazberdiyeva, du Bureau des Nations Unies de lutte contre le terrorisme, s'adresse au Conseil de sécurité réuni sur les menaces à la paix et à la sécurité internationales causées par des actes terroristes. Un groupe plus dispersé mais toujours dangereux Selon le rapport, les opérations antiterroristes ont considérablement affaibli la direction centrale de Daech et réduit sa capacité à planifier et coordonner des attaques complexes à l'échelle internationale. Toutefois, cette pression n'a pas fait disparaître la menace. Le groupe s'est progressivement transformé en un réseau décentralisé de filiales régionales, liées par une idéologie commune et bénéficiant d'une plus grande autonomie opérationnelle. Cette évolution lui permet de s'adapter plus facilement aux contextes locaux et de poursuivre ses activités malgré les pertes subies. L'ONU estime ainsi que le risque terroriste demeure particulièrement élevé dans plusieurs régions d'Afrique, où certaines branches de Daech continuent d'étendre leur influence. L'Afrique au cœur des préoccupations Le rapport identifie le Sahel et le bassin du lac Tchad comme les principaux foyers d'expansion du groupe. La Province de l'État islamique en Afrique de l'Ouest (ISWAP) reste aujourd'hui la filiale la plus active de Daech dans le monde. Selon les Nations Unies, elle poursuit son développement militaire tout en recourant de plus en plus à des drones commerciaux afin d'améliorer ses capacités de surveillance et d'attaque. En République démocratique du Congo (RDC) et au Mozambique, les groupes affiliés poursuivent également leurs offensives malgré la pression exercée par les forces nationales et régionales. Ils continuent parallèlement à recruter de nouveaux combattants et à renforcer leurs réseaux locaux. Pour les Nations Unies, cette dynamique illustre la capacité de Daech à exploiter les fragilités institutionnelles, les conflits prolongés et les difficultés économiques pour étendre son implantation. Des inquiétudes persistantes en Syrie et en Afghanistan En Syrie, l'évolution du contexte politique et sécuritaire modifie également la nature de la menace. L'ONU s'inquiète notamment des conséquences de la fermeture, en février dernier, du camp d'Al-Hol. Les autorités ne savent plus où se trouvent plusieurs milliers d'anciens résidents, ce qui fait craindre une dispersion de personnes potentiellement liées à Daech. Les Nations Unies réitèrent leur appel au rapatriement « sûr, volontaire et digne » des personnes concernées, conformément au droit international. En Iraq, les autorités ont réussi à réduire de manière significative les capacités opérationnelles du groupe. Mais Mme Niyazberdiyeva a insisté sur la nécessité de consolider ces progrès. Selon elle, la lutte contre le terrorisme ne peut se limiter aux seules opérations militaires. Elle passe également par le renforcement des institutions publiques, une justice efficace, ainsi que des programmes de réhabilitation et de réinsertion destinés aux anciens combattants et à leurs familles. En Asie du Sud, la branche État islamique au Khorasan (EI-K) demeure l'une des plus préoccupantes. Le rapport estime qu'elle conserve la capacité d'inspirer ou de soutenir des attentats au-delà des frontières afghanes, tout en profitant de l'instabilité régionale pour recruter de nouveaux membres et préparer d'autres opérations. Les nouvelles technologies au service du terrorisme L'ONU alerte également sur l'utilisation croissante des nouvelles technologies par Daech. Selon le rapport, le groupe terroriste exploite désormais l'intelligence artificielle, les plateformes numériques, les communications chiffrées, les actifs virtuels et les drones sans pilote afin d'adapter ses méthodes de propagande, de recrutement, de financement et de planification. Pour l'ONU, cette évolution rend indispensable un renforcement de la coopération internationale, mais aussi un dialogue plus étroit avec les entreprises technologiques et le secteur privé afin d'améliorer la gouvernance de ces outils émergents. Toutefois ces mêmes technologies peuvent également devenir de puissants instruments de prévention et de lutte contre le terrorisme lorsqu'elles sont utilisées de manière responsable et dans le respect du droit international. UN Photo/ Manuel Elías Carmen G. Cantor, directrice exécutive adjointe de la Direction exécutive du Comité contre le terrorisme (CTED), lors d'une réunion du Conseil de sécurité sur les menaces à la paix et à la sécurité internationales causées par des actes terroristes. Un « écosystème » terroriste en ligne Intervenant également devant le Conseil de sécurité, la Directrice exécutive adjointe de la Direction exécutive du Comité contre le terrorisme, Carmen G. Cantor, a mis en garde contre l'essor d'un véritable « écosystème » numérique qui favorise la radicalisation. Selon elle, les groupes terroristes exploitent désormais les réseaux sociaux, les plateformes de jeux en ligne et les services de messagerie chiffrée pour diffuser leur propagande, recruter de nouveaux membres et lever des fonds. Face à une menace toujours plus diffuse, technologique et transnationale, Mme Niyazberdiyeva et Mme Cantor ont appelé les États à maintenir leur coopération et à privilégier des réponses globales qui associent sécurité, prévention, développement et respect des droits humains. Source: ONU Info L’article Daech: l'Afrique au cœur de la menace est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 2027: Orji Kalu dismisses ‘weak opposition’, says Tinubu has no competition
items.description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has declared that President Bola Tinubu faces no formidable challenge ahead of the 2027 presidential election, describing the opposition as too fragmented to mount a credible contest. Kalu made the remarks on Wednesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that the inability of opposition parties to unite had significantly strengthened the ruling All Progressives Congress’ chances of retaining power. “He has no competition. The opposition is very weak. He has no competition because you check what we did during the primaries, the number of people, our membership, things Tinubu has done all over Nigeria, the new roads he has created,” Kalu said. He added that the political landscape would have been different if opposition parties had remained united. “If they were together, we would start having some sleepless nights. Now they are not together,” he said. The senator, however, acknowledged that the Tinubu administration had not done enough to publicise its achievements, noting that the President had shown little interest in promoting the activities of his government. Kalu also claimed that Tinubu was contending with opposition from both within and outside government. According to him, the President has “a lot of archenemies” working against his administration despite what he described as its progress in office. Assessing the administration’s performance, the former governor said Tinubu had delivered on a substantial part of his mandate and expressed confidence that his approval rating would continue to improve. “He has done 65 per cent well,” Kalu said, adding that the President could be approaching “70 per cent by September or October.” He also predicted that voters in northern Nigeria would ultimately support Tinubu’s bid for a second term based on the administration’s performance. Kalu’s comments come amid continued political realignments ahead of the 2027 presidential election. A coalition initially championed under the African Democratic Congress in 2025 brought together several opposition figures, including former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso. However, disagreements over the coalition’s leadership and structure later triggered fresh political alignments, leaving opposition parties divided ahead of the next general election. items.title: Government ignoring internal corruption while targeting opponents – Afenyo-Markin alleges
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused the government of practising selective justice, alleging that corruption involving government officials is being ignored while political opponents and critics are singled out for investigation and prosecution. Speaking at the “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on Thursday, August 6, Mr Afenyo-Markin claimed that the selective application of justice is undermining Ghana’s democratic principles. According to him, allegations of corruption involving government officials are not receiving the attention of state security agencies and anti-corruption institutions. He alleged that while political opponents continue to face what he described as harassment, reports of wrongdoing within government are being overlooked. “The rot in government is being ignored,” he claimed. Mr Afenyo-Markin also criticised the ongoing process seeking the removal of the Chief Justice, arguing that it reflects what he described as selective justice. He alleged that the committee established under the law to investigate the matter had not completed its work before a report was purportedly produced and relied upon as the basis for the Chief Justice’s removal. The Minority Leader further expressed concern over the arrest and detention of citizens over comments on governance, saying such actions threaten democratic freedoms. “We are not saying that we endorse excesses in such actions,” he said. “But where anybody is affected, the person can go to court, not spend time in prison.” He maintained that the alleged failure to investigate corruption allegations within government, coupled with the treatment of political opponents and critics, points to what he believes is a growing threat to Ghana’s democracy.

items.title: Conseils médicaux pour bien traverser la vague de chaleur
items.description: Les températures grimpent, et avec elles, le risque pour la santé. Comment bien traverser ces journées caniculaires ? Mauvais sommeil, maux de tête et problèmes de concentration : la chaleur pèse sur le corps et l'esprit. Dans le pire des cas, elle peut devenir mortelle. Avec le changement climatique, les vagues de chaleur deviennent plus fréquentes, plus intenses et plus longues – devenant ainsi l’un des plus grands risques pour la santé en été. Comment se protéger, quels signaux d'alarme prendre au sérieux et quels mythes sur la chaleur ont la vie dure ? En ma qualité de médecin pédiatre, voici ce que je conseille. Dr Salem Sahli * La chaleur représente un stress pour l’organisme. Lors de températures élevées, le cœur, les reins et la circulation sanguine tournent à plein régime. L’organisme tente de maintenir sa température corporelle constante. Et cela coûte de l’énergie avec pour conséquences des problèmes circulatoires, des maux de tête et des difficultés de concentration. Les personnes particulièrement vulnérables sont les personnes âgées, les jeunes enfants et les personnes souffrant de maladies cardiovasculaires ou d’autres maladies chroniques. Mais la chaleur peut s’avérer très dangereuse même pour les personnes en bonne santé. Même si l'on se sent en forme, il convient d’adapter son quotidien lors des journées de canicule et de renoncer durant la journée à tout ce qui fatigue le corps, qu’il s'agisse du jardinage ou du sport. L’une des règles les plus importantes est de boire suffisamment. En transpirant, le corps ne perd pas seulement de l’eau, mais aussi des minéraux. C’est pourquoi toute personne qui transpire abondamment doit non seulement boire en quantité suffisante, mais aussi veiller à un apport adéquat en électrolytes, par exemple via des boissons isotoniques. Le corps souffre d’une vague de chaleur de jour comme de nuit. Si les températures ne descendent pas en dessous de 20°C, on parle de nuit tropicale. L’organisme peut alors à peine se régénérer, car il doit continuer à dépenser de l’énergie pendant le sommeil pour se refroidir. Ceux qui ont du mal à s’endormir devraient appliquer des compresses fraîches, prendre une douche tiède avant de se coucher et n’utiliser qu’une couverture légère. Je déconseille en revanche les douches glacées qui ont tendance à stimuler le corps plutôt qu’à le détendre. Un rafraîchissement doux, comme un bain de pieds froid, est bien plus judicieux. Les personnes sous traitement médical doivent redoubler de vigilance les jours de forte chaleur. La perte d’eau réduit le volume sanguin, ce qui augmente la concentration de certains médicaments dans le sang. Les médicaments agissent alors différemment. Cela concerne surtout les antihypertenseurs et les diurétiques. La chaleur pouvant abaisser davantage la pression artérielle, le dosage doit être adapté avec le médecin traitant, jamais de son propre chef. Lors de la prise d’antalgiques, il faut veiller à boire beaucoup pour maintenir une bonne irrigation des reins. Les sédatifs, quant à eux, peuvent atténuer les signaux d’alarme émis par le corps. Il est également essentiel de conserver les médicaments au frais et au sec, conformément à la notice. Les jours de canicule, il faut être attentif aux signaux d’alerte : si l’on ne se sent pas bien, qu’on a des vertiges, des maux de tête ou des démarches hésitantes, il faut prendre cela au sérieux. La règle est alors de se mettre immédiatement à l’ombre ou dans un endroit frais, de s’asseoir ou de s’allonger, et de refroidir progressivement son corps. Si des symptômes tels que des crampes musculaires, des difficultés respiratoires ou des malaises circulatoires apparaissent, il faut contacter immédiatement les secours. La chaleur n’affecte pas seulement le corps – elle impacte aussi le mental. Les gens sont plus irritables, plus agressifs et souffrent plus souvent d’anxiété. Une étude américaine menée sur 45 ans a montré que les violences augmentent les jours de canicule. En plus du potentiel d’agressivité, le risque de suicide augmente également. Le corps est tellement concentré sur la régulation de sa température que le moindre stress supplémentaire le surcharge rapidement. De plus, l’équilibre hormonal est perturbé. Le cerveau sécrète davantage d’hormones de stress comme le cortisol ou l’adrénaline, ce qui peut favoriser l’agitation, l’anxiété et les états dépressifs. Insolation, coup de chaleur ou malaises : lors des journées chaudes, les services d’urgence sont sollicités bien plus souvent qu’à l’accoutumée. Bien souvent, un simple coup d’œil et un contact tactile suffisent pour identifier le problème. La chaleur monte dans le corps, les gens ont souvent le visage très rouge. Quand on touche leur peau, elle est totalement sèche parce qu’ils ont déjà évacué toute leur transpiration. Les personnes âgées sont particulièrement exposées. Elles ne boivent pas assez et sont souvent habillées trop chaudement. Je suis souvent surpris, en me promenant en ville, de voir que même par forte chaleur, les personnes âgées restent habillées de façon très stricte. Au lieu de pantalons longs et de chemises, des tissus clairs et légers sont recommandés. Les courses ou les promenades doivent être planifiées de préférence tôt le matin ou en soirée. Pour éviter que les logements ne surchauffent, il faut aérer à fond tôt le matin, puis garder fenêtres et volets fermés. On n’aère à nouveau que lorsque la température extérieure baisse en soirée. Il est également conseillé de privilégier des repas légers, une consommation d’eau suffisante et un peu moins de café afin d’éviter de surcharger le système cardiovasculaire. * Médecin pédiatre. L’article Conseils médicaux pour bien traverser la vague de chaleur est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Galamsey operators exploiting cooperative mining scheme to destroy communities – Erastus Asare Donkor
items.description: Award-winning JoyNews environmental journalist Erastus Asare Donkor has alleged that some illegal miners are exploiting the government’s cooperative mining scheme as a cover to continue destructive mining activities in parts of the country. According to him, the abuse of the initiative is occurring in communities including Berekum, Dawma and along the Bekwai–Esiwa road, as well as in several farming communities across the Eastern, Western and Ashanti regions. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, August 6, to mark one year since the helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight state officials travelling to support the fight against illegal mining, Mr Asare Donkor expressed concern over what he described as a resurgence of galamsey activities. “When you go to Berekum, the whole place has been taken over; it is as if there is no chief in Berekum. Go to Dawma; recently, NAIMOS was there, and I thought they could contain the situation. The people are back within the town itself,” he said. He alleged that some miners are operating under the guise of the cooperative mining programme, undermining the very purpose for which it was introduced. “People are mining under the guise of cooperative mining, the very reason why these men had to die. That is the most painful part. The very reason why these people had to die was so that we could set up a cooperative mining scheme that is doing sustainable mining. Now people are coming under the cooperative mining initiative and using it to destroy communities.” Citing Bekwai Municipality as an example, Mr Asare Donkor claimed some operators were carrying out mining activities dangerously close to major roads. “A typical example is in Bekwai Municipality where they are mining inches away from the main road.” He further alleged that enforcement actions by the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) had yielded only temporary results. “When I reported it, NAIMOS went in there, burnt a few pumping machines and said they had taken control of the situation. But the people are back there. Just three days later, they were back mining,” he claimed. Mr Asare Donkor also alleged that some traditional leaders in affected communities were supporting illegal mining activities. “This is controlled by tradition itself; the chiefs are now supporting illegal mining within their enclaves,” he alleged. The environmental journalist, who has extensively reported on the impact of illegal mining, called for stronger oversight of the cooperative mining programme to ensure it is not exploited by individuals engaged in galamsey. The government introduced the cooperative mining model as part of efforts to formalise small-scale mining and promote responsible and sustainable mining practices. However, concerns have been raised by some stakeholders over the alleged abuse of the initiative by illegal miners.

items.title: We’re at ‘a point of hopelessness’ in the fight against galamsey – Daryl Bosu
items.description: Deputy Director of A Rocha Ghana, Daryl Bosu, has warned that Ghana’s fight against illegal mining has reached “a point of hopelessness”, saying the country’s rivers and forests continue to suffer despite government interventions and the sacrifice of eight officials who died in last year’s helicopter crash. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, August 6, during a discussion marking the first anniversary of the helicopter crash and the country’s battle against galamsey, Mr Bosu said the systems introduced to tackle illegal mining have failed to deliver the expected results. “I think that we started well, but if you ask me, I would say now we are at a point of hopelessness because every system we put in place is failing to yield the needed results and outcomes,” he said. According to Mr Bosu, the government must urgently prioritise the protection of key national assets, particularly forest reserves and river bodies, if it wants to win the fight against illegal mining. “We need to secure our forest reserves against galamsey. We need to secure our river systems against galamsey, and our approach should be very uncompromising,” he stressed. He said that enforcement should be applied fairly and consistently, warning against selective action. “It is not enough to jail Wontumi while many others are left to continue the impunity,” Mr Bosu said. “If there is anything this government can do, then these key economic sectors need to be protected, and government must start that now.” Reflecting on the helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight people, he described the anniversary as “a sad day”, recalling that he represented the Coalition Against Galamsey in Obuasi while waiting for the delegation to arrive for the commissioning of a responsible community mining project. The victims of the August 6 helicopter crash were attending the launch of the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme, rCOMSDEP, at Obuasi, a flagship initiative designed to transform Ghana’s artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) sector. Mr Bosu said the country had failed to honour those who died through meaningful action against illegal mining. “It is really sad to see that despite Ghanaians compassionately mourning, pouring in tributes and all of that, we have not taken action to honour their names,” he said. “What we have rather done is play around with a lot of propaganda, a lot of optics without really showing true commitment.” Drawing on recent visits to mining communities, Bosu said the situation on the ground suggests that illegal mining continues almost unchecked. He recounted a recent visit to Dunkwa where illegal mining equipment was operating openly near a police station. “Recently we were in Dunkwa, and just after crossing the bridge into the town, there was a changfan machine operating. You could hear it as you drove over the bridge, and not far from there was the police station,” he said. According to him, similar scenes are becoming common across mining communities, with rivers continuing to be heavily polluted. He pointed to the deteriorating condition of major rivers, including the Ankobra, Birim, Offin and Tano, saying pollution levels remain alarming. “We have seen more and more of our rivers staying polluted. If you look at how polluted the Ankobra is as it flows into the sea, if you look at places like the Birim River and the Offin, it is a very devastating situation,” he stated. Mr Bosu said research conducted by A Rocha Ghana shows that the quality of Ghana’s water bodies has not improved despite ongoing anti-galamsey operations. “We did some research on the levels of pollution in our water bodies, and it was very clear that it is not getting better. It hasn’t gotten better,” he said. He also linked the continued destruction of rivers to growing challenges in access to safe drinking water across the country. “If you listen to communities complaining more and more about the lack of potable drinking water, it tells you there is a problem,” Bosu noted. “Ghana Water Company is rationing water not only in Accra but also in other parts of the country where it supplies water.” While acknowledging the deployment of military personnel and other enforcement measures, Bosu argued that these efforts have not produced the environmental improvements Ghanaians had hoped for. “There is a lot of military deployment and a lot of actions here and there, but that is not really the solution that is needed,” he said. He further criticised what he described as weak law enforcement, alleging that illegal mining activities are taking place openly without intervention. “You see activities happening right by the roadside, five or ten metres away, and these people are driving through with their excavators, and nothing is happening. You don’t see any corresponding action from the police in particular.” Mr Bosu warned that illegal miners are expanding into new areas that were previously untouched, causing even greater environmental destruction. “From what we have seen on the ground, there has been no improvement in the environment. These miners are expanding their territories. They are entering areas that have not seen mining before, and they are using that to devastate and destroy the land even more. We really have a long way to go,” he said.

items.title: Pénuries de médicaments, médecins non payés... le système de santé palestinien au bord de l'effondrement
items.description: Les centres de santé publics palestiniens fonctionnent seulement une ou deux fois par semaine, les hôpitaux sont submergés et n’assurent que les urgences, les médecins sont partiellement payés et il y a des pénuries de médicaments. Le rapport de l’ONG Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) pointe la responsabilité des autorités israéliennes qui refusent de verser les taxes douanières prélevées au nom de l’Autorité palestinienne. Le blocage de ces recettes fiscales met en péril l'accès aux soins en Cisjordanie occupée. Pour de nombreux Palestiniens, les cliniques mobiles de Physicians for Human Rights Israel figurent désormais parmi les seules structures à combler ce vide.

items.title: NPP’s ‘Democracy Under Attack’ demonstration underway
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has commenced its planned nationwide demonstration dubbed “Democracy Under Attack,” with the party raising concerns over what it describes as threats to Ghana’s democratic governance. Clad in red and black, carrying placards bearing the hashtags #DemocracyUnderAttack, #SaveGhanaNow, and #SayNoToStateCapture, NPP supporters have joined the ongoing “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration as the party highlights what it describes as threats to Ghana’s democratic space. The protest is expected to start from the Supreme Court and end at the Jubilee House, according to promotional materials released by the party. The party says the demonstration is intended to highlight alleged restrictions on free expression, concerns over the treatment of opposition voices, and what it describes as threats to democratic institutions. Backing the protest, NPP Communications team member and spokesperson for former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said the demonstration was in response to what he claims are increasing attempts by the government to silence dissent and weaken democratic institutions. The NPP has insisted that the action is aimed at defending civil liberties, the rule of law, and democratic accountability. The planned protest comes amid heightened political tensions, with the NPP insisting the demonstration is intended to defend civil liberties, the rule of law, and democratic accountability. The government has, however, rejected claims that it is targeting political opponents, maintaining that law enforcement agencies and the judiciary operate independently and that arrests and prosecutions are undertaken in accordance with the law. The NPP’s demonstration is expected to culminate at the Jubilee House, where party leaders are scheduled to address supporters on their concerns over the state of Ghana’s democracy.
