items.title: The Death of Romance
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Reports confirming the death of young love are pouring in: Post-COVID declines in dating aren’t rebounding. Way fewer teens and young adults are having sex. In 2019, 42 percent of single adults younger than 40 told Pew Research Center that they’d never been in a committed relationship. Thirty years ago, my friends and I thought of romance and marriage much the same way screenwriters did: They were just the expected ending. Now this attitude seems to be less and less the norm. It’s not that people don’t want romantic relationships. But chasing them feels to people like it exacts too much of a toll. So over time, they’ve become less of a priority. As a result, we have entered what The Atlantic ’s staff writer Faith Hill calls the “ great romance slump ,” in which romance is no longer the center of people’s lives. Hill created a survey and sent it to people all over the country. She heard from men, women, nonbinary people, queer people, and straight people. From their answers and insights from research, Hill came up with solid theories about why more people are giving up on love. On this week’s Radio Atlantic, Hill explains what’s driving the romance slump, and what its long-term implications are for families, the economy, and politics. And we hear from two people Hill interviewed who have given up, at least for now. The following is a transcript of the episode: Hanna Rosin: It didn’t happen all at once. Instead, the modern disenchantment with romance unfolded slowly, subtly, but still unmistakably. Post COVID, young people stopped dating as much. If you talk to them about why, what you hear is exhaustion with the apps—the whole hassle of combing through matches, chatting, finding a mutually convenient time, and then dragging yourself out of the house to meet a total stranger. All of that started to seem less important than seeing friends, caring for family, getting some work done, watching the series that everyone else was talking about. These shifts were made one by one, inside people’s heads. And then all of these individual decisions accumulated over time and turned into something new, something which staff writer Faith Hill calls the romance slump. Rosin: I have a question for you, as my colleague. Are you the romance reporter? Is that your actual job? Faith Hill: ( Laughs .) You know, I’m proud to hold that mantle. I report on some other things, too, but romance and dating and singlehood specifically has kind of become a big thing for me. Rosin: That’s amazing. So The Atlantic has a romance-and-relationship reporter, and that is you. Hill: I guess so. [ Music ] Rosin: I’m Hanna Rosin. This is Radio Atlantic . Faith spent the last several months reporting on what she called the great romance slump. In the last 40 or so years, we’ve seen huge drops in both marriage and cohabitation rates, especially among 25-to-34-year-olds. Hill: But there’s also just a shrinking share of young adults who have a steady partner. And, you know, in 2019, 42 percent of single adults younger than 40 told Pew Research Center that they’d never been in a committed relationship. Rosin: That is the statistic that really surprised me. Hill: I felt the same when I saw that, and I think it’s important to talk about because it’s pretty easy to shrug off the declining marriage rates as kind of: The institution of marriage is not as important to people. You can easily have romance without marriage. Rosin: Or intimacy without marriage, or children without marriage. Hill: Right. Exactly. But that’s not the only thing going on. You know, it’s not just about sort of views towards marriage, and I think this is really quite a profound change. Rosin: Listening to you, I see why you called your story “The Great Romance Slump,” because it is something of a resignation. It’s kind of like a shrug. Faith: Yes. That’s exactly it. I liked the term for that reason. It, you know, has this kind of subtle, almost passive feel to it. You know, it’s not a sudden and dramatic plummet. It’s not that active. Like, it’s not people all swearing off romance, but rather sort of a lot of people kind of slowly giving up on it kind of captures this pessimism and fatigue. Rosin: Yeah. It’s like a slight bad smell in the air. Faith: Yeah, exactly. But it also implies that it’s not necessarily permanent. You know, you can come back from a slump, so there’s that too. Rosin: Okay, let’s get into some of the reasons this is happening. Some I can just guess right off the bat. I did write a book called The End of Men about a decade ago, so I did a lot of study into how men’s and women’s relationships were changing, and just the basic fact of women being more financially independent, women being able to buy houses. We can have credit cards now—amazing—have any career you want. So the basic idea that you need a man in order to survive is just not true anymore. What are some of the other reasons that you came across? Or at least, what’s your take on the cause? Hill: I think that there’s kind of a combination of people needing romance less than they used to, which is great, and also dating being hard in these, you know, very specific frustrating ways. You hear so much about the dating apps, of when people talk about singlehood and romance, and a lot of times, I think people are talking about the sort of distance of the technology making it easier to ghost and people being on bad behavior because of that, kind of a lack of accountability. [ Music ] Hill: And also, you hear a lot about the kind of paradox of choice—like, people are just swimming in options. And I think there’s truth there. But I do kind of think, you know, the big thing that comes to mind for me when I consider online dating is just the toll that it takes on people. You know, when you’re having to set aside time and energy and money to meet strangers, to suss them out on the app, and then meet up with them, and then, you know, try to keep the momentum up, it just is a huge toll. And, you know, I think that toll means that a lot of people, like, want a relationship but aren’t going to prioritize it. But I think the combination of dating being kind of exhausting and time-consuming and requiring sacrifice from other areas of life, and singlehood being so normal and doable, it starts to make it very easy for romance to just, like, not be the top thing that you wanna pursue. And, you know, when you want romance but don’t need it, and you don’t feel like it’s gonna be easy to get, and you don’t feel optimistic about those chances or about the people you would be dating, a lot of people are just gonna give it up. Rosin: And so if you were a sociologist, what would be the sentence? Like, what is the headline in the world of romance that merits bigger attention? Hill: Well, I would say, you know, romance is obviously a very broad term. Under that umbrella, you know, you might fit sex, dating, partnership, marriage. But all of these forms, particularly among young people, seem to be on the decline. And I think that shift has a lot of downstream implications. You know, it’s changing how and whether people have families, how people spend their time, how they spend their money, potentially who they vote for. And, you know, if romance is no longer the center of nearly everyone’s life, something else is. [ Music ] Rosin: How fed up with romance do people have to be before they give up? The line is different for everyone, but there are some patterns in people’s breaking points. Faith created a survey and sent it far and wide—she heard back from men, women, nonbinary people, queer, straight, and living in all different parts of the country. One loud theme that emerges, from the respondents but also from the research, is a gender gap—more women giving up on men, not trusting them to be supportive in the right ways, not getting what they need from them, and not willing to give so much when they’re not getting back. One of the people that Faith talked to was a woman named Treasure, who drifted away from romance and then did find new things to put at the center of her life. Hill: Treasure is a 39-year-old woman in Chicago who has been single for a long time, and she’s loving it. Treasure: I have been single now for 10 years. Hill: She, for many years, was trying to date seriously, trying to find someone to marry. She was, you know, really a romantic and had high hopes about it. Treasure: From 18 to about 27, I took dating very seriously. Hill: She was engaged four different times. In each one, she felt like she was contributing half financially, and yet she was also doing all of the child care. She has three children. Treasure: I already had two children before I turned 18. I started off as a teen mother. All four relationships failed because it’s like raising another child. Hill: After that fourth relationship ended, the fourth engagement, that was really the last straw for her. Treasure: I’m going to get extremely personal here, but I had a miscarriage, and my significant other at the time noticed that I was depressed and noticed that I was upset, and I kept trying to explain to him, “Well, you know, my hormones are changing right now.” I was already four months along. I was like, “I’m really sad right now. I know you feel like you need attention, but right now I can’t do this. This isn’t about you.” Hill: She said, “You know, the one time that I need something from him, his support, he couldn’t be there.” Treasure: In my mind, it was like I overperform in these relationships, and when it comes down to the wire and something is needed for me from them, I was not receiving it. And if that’s the case, then what is the purpose? Hill: I think she just felt really exhausted by holding everyone else up and feeling like the mother to the partners she had. Treasure: That was the last time for me. I was like, “This isn’t for me.” [ Music ] Hill: She likes to say, you know, she realized if she wasn’t gonna find a husband, she had to make “husband money.” So she did a bunch of training and an apprenticeship, and she ended up becoming a technical engineer in a union job, and that totally changed the financial picture for her, where she felt like, you know, she could be single and take care of her kids herself. Treasure: I've been in the trades now for nine years, and I choose not to date anymore. Hill: When she first gave up on dating and romance, she felt really lonely. I think it was a big change. But she realized she just had to start replacing what she had gotten from those partnerships with other things. Treasure: I adjusted, and I made more friends, and I found myself again. I have new hobbies and go places alone. I travel alone. I go to the movies alone. I go out to dinner alone. I’m literally dating myself, and I’m so much happier. I am the one for me. Hill: She wishes that she could have found the relationship that she once dreamed about, but she said, “I think at this point, it’s a fantasy.” Treasure: It’s kinda like, How do you get it all? Is there a way? I haven’t found it. I had to give up romantic love with a spouse in order to achieve everything else that I wanted. Rosin: That’s so interesting. It’s like when Esther Perel says we look to our partners and we expect everything from them, and that’s not realistic. It sounds like she just took the everything and divided it among people—like, I’m gonna have best friends here. I’m gonna have a community there. I’m gonna make money here , and maybe she just has sex somewhere else. You know? Hill: Right. Exactly. Rosin: I bet that there are women who can definitely relate to that. Does she seem happy to you now? Hill: She really does seem happy. Yeah. She was, I think, one of the happiest people I talked to for this story. I found that really beautiful to kind of realize that if you can sort of round that bend psychologically, sometimes you just can grow to love your life in the way it is if you sort of lean into it. I don’t think it would necessarily be the same for everyone, but Treasure is really independent, and she has great friendships and meaningful work. I think she just had such a hard time trying to find love that, in comparison, she feels so free. Rosin: It’s important, because I guess she counts as a post-romance model. Like, it’s not for everyone, but that is a template that might work for some people. Because she did wanna have a romantic relationship at some point. She sought it. She tried many times. And so for anyone in that situation, this is an alternate model that’s maybe hopeful at the other side. Did you have a sense of how typical she was? Hill: Yeah, I’ve talked to a lot of people who have sort of stopped searching for romance. I think she might be a little atypical in just how much she’s loving it and thriving. But I’ve talked to a lot of people who say that they would welcome a relationship if it fell in their lap, but they’re not gonna search for it. They just can’t do that anymore. They’re too exhausted. They spent too much time on it. They wanna focus on other things. And I actually talked to one researcher who said, you know, she had to stop asking in studies whether people were “actively” looking for a relationship, because what resonated more with people was whether they were “open” to a relationship. [ Music ] Rosin: It’s also interesting because the word slump is sort of a negative word, but Treasure’s case implies that the romance slump is not necessarily a negative thing, because it does open up alternate possibilities, particularly for women. Hill: I think that’s definitely the hope. And, you know, I think for some people like Treasure, who can kind of pull this off and find meaning and community in all these other ways, it could be really beautiful. And of course, it is a great thing that this change is happening, partly because women are able to live independently and focus on other things. So I definitely don’t think the shift is all negative. At the same time, you know, the majority of single people do still say that they want a long-term partnership. And so for me, that’s kind of at the heart of this story. You know, what happens to the people who want love and are struggling to find it or give up on it altogether? I do think that there’s real loss there that we can take seriously, even if, you know, it does open up sort of new ways to think about purpose and community and meaning. Rosin: Next up: the men. What’s their experience of the romance slump? That’s after the break. [ Break ] Rosin: Okay. We’ve talked about the women’s point of view. What about the men? I wanna talk about one of the guys you interviewed, Arthur. Can you tell me about him? Hill: Arthur is a guy in his 40s who has spent many years dating. He’s had one-off dates here and there. He’s dated some people for a month or so. He’s had some one-to-two-year relationships. But he’s always felt like it just kind of hasn’t totally worked out. Arthur: It was always kinda like hedged by them saying stuff like, “Oh, you’re nice and everything. We’ve had some good times, but honestly, you’re not really right for me.” Hill: Some exes have kind of told him that they feel like he’s almost too nice. Arthur: I’m not sure how to square that. Like, I mean, I will be, you know, the man and, you know, make all the plans and execute and everything if you want. Hill: You know, they want him to kind of be more decisive or be the man in the relationship. Arthur: But I mean, that does kinda come at the cost of me being somewhat less, you know, supportive and more demanding, because it kinda has to be that way. Hill: One person said that he has “dad” energy. Arthur: I’m not 100 percent sure what that means, but I’m guessing it’s not very sexy. Rosin: Ugh. Hill: Right? Rosin: That’s trauma. I mean, that could be great, I guess, but it sounds like he did not take it as a good thing. Hill: Right, and I think this person didn’t take it as a good thing in the romantic context. She wasn’t looking for “dad” energy. Rosin: Yeah. That gets into something very important, which is the impossible dilemma that men seem to be in. It’s very hard to know how to be, because you mentioned earlier that part of the problem between Treasure, who we talked about, and lots of women, was that men could not see their needs or weren’t open or communicative enough. And yet, here is poor Arthur maybe trying to be that way and getting dinged for it. Did you hear men talk about their confusion over roles? Hill: Yeah, absolutely. I think we’re in a kind of confusing in-between time, where there are sort of these new standards for men that they’re trying to reach, like this—you know, being kind and communicative and emotionally open—but at the same time, the old standards haven’t really gone away fully. So a lot of men did still feel like they were expected to pay for everything on the dates and, kind of, take the lead on everything, initiate flirting, kissing. And they felt sort of torn between those two and confused. Like, they were trying to kind of exemplify all of these traits at once—like, be sort of masculine and sturdy, but also gentle and empathetic—and feeling like they were sort of always falling down on the job on one of those sides. Rosin: And did Arthur have any positive experiences? Like, did he have any success or things that worked for him? Hill: He definitely had some, you know, relationships that ended in friendships. And so it hasn’t been all, you know, a bad time. And yet, I think he felt like he was just putting so much into it. You know, he still very deeply wants to find love. Arthur: I’m human, right? Like, I want to go out and, like, meet people and, you know, kiss the pretty ladies and all that. Hill: But he just feels like he can’t be prioritizing it anymore. Arthur: There’s so much going on. I’ve got all this stuff that I need to learn. I wanna go play with my niece and my nephew. You know what I mean? So something had to give, and I decided it was kinda like, You know what? This romantic stuff is not going my way anyway. Instead of being, like, top three things in my life, let’s bring it down to, like, maybe the bottom of the top 10 . Hill: He’s kind of pulled back from it. He’s focusing on being a good uncle, a good person, a good employee. So he’s like, “Let me just focus on myself and being the best person I can be,” and that has been a real sort of grief that he’s carrying. Arthur: It really broke my heart to feel like I wouldn’t find my person. Like, it really did. I carried that. It was like I lost a parent. Like, it really felt that hard. Hill: He feels like he kind of had to at least temporarily say goodbye to this partner he kept expecting to show up. Rosin: Did Arthur have a moment in the same way that Treasure did? Like, a moment where he thought—you know, like Treasure’s miscarriage moment—where he thought, I gotta stop ? Hill: I think for him, it was a little bit more gradual over time, like, just realizing sort of how draining this was. He also talked about COVID. There was a huge pandemic dating recession, and a big part of that was just young people not meeting as much. You know, the singlehood rates rose a lot after COVID. But there’s also another element, which is something that Arthur talked about, which is, you know, feeling like he actually lost some social skills when he was isolating in COVID. You know, he just was, obviously, not seeing people as much for a long time, and then when the world kind of opened up there, you know, it takes a while to sort of get back into the social life you used to have. Arthur: The world fully started opening up again, and I found myself feeling awkward. You know, it’s like being 17 again and, like, afraid to talk to the pretty girl you see. Hill: I think a lot of people can relate to that, right? Like, in the dating context or otherwise, just, like, feeling weirdly socially rusty. And that does not make making good chat and being charming with a stranger easy. Like, dating is already pretty hard socially. Rosin: Yeah. Yeah. You said that Arthur was focusing on other things. How do you hear something like that? Like, do you hear that to mean he’s given up on romance? He’s not actively dating? Hill: I think that’s kind of one of the big questions of this piece, you know: How much is this a sad thing for people, or how much is it kind of a triumph that people can have other priorities? And I think it’s a big mix. You know, I do think he has a meaningful and full life, and he’s getting a lot of purpose and enrichment from the relationships and the hobbies he does have. But at the same time, you know, he says himself that he is yearning for a partner. You know, he wants to do all of this with someone. Arthur: I do wanna find somebody that I can wake up in the morning and snuggle with, you know, for the next 20 or 30 years. Hill: And so I think it’s kind of both at once. You know, I’m very happy for him that he is able to find meaning in these other ways and that he has taken kind of, you know, a break from dating when it was not feeling good. But at the same time, he’s not getting something that he wants. And I want that for him. Rosin: So you’re a romance reporter. You’re also an adult woman looking for a long-term partnership. So I’m curious what this reporting experience has done to your outlook. Did you talk to all these people and feel comforted and more hopeful? Or did you talk to all these people and think, Oh, we just have to really accept a new reality ? Like, We are entering a kind of post-romance, post-marriage age, and we have to be creative about how we adapt to it ? Hill: Yeah, it’s a little bit of both. I definitely feel comfort in the sense that there are so many great people who just have been struggling with this for a really long time, and it does make one feel less alone in it. So there’s something really important about knowing there are, like, structural forces at work and a lot of luck too. Rosin: Like, It’s not just me . Like, The world is conspiring against me in some way . Hill: Right. Exactly. But at the same time, of course, that makes you feel, like, a little more pessimistic, right? Because it’s not like I can just change something about myself. It’s like, yeah, you know, dating is really hard right now, and a lot of people are in this situation. And we can’t just sort of fix all of the things that are making it hard. Rosin: Yeah. You’ve mentioned the yearning a couple of times. I wonder if that made you pessimistic or hopeful. Like, when I think of tens of thousands of young people yearning for a partner, it makes me sad, but maybe also makes me happy. Like, it’s a motivating factor. How did you receive that? Hill: Yeah, I think the yearning is kind of a beautiful thing. I mean, it’s a human emotion, you know? It can be positive in that it drives people forward to look for something that they really want. And I love to hear when people can sort of find peace with singlehood and close that door if that makes their life better. And yet, at the same time, I think that’s the thing with the slump, right? Like, a lot of people who do want partnership are just kind of giving up. And I think the yearning is one thing that is gonna kind of keep people having hope and still trying. You know, I wouldn’t want all of that to go away. And I also hope that, you know, people can maybe channel the yearning into other parts of life. Like, I do think there’s not such a clear objective divide between the romantic and other forms of love and passion. And, you know, I think maybe these single people who are turning their attention elsewhere are really bringing a lot of their heart and soul because they’re looking for other ways to kind of fill the center of their life and, like, give love. And I think that makes them—it gives them sort of a powerful energy. Rosin: Yeah. Can I ask: Did you shift in any way? Like, after doing all of this reporting and talking to all of these people and finding all of this company in the looking for romance in an ambivalent way, did you make any decisions about your own life? Hill: I didn’t make any clear ones, but I will say, you know, when I talk to people who have stopped dating—and, you know, a lot of those people are enjoying their life more now than when they were dating, ’cause they weren’t having a good time; that’s why they stopped. So it does, it feels pretty tempting, and I do start to think, you know, of all the different things I could be doing with my time. Like, I feel like I might be a better daughter and a better friend, and maybe I could, like, start writing fiction or—you know, my mind starts racing, and I think those are good things to be thinking about. We all do have limited time on this Earth, and we have to make choices about how to use it. So that’s something I’m considering, but I also know that some people I talk to, you know, when I checked in after we had an interview, they had had, you know, some dates with someone they were really excited about. I talked to at least one person who was like, “Oh, I found someone. Like, he’s the one. I am not right for your story anymore.” So that also was a reminder that, you know, if you do keep trying, for a lot of people, eventually, like, there is, you know, someone who makes the rest of it all feel like it was worth it to lead to that. So I’m split. [ Music ] Rosin: Ugh. We can never give up on the rom-com ending. Hill: Yeah. Rosin: It’s just how we are. We’re just built that way. Well, Faith, thank you so much for joining me today. Hill: Thank you so much. Rosin: This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Rosie Hughes with help from Jacob Smollen and Jinae West. It was edited by Kevin Townsend. Rob Smierciak engineered and provided original music. We also had music from Breakmaster Cylinder. Fact-checking by Genevieve Finn and Álex Maroño Porto. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. Listeners, if you enjoy the show, you can support our work and the work of all Atlantic journalists when you subscribe to The Atlantic at TheAtlantic.com/Listener . I’m Hanna Rosin. Thank you for listening.

items.title: PM Shehbaz departs for Saudi Arabia on 3-day visit
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday left for a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia, where he will be accompanied by the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. In a post on X, the government said that the premier has left for the visit at the invitation of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Apart from CDF Munir, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, and Special Assistant Tariq Fatemi will also accompany the premier on the visit. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar, who is currently in Saudi Arabia after concluding a visit to Jordan, will be part of the delegation as well. The premier will also perform Umrah and visit Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) mosque in Madina during the visit, the government said. Earlier, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi announced the visit in a weekly briefing. “During the visit, the prime minister will meet the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and discussions will focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relationship and exchange views on areas of regional and international developments of mutual interests,” he said. He stressed that the visit marked Pakistan’s “long-standing partnership” with Saudi Arabia, which he said was “anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood”. Andrabi noted that while the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, he said that “it will carry immense significance beyond the immediate crisis and short-term considerations”. He added that the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest and also reinforce multilateral cooperation”. Shortly after, an official statement regarding the visit was also issued. The premier had last visited Saudi Arabia in April, meeting with the kingdom’s top leadership. As the Middle East conflict has expanded across new fronts, Saudi Arabia has unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition. In July, Pakistan also endorsed Saudi Arabia’s air strikes in Iraq as an exercise of its right to self-defence. The remarks came two days after Saudi Arabia and the US carried out coordinated strikes against installations of Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Units, accusing elements within the umbrella force of launching attacks on Saudi oil facilities. The remarks followed Pakistan’s earlier warning after Yemen’s Houthi rebels announced a maritime blockade targeting shipping linked to Saudi Arabia. Islamabad had then described attacks on Pakistani maritime interests as a “red line”, warning that any hostile action against Pakistani-flagged vessels or commercial shipping would be treated as an attack on Pakistan. The country also simultaneously reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the uninterrupted flow of lawful maritime commerce through the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb. Last year, Islamabad and Riyadh concluded a Strategic Mutual Defence Agree­ment, which became operational earlier this year as Pakistan simultaneously embarked on a diplomatic effort to mediate between Iran and the United States.

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El PP reconoce que acogerá a los menores en sus comunidades: “El Partido Popular siempre cumple la ley, en esta ocasión, también”
items.description: La dirección nacional del PP, por boca de su vicesecretario de Política Autonómica y Local, Elías Bendodo, ha reconocido este jueves que las comunidades autónomas realojarán a los menores no acompañados que salgan de Ceuta pese a haber pactado con Vox que no acogerán más menores extranjeros. “El Partido Popular siempre cumple la ley, en esta ocasión, también”, ha dicho Bendodo. Este jueves, el Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia ha informado de que más de un centenar de menores migrantes están siendo atendidos y han pasado su primera noche en un colegio ceutí. Infancia solicitó el martes que se permitiese el uso de dos colegios de la ciudad para atender de urgencia a las niñas y niños no acompañados que se encuentran en Ceuta desde la pasada semana. Por otro lado, el delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez, ha negado que el presidente de Ceuta, Jesús Vivas, advirtiese de la entrada masiva de migrantes en la ciudad autónoma los días previos. “He leído una información sobre los días previos a la avalancha que decía que el presidente Vivas había intentado advertir al presidente del Gobierno de lo que iba a pasar. Supongo que será un malentendido porque no es cierto”, ha asegurado. Además, el Rey recibe en audiencia al presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta a las 18.00 horas en Marivent, en Palma, según informa la Casa del Rey. La audiencia real se producirá después de una reunión entre Vivas y la presidenta de Baleares, Marga Prohens, también del PP, prevista para las 13.00 horas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ex-minister Kemi Adeosun’s husband dies at 62
items.description: Anthony Adeosun, husband of former Minister of Finance Kemi Adeosun, has died at the age of 62, a statement by the family said. The businessman passed away on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, in Lagos State. The announcement, titled “Announcement of the passing of Mr Anthony Adeniyi (Niyi) Adeosun,” was issued by Rev. C. A. Adeosun on behalf of the family and made available to journalists on Thursday. In the statement, the family described the late Adeosun as a distinguished businessman and a committed Christian whose life was marked by integrity, generosity and faith. “It is with profound sorrow, yet in total submission to the will of Almighty God, that the Adeosun family announces the passing of our beloved husband, father, and brother, Mr Anthony Adeniyi (Niyi) Adeosun, who was called home to glory on Wednesday, 5th August 2026, in Lagos. “He was 62 years old. Niyi was a distinguished businessman and a devoted Christian whose integrity, generosity, and steadfast faith touched the lives of all who knew him. “He lived a life defined by hard work, service to God, and an unwavering commitment to his family and community,” the statement partly read. The family said it was taking solace in God during the period of mourning and prayed for strength as it copes with what it described as an irreplaceable loss. It added that details of the funeral and Christian burial arrangements would be announced later. Adeosun is survived by his wife, children and siblings, including Kuramo Capital founder Adewale Adeosun. The post Ex-minister Kemi Adeosun’s husband dies at 62 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bodies of Nirmal Purja, 4 other climbers airlifted to Skardu after Broad Peak avalanche
items.description: Bodies of five more international climbers, including world-renowned British-Nepali Nirmal Purja, have been airlifted to Skardu after they were killed in an avalanche on Broad Peak, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Thursday. The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by 43-year-old Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. His company confirmed there were no survivors . “Following one of the most technically demanding recovery operations on Broad Peak, the Alpine Club of Pakistan confirms that the bodies of Nirmal Purja, Wang Zhong, Nima Sherpa, Gyalu Sherpa, and Killi Pemba “Kilu” Sherpa have been transported to Skardu CMH Hospital by helicopter,” ACP said in its statement on Thursday. “Following necessary procedures and documentation, they will be transferred to Islamabad,” it said, adding that they have been prepared for repatriation to their respective home countries under special arrangements. ACP Secretary General Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that so far, seven bodies have been recovered and airlifted to Skardu. The search operation continues for the eighth day as Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi and American Sarah Mallory Geis remain missing. Shigri said remains believed to belong to Geis had been airlifted on Saturday along with bodies of two other climbers, but her body has still not been found. The body of Nawang Thindu Sherpa was spotted but could not be recovered due to its location in a high-altitude, avalanche-prone area, Naila Kiani of the ACP told Dawn . A Pakistan Army helicopter on Thursday brought the five bodies to Skardu, where they were received by ACP, Baltistan Commissioner Kamal Khan, army officers, civil administration officials, the tourism department, the district administration and local representatives. The participants paid tribute to the deceased climbers, acknowledged their contributions and expressed their condolences to the bereaved families. Later, all the bodies were transferred to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Skardu, where the necessary legal formalities, documentation and identification procedures were completed, ACP said. The bodies were then placed in coffins, each draped with the national flag of the respective country before being accorded an official farewell with state honours. Officials said that the search and rescue operation was carried out under extremely challenging conditions. They praised the exceptional efforts of the local high-altitude porters, rescue personnel and mountaineers who took part in the operation, and also commended the rescue team’s professionalism and dedication. “Pakistan Army, local rescue teams and relevant agencies are participating in the search and rescue operation, and the search for the remaining missing mountaineers is continuing using all possible resources,” the ACP statement noted. The bodies of Purja, Wang, Nima Sherpa and Kili Pemba Sherpa had been recovered on Sunday and airlifted to the base camp on Wednesday. Previously, Gyalu Sherpa’s body had also been shifted to base camp. The five bodies could not be immediately moved from the base camp of Broad Peak as helicopter service was needed to airlift them, but bad weather had created difficulties in the transfer. The bodies of two other climbers, identified as Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy and Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung, had been recovered on Friday and their remains were later airlifted to Skardu.

items.title: Toxicologie et maintenance biomédicale : le Sénégal renforce ses capacités
items.description: Le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Dr Ibrahima Sy, a présidé, ce mercredi 5 août 2026, au Centre anti-poison sénégalais (CAP) de l’Hôpital de Fann, la cérémonie officielle de lancement des activités du laboratoire de toxicologie et de pharmacologie clinique. Réhabilité et doté d’équipements de dernière génération pour une enveloppe globale de 1,6 milliard de francs CFA, ce laboratoire permettra, selon une note de la tutelle publiée jeudi, d’améliorer le diagnostic des intoxications, de renforcer l’expertise médico-légale, la lutte contre le dopage, la recherche et la vigilance sanitaire. A lire aussi : L’hôpital Fann mobilise plus de 85 milliards de FCfa La cérémonie a également été marquée par la remise de deux véhicules spécialisés, d’une valeur globale de plus de 965 millions de FCFA. Il s’agit notamment d’un laboratoire mobile destiné à l’Agence sénégalaise de Réglementation pharmaceutique (ARP Sénégal) et d’un camion-atelier de maintenance biomédicale remis à la Direction des Équipements et de la Maintenance (MSHP). Ces investissements, réalisés avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale, contribuent, estime la tutelle, à la modernisation du système de santé et au renforcement de la sécurité sanitaire au Sénégal. M. DIEME

items.title: As Iran war drags on, Americans are bracing for more chaos in Middle East, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
items.description: By Jason Lange and Simon Lewis WASHINGTON, Aug 6 (Reuters) - Five months into the U.S. war with Iran, Americans who expect the Middle East to slide toward chaos outnumber those who see the war bringing more stability by three to one, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll. The six-day poll concluded on Monday, as Republican President Donald Trump again backed away from threatened "massive attacks" on Iran, underscoring uncertainty surrounding a conflict he initially predicted would bring a swift victory.

items.title: ‘Democracy under attack’: We’re not against accountability, but against selective justice – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has called for an end to what he describes as selective justice and political retaliation, insisting that the opposition is not against accountability but opposed to the unequal application of the law. Speaking at the “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on Thursday, August 6, Afenyo-Markin argued that Members of Parliament are being subjected to investigations after making contributions on the floor of Parliament. “We are not against accountability, but we are against selective justice,” he said. He claimed that an MP makes a contribution on the floor of Parliament and is subsequently invited by investigative agencies, questioning what he described as the selective application of the law. He also referred to concerns raised by some members of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) over the conditions under which suspects are held. According to him, former Minority Leader Haruna Iddrisu has complained on the floor of Parliament about what he described as unlawful conditions, while Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak has also raised concerns on the matter. Afenyo-Markin maintained that the opposition is merely expressing its views on the way the country is being governed and stressed that criticism of government should not be met with intimidation. He urged political leaders to end what he called the “you do me, I do you” approach to politics, saying Ghana’s democracy would only thrive if successive governments resisted the temptation to target political opponents. “As a country, we must end this vicious cycle of ‘you do me, I do you.’ I’ve been talking about this for quite some time now,” he said. The Minority Leader said his position was not influenced by the fact that members of his party were currently affected but by his long-held belief that politics should be conducted with decency and mutual respect. “I don’t say this because it is my people who are going through this situation. I say this because all my life I’ve believed that we can do politics in a very decent way. I believe in that decent approach to politics.” He further urged politicians to shift their attention from partisan disputes to addressing the country’s development challenges. “If you leave Accra and go deep into the hinterlands, you see the serious underdevelopment in our country. That should be what should occupy our minds as political leaders,” he said. Afenyo-Markin warned that if the alleged cycle of political persecution continues, it could make it difficult for moderate voices within the New Patriotic Party (NPP) to restrain more hardline elements when the party returns to power. “For me, if they don’t stop, it will be difficult for the moderates in the NPP to calm the nerves of the extremists when the NPP comes to office tomorrow. But is that what we want as a country? No. That’s not what we want.” He concluded by stressing that the demonstration was not against Ghana but a call for fairness, justice and the protection of democratic principles.

items.title: Bénin: le Sénat met en place son premier bureau, la présidence réservée aux membres de droit
items.description: Réuni ce jeudi 6 août 2026 pour élire son premier bureau, le Sénat béninois franchit une étape clé de son installation. Conformément à la Constitution, seuls les membres de droit de l'institution peuvent briguer les postes de président et de vice-président, tandis que le rapporteur peut être choisi parmi l'ensemble des sénateurs. Une semaine après son installation officielle, le Sénat du Bénin s'apprête à désigner les membres de son premier bureau. Cette élection, prévue ce jeudi 6 août 2026, intervient à la suite de l'entrée en vigueur du règlement intérieur de la chambre haute, validé le 3 août par la Cour constitutionnelle. D'après des informations rapportées par Banouto, l'absence de ce règlement avait retardé l'organisation du scrutin à l'issue de l'installation des 25 sénateurs, le 30 juillet dernier. Sa validation permet désormais à l'institution d'engager pleinement son fonctionnement. En application de l'article 113-5 de la Constitution, le bureau du Sénat est composé d'un président, d'un vice-président et d'un rapporteur, élus pour un mandat de cinq ans renouvelable. Toutefois, les deux premières fonctions sont exclusivement réservées aux membres de droit de l'institution, ce qui limite à onze personnalités les candidats potentiels à ces postes. Ce groupe comprend les anciens présidents de la République Nicéphore Dieudonné Soglo, Boni Yayi et Patrice Talon, les anciens présidents de l'Assemblée nationale Adrien Houngbédji, Bruno Amoussou, Mathurin Coffi Nago, Antoine Kolawolé Idji et Louis Vlavonou, ainsi que les anciens présidents de la Cour constitutionnelle Élisabeth Pognon, Théodore Holo et Robert Dossou. En revanche, la fonction de rapporteur est accessible à l'ensemble des membres du Sénat. La participation de Boni Yayi à cette première élection attire particulièrement l'attention. Le 22 juillet dernier, l'ancien président de la République avait annoncé sa décision de siéger finalement au Sénat, revenant ainsi sur son refus initial de prendre part à cette institution instaurée par la révision constitutionnelle de décembre 2025. Dans sa déclaration, il avait expliqué que le contexte politique avait changé depuis l'adoption de la réforme, faisant notamment référence à l'installation d'un «Parlement monocolore» et à la diminution des espaces de dialogue. Selon lui, le Sénat est désormais susceptible de devenir un cadre de concertation politique et un espace où pourront s'exprimer les préoccupations des citoyens. S'appuyant sur l'article 113-3 de la Constitution, Boni Yayi avait également affirmé qu'il exercerait son mandat de sénateur afin de travailler avec les autres membres de l'institution pour en faire «un vase d’honneur pour les intérêts du peuple». L'élection du premier bureau marque une étape déterminante dans la mise en œuvre du Parlement bicaméral voulu par la réforme constitutionnelle. Avec la désignation de son équipe dirigeante, le Sénat béninois entre désormais dans sa phase opérationnelle et amorce pleinement l'exercice de ses missions institutionnelles. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Bénin: le Sénat met en place son premier bureau, la présidence réservée aux membres de droit est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Gendarmerie nationale : Le colonel Théophile Tago prend officiellement le commandement de la 3e Légion
items.description: La 3e Légion de la Gendarmerie nationale a un nouveau commandement. Le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago a été installé dans ses nouvelles fonctions, ce jeudi 6 août 2026, en présence des autorités administratives, militaires, coutumières et communales, ainsi que de nombreux invités. La cérémonie a été presidée par le chef d’état-major de la Gendarmerie nationale, le colonel Issa Yaguibou. Le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago prend officiellement le commandement de la 3e Légion de la Gendarmerie nationale. Il succède à l'actuel chef d'etat-major de la Gendarmerie nationale Colonel Issa Yaguibou. Cette installation marque l’entrée en fonction du colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago à la tête de la 3e Légion de Gendarmerie dont le ressort couvre les régions du Kadiogo, du Nando, du Nazinon et de l’Oubri. Fort de vingt-quatre années de carrière militaire, le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago entend inscrire son action dans la dynamique de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). Le colonel Tago prend ainsi la relève du colonel Issa Yaguibou, récemment nommé à la tête de l’état-major de la Gendarmerie nationale, pour continuer l'œuvre de sécurisation du Burkina Faso. items.title: Catholic Bishops spoke for Nigerians – Archbishop Onuoha
items.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI – Reactions from the Presidency on the recent submission by the Catholic Bishops and the attempt to place a political tag on it, “is rather very unfortunate, as they spoke for Nigerians”. The National President of Christian Council of Nigeria, CCN, Most Rev. Dr. David O. C. Onuoha, stated this yesterday, while speaking with Vanguard in Owerri. Onuoha said: “The truth remains that the Roman Catholic Bishops Conference spoke not for the Church or any other body, but for the entire nation. “The matters they raised before the President were real, and affect every Nigerian, irrespective of tribe, religion or ethnicity. Continuing, the cleric said: “Rather than castigate them or live in denial of the pain, suffering, hardship, poverty and insecurity that are a present reality in Nigeria today, the Federal Government should see the Church as a partner in the search for a Nigeria that works. “Religious leaders are in constant touch with the people, both in the urban and rural areas. They live among them, and should be trusted for an unbiased assessment of how government policies affect the people of this nation. “The President should be wary of those assistants and staff who make enemies for the administration in the guise of defending the government. Those around the President, who present false pictures of the situation of things in the country in order to keep their positions and offices, are the real enemies of the people.” Answering another question, Archbishop Onuoha said: “Any leader, whose interest is for the good of the people he leads, is required to always be courageous enough to accept the truth no matter who says it or where it is coming from. As the bible has said, ‘you shall know the truth and the truth shall set you free’. “The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria should be commended for its constant, bold and courageous interventions for the wellbeing of the nation. “To single out any of them for vilification is not the way to go. The implication of not listening to the voice of wisdom and reason, such as the one in issue, is the government’s unwillingness to make policies that will benefit the people. The consequences there from are better imagined than experienced. “For the avoidance of doubt, government policies and reforms in the last three years have produced more adversity than prosperity. To review these policies for a more positive impact on the life of the people, and to ensure that people are safe and secure in the country, are not only desirable but also the basic expectations of the Nigerians.” The post Catholic Bishops spoke for Nigerians – Archbishop Onuoha appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rennes repousse une première offre de Fulham pour Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal
items.description: Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal continue d'attirer les convoitises en Premier League. Selon les informations du New York Times, Fulham a transmis une première offre de 23 millions d'euros au Stade Rennais pour s'attacher les services du défenseur central marocain. La proposition du club londonien a toutefois été rejetée par les dirigeants rennais, qui estiment leur joueur à un montant supérieur. Malgré ce refus, Fulham n'aurait pas abandonné le dossier et réfléchirait à revenir avec une offre revue à la hausse, tout en étudiant d'autres pistes pour renforcer sa défense. Âgé de 20 ans et originaire de Marrakech, Aït Boudlal a rejoint le Stade Rennais en 2024. Depuis son arrivée en Bretagne, l'international marocain s'est progressivement imposé, disputant 20 rencontres de Ligue 1 et inscrivant deux buts. S'il n'avait pas été retenu pour disputer la Coupe du monde 2026, le jeune défenseur figurait en revanche dans le groupe du Maroc lors de la dernière Coupe d'Afrique des nations, confirmant son statut de grand espoir des Lions de l'Atlas. Fulham cherche activement à renforcer son secteur défensif après le départ d'Issa Diop vers Ipswich Town. Le club anglais, désormais dirigé par Álvaro Arbeloa, a déjà animé son mercato avec les arrivées de Gonzalo Garcia et Cesar Palacios, recrutés en provenance du Real Madrid. Le dossier Aït Boudlal devrait rester l'un des principaux chantiers des Cottagers d'ici la fermeture du marché des transferts, alors que Rennes entend conserver son jeune défenseur ou obtenir une indemnité à la hauteur de son potentiel. The post Rennes repousse une première offre de Fulham pour Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Livestream: Gov’t holds interfaith memorial service for victims of August 6 helicopter crash
items.description: The government is holding a national interfaith memorial service in honour of the eight people who lost their lives in the August 6, 2025 helicopter crash. The ceremony is taking place at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), with President John Mahama, Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, government officials, families of the deceased and loved ones in attendance. The crash claimed the lives of Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane-Boamah and seven others, including officials and crew members, while they were travelling to the Ashanti Region to support efforts in the fight against illegal mining. The Ghana Armed Forces said the Ghana Air Force Z9 helicopter, carrying three crew members and five passengers, took off from Accra at 0912 GMT on August 6, 2025, and was heading to Obuasi when it crashed in a wooded area at Adansi Sikaman in the Ashanti Region. The aircraft was destroyed by fire following the crash, which shocked the nation and led to widespread tributes from political leaders, state institutions and members of the public. The memorial service is expected to provide an opportunity for the country to remember the lives and contributions of the departed and offer support to their families a year after the tragedy. Watch the live service below.

items.title: BBNaija: Flora fights back tears after learning she’s a Gambit
items.description: Big Brother has formally informed Flora that she is one of the Gambits in Big Brother Naija Season 11 and instructed her to keep the role hidden from the other housemates. The revelation was made during Flora’s diary session on Thursday, when Big Brother outlined the responsibilities attached to the assignment and stressed that her identity must remain confidential. “Flora, you are the Gambit. From this moment on, your identity as the Gambit must remain a secret. If you reveal your identity, you may be disqualified,” Big Brother told her. The announcement appeared to overwhelm Flora emotionally, as she struggled to hold back tears after hearing the implications of the role. Responding, she said, “I will try my best. I do not think staying longer is enough.” Host of the eviction show Ebuka Obi-Uchendu announced last Sunday that viewers had selected Flora and Aikou as the two Gambits for Season 11. Big Brother informed Aikou of his role during his diary session on Wednesday. As Gambits, Flora and Aikou are no longer eligible to compete for the ₦160 million grand prize. Instead, they will remain in the house as Big Brother’s undercover agents, carrying out secret missions designed to influence events and interactions among the other contestants without exposing their identities. items.title: Classement CAF 2026-2027 : le Horoya AC et la SOAR Académie, seuls représentants guinéens
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a dévoilé son classement des clubs pour la saison 2026-2027, établi sur la base des performances enregistrées par les équipes lors des cinq dernières saisons dans les compétitions interclubs africaines. Dans cette hiérarchie continentale, la Guinée ne compte que deux clubs parmi les 79 équipes classées : le Horoya AC et la SOAR Académie. Le Horoya AC demeure le club guinéen le mieux classé. Le club de Matam occupe la 41e place avec 5 points, confirmant son statut de principal ambassadeur du football guinéen sur la scène africaine grâce à ses participations régulières aux compétitions de la CAF. Quant à SOAR Académie, le club guinéen figure à la 73e position avec 1,5 point. Malgré un parcours continental plus limité, le club reste le deuxième représentant guinéen dans ce classement quinquennal de la CAF. Au sommet du classement, les Sud-Africains de Mamelodi Sundowns dominent avec 73 points, devant Al Ahly d'Égypte (66 points) et l'Espérance Sportive de Tunis (58 points). Pour le football guinéen, cette présence limitée à deux clubs explique les efforts qui restent à accomplir afin d'améliorer les performances des représentants nationaux dans les compétitions africaines.

items.title: Tunisie – Algérie | Aux origines d’un contentieux territorial
items.description: L’auteur de cette tribune répond à l’article du Dr Abderrahmen Cherfouh ‘‘En diabolisant l’Algérie, on dessert les intérêts de la Tunisie’’ , qui répondait, pour sa part, à un article de l’ambassadeur Elyes Kasri intitulé ‘‘Les menaces réelles de l’instabilité tunisienne’’ , tous deux publiés par Kapitalis. Il situe les relations tuniso-algériennes, et notamment les vieux différends frontaliers entre les deux pays, dans leur contexte historique exact, loin de toute propagande ou de révisionnisme. (Photo : Houari Boumediene revient sur la parole donnée par le GPRA et Ahmed Ben Bella à Habib Bourguiba). Abderrahmane Fekih * Je n’ai aucune raison de douter de votre sincérité mais je dois à la vérité d’apporter quelques éclaircissements à votre discours par des faits historiques que vous semblez ignorer, dans le seul but de rétablir la vérité afin de mieux dépasser nos malentendus pour ne pas dire nos différends. Attaché comme vous à des relations algéro-tunisiennes de coopération fraternelle à l’abri de tous risques de conflit mais j’ai du mal à comprendre les faits exposés ci-après à moins que vous ayez des éléments de réponse correctifs que je ne connais pas. La dimension coloniale des frontières terrestres Durant l’occupation de l’Algérie par la France celle-ci se croyant installée pour toujours a annexé plus d’un territoire de tous les pays limitrophes à l’Algérie : c’est une vérité historique bien établie. A l’aube de l’indépendance, la Tunisie a réclamé à la France de lui restituer les territoires spoliés , le contentieux n’est-il pas franco-tunisien sur le plan juridique Dr. Cherfouh ? La réaction du GPRA à l’époque fut immédiate, en prétendant que c’est «un coup de poignard dans le dos de l’Algérie combattante» et d’ajouter qu’après l’indépendance de l’Algérie «le problème sera réglé entre frères». La mauvaise foi du GPRA ne peut être plus flagrante car transformer un litige franco-tunisien en litige algéro-tunisien n’est pas la meilleure façon de le résoudre, mais d’ «acheter du temps ! » . Car la France ayant rogné de façon arbitraire des terres sur le territoire tunisien pour les annexer à l’Algérie, il était de son devoir de corriger son abus de pouvoir d’autant plus qu’elle avait le pouvoir de le faire sans aucune difficulté et sans léser l’Algérie : c’était juste retour à la situation antérieure. Le GPRA n’a rien voulu savoir et a maintenu sa position contre toute logique. Ainsi donc tout se passe comme si le GPRA s’est déjà approprié les territoires annexés. Quand l’Algérie a recouvré son indépendance le gouvernement tunisien a rappelé au gouvernement algérien sa promesse de solution à l’amiable ( «entre frères» !) du problème. Mais le gouvernement algérien, au lieu d’honorer son engagement envers la Tunisie (vous savez certainement comme moi le caractère sacré de la parole donnée dans notre culture commune), a préféré se référer au principe de ne pas modifier les frontières héritées de la colonisation décrété par l’Organisation de l’Unité Africaine de l’époque pour éviter à l’Afrique les affres des guerres de frontières. Ce principe étant décrété après l’engagement pris par le GPRA n’est pas opposable à la Tunisie car il ne pouvait pas avoir d’effet rétroactif (vous en convenez j’espère, vous qui semblez si bien connaitre le droit). Devant la position ferme de l’Etat algérien, Bourguiba a préféré contre mauvaise fortune faire bon cœur pour ne pas entrer en conflit (pour ne pas dire en guerre) contre son voisin en déclarant qu’ «il renonce à ses revendications (pourtant légitimes) en hommage aux martyres algériens» . C’est dans ce contexte qu’il faut placer l’accord du 20 mars 1970 : ce dernier n’est pas le résultat d’une négociation (mais d’un rapport de forces !) entre deux partenaires égaux mais entre une Algérie dominante imbue de sa puissance (et non de son droit) et une Tunisie qui n’a pour elle que la légitimité des faits historiques qui ne pèsent pas lourds malheureusement dans les relations internationales. Certes l’accord ci-dessus (résultat du rapport des forces de l’époque !) a réglé définitivement le problème sur le plan juridique pour établir la paix entre voisins mais pas sur le plan légitimité. La mémoire populaire en gardera souvenir longtemps comme d’une injustice insupportable. Le comble c’est que l’Etat Algérien, pour remercier Bourguiba de son geste de conciliation, n’a pas trouvé mieux que de forer un puit oblique pour pomper le pétrole du seul bassin pétrolier tunisien El Borma ! On ne peut pas qualifier cet acte de bienveillant ni de fraternel mais bel et bien de prédateur, ne vous en déplaise ! La sécurité énergétique en question Cette sécurité n’est pas due à la magnanimité de l’Algérie ni à sa bienveillance envers la Tunisie mais à la position stratégique dont l’Algérie bénéficie pour exporter son gaz vers l’Europe. Donc un peu d’humilité SVP (pour ne pas dire trêve d’arrogance !). Vous prétendez que l’Algérie «subventionne le gaz qui éclaire les foyers tunisiens» sans préciser à quelle hauteur, c’est pour le moins une contrevérité (pour ne pas dire une insulte gratuite aux Tunisiens), car les fournitures de gaz à la Tunisie sont régies par la loi de l’offre et la demande et les prix sur le marché international (je suis bien placé pour le savoir en tant qu’ingénieur ex-chef du Département de la distribution électrique de la Steg à la retraite) : donc l’Algérie ne nous fait pas de cadeaux contrairement à vos insinuations. Les vérités historiques étant ainsi établies, à mon humble avis les peuples nord-africains resteront unis à jamais par les liens de fraternité, de sang et d’entraide tissés durant des siècles de vie commune malgré les aléas politiques. Mais les responsables algériens seront toujours vus par les Tunisiens comme arrogants, dominateurs et particulièrement malveillants envers la Tunisie, tant qu’ils ne changent pas de comportements sur la base du principe «il faut rendre à César ce qui appartient à César ! Est-ce trop demander ?» J’ose espérer que la compétition entre les responsables nord-africains pour exercer leur hégémonie sur la Région se transforme en volonté de servir sincèrement les intérêts bien compris de leurs peuples respectifs loin de tout esprit hégémonique et de toute volonté de puissance. Ils gagneraient à réduire leurs égos pour se mettre au service de leurs peuples et non au service de leurs intérêts personnels étroits. Ces derniers ont coûté déjà à la communauté nord-africaine la non-réalisation de son unité décidée pourtant par l’accord de Tanger de 1958, la même année que la création du pool charbon acier fondateur de l’Union Européenne actuelle. Tandis que les Européens que tout séparent (langues, religions, histoires tumultueuses, etc.) construisent leur Etat Fédéral patiemment «pierre à pierre et brique à brique», nos leaders ont perdu leur temps dans des querelles marginales stériles (d’abord querelle de leadership ensuite le problème du Sahara créé de toutes pièces et maintenant le Maroc trouve son intérêt avec le pire ennemi des Arabes et des Musulmans, Israël, et non avec son voisin, l’Algérie, à laquelle tout le lie (géographie, langue, culture, religion, histoire commune, etc.). Le statu quo n’est pas dans l’intérêt des peuples nord-africains mais il faut espérer que ces derniers finissent par imposer à leurs leaders les mesures correctives nécessaires pour assurer d’abord la réalisation de l’unité nord-africaine ensuite sa prospérité. * Ingénieur, ex-chef du département de la distribution électrique de la Steg à la retraite. L’article Tunisie – Algérie | Aux origines d’un contentieux territorial est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: 6 août 1968 – 6 août 2026 : 58 ans du rappel à Dieu de Serigne Fallou Mbacké
items.description: Il était le deuxième Khalife général des Mourides, Serigne Fallou Mbacké, né en 1889, a accédé à la tête de la confrérie à la suite du rappel à Dieu de son frère Serigne Mouhamadou Moustapha Mbacké, en 1945. Ainsi, l’initiateur du Grand Magal de Touba guidera la Mouridiyyah pendant 23 ans. Il sera rappelé à Dieu le 6 août 1968. Fils de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba, le deuxième khalife du Mouridisme, Serigne Fallou Mbacké, est né en 1889. Il a grandi dans un foyer entièrement dédié à la foi, à l’éducation et au service d’Allah. Formé dès son jeune âge au Saint Coran et aux sciences religieuses par de grands maîtres, il incarna très tôt la discipline, la rigueur et la fidélité à la voie mouride. Son parcours le mena à assumer le khalifat général de la Mouridiyyah en 1945, à la suite du rappel à Dieu de son frère aîné et premier khalife général des mourides, Serigne Mouhamadou Moustapha Mbacké. Un règne qui a débuté dans un contexte difficile marqué par la pauvreté et la famine. A lire aussi : Magal de Kazou Rajab : « Tout est fin prêt » à Touba Cependant, dès les premières années de son magistère, un renouveau s’opéra au sein de la communauté, attribué à la baraka de ses prières et à son sens élevé des responsabilités. En 1947, il consacra la célébration du premier Grand Magal à Touba, faisant de la ville sainte le cœur du rassemblement mouride. Attaché à l’intention de son père, il accomplit le pèlerinage aux Lieux Saints de l’Islam en 1928, marquant une étape spirituelle majeure de son parcours. Sous son magistère, Touba connut une transformation durable : l’achèvement et l’inauguration de la Grande Mosquée le 7 juin 1963, en présence du président de la République de l’époque, Léopold Sédar Senghor ; l’urbanisation de la ville, l’accès à l’eau et à l’électricité, ainsi que la mise en place d’infrastructures sociales essentielles. Il peut citer aussi la création du marché Ocass, devenu l’un des plus grands centres commerciaux du pays. Par son enseignement, ses relations spirituelles profondes et son engagement constant au service des populations, il laissa un héritage durable, façonnant la Mouridiyyah et faisant de Touba un centre spirituel, social et économique toujours vivant. Sur le plan éducatif et spirituel, il a créé un “daara” (école coranique) à l’intérieur de la grande mosquée de Touba pour l’apprentissage du Coran et l’enseignement des valeurs islamiques. Au-delà, il offre l’opportunité, pour des centaines de disciples mourides, d’effectuer un séjour spirituel à Ndindy, un village fondé en 1913 par Serigne Fallou et qui fait désormais partie de la commune de Touba. Il a également instauré la lecture quotidienne du Saint Coran dans la grande mosquée, une tradition toujours perpétuée. Convaincu que l’agriculture constituait la base du développement du mouridisme, Serigne Fallou Mbacké initia une véritable révolution agricole à travers la fondation de nombreux villages, faisant du travail licite un pilier du financement de la mosquée et de la solidarité sociale. Dans le domaine de l’urbanisme, Serigne Fallou Mbacké a procédé au lotissement de Touba en 1959, afin d’améliorer le cadre de vie des populations. Il a aussi œuvré au renforcement de l’approvisionnement de la cité religieuse en eau potable, notamment à travers la construction de nombreux puits. M. DIEME

items.title: 16e édition du SITHO : La région du Guiriko à l’honneur, 50 000 visiteurs espérés
items.description: Le Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT), par l’intermédiaire de Faso Tourisme, a tenu une conférence de presse, ce jeudi 6 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, pour marquer le lancement officiel des activités de la 16e édition du Salon international du tourisme et de l’hôtellerie de Ouagadougou (SITHO). La cérémonie était présidée par le secrétaire général du MCCAT, Bètamou Fidèle Aymar Tamini. Prévu du 22 au 27 septembre 2026 sur le site du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), cet événement majeur pour les acteurs du tourisme et de l’hôtellerie vise à promouvoir la destination Burkina Faso et à renforcer les échanges entre professionnels du secteur. Placée sous le thème « Financement des projets structurants : un levier pour le développement du tourisme », cette nouvelle édition entend, selon les organisateurs, consolider les acquis des années précédentes pour conforter la place du salon comme vitrine privilégiée du tourisme burkinabè. La région du Guiriko a, par ailleurs, été désignée région invitée d’honneur. Le programme prévoit notamment le Forum des acteurs du tourisme de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), des rencontres d’affaires (B to B) ainsi que l’Éduc’Tour, une initiative destinée à faire découvrir aux professionnels les richesses touristiques du Burkina Faso. Pour cette 16e édition, les organisateurs ambitionnent d’attirer au moins 50 000 visiteurs, 500 exposants, une dizaine de pays participants, 30 professionnels du voyage dans le cadre de l’Éduc’Tour, 1 500 participants aux excursions touristiques grand public et 1 000 visiteurs pour l’espace de visites virtuelles. Des détails à venir sur Minute.bf

items.title: Cameroun : Mgr Andrew Nkea est le nouveau Grand chancelier de l’UCAC
items.description: © DR L'archevêque de Bamenda et président de Conférence épiscopale nationale du Cameroun remplace à cette charge Mgr Jean Mbarga, archevêque de Yaoundé. La gouvernance de l'université catholique d'Afrique centrale entre dans une nouvelle ère. Les évêques du Cameroun confient à Mgr Andrew Nkea la charge de Grand chancelier de l'Ucac. La décision émane d'une consultation des évêques du Cameroun au terme de laquelle 13 votants sur 19 ont choisi l'archevêque de Bamenda pour veiller sur la gouvernance de l'institution universitaire sous régionale. Le secrétaire général de la Conférence épiscopale nationale, Mgr Paul Nyaga, a porté la nouvelle par correspondance en date du 04 août 2026 au président de l'Association des conférences épiscopales de la région d'Afrique centrale, Mgr Bertrand Guy Richard Appora Ngalanibe, par ailleurs président de la Conférence épiscopale centrafricaine. Garant de de l'identité catholique de l'Ucac, le Grand chancelier exerce une mission similaire à celle d'un président du conseil d'administration au sein d'une université d'Etat. Cette mission consiste à présider le conseil supérieur de l'université regroupant les conférences épiscopales de l'association des conférences épiscopales d'Afrique centrale ; il représente aussi l'université auprès des instances ecclésiastiques régionales et du Vatican. Dans son rôle d'orientation et de supervision, il assure la supervision des orientations globales de l'Ucac en collaboration avec le recteur. Il soutient par ailleurs le rayonnement académique de l'université. Souvent élu au terme d'une consultation et d'un vote de l'Assemblée plénière des évêques de la sous-région, il est confirmé par le Vatican. Mgr Andrew Nkea entre ainsi dans la liste des prélats désignés pour assurer la charge du Grand chancelier de l'Ucac. Il poursuivra la mission de Mgr Jean Mbarga, lui qui a remplacé Mgr Victor Tonye Bakot, le successeur à cette charge du Cardinal Christian Tumi de regrettée mémoire, ancien archevêque de Douala. Il va exercer cette charge cumulativement avec celle de Grand chancelier de Pax University Institute de Ndop appartenant à l’archidiocèse de Bamenda ; de Grand chancelier de l’Université catholique du Cameroun appartenant à la province ecclésiastique de Bamenda. Cet article Cameroun : Mgr Andrew Nkea est le nouveau Grand chancelier de l'UCAC est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Karachi court allows exhumation of Mir Raza Ali's body amid controversy over autopsy
items.description: KARACHI: A Karachi court on Thursday allowed the exhumation of Institute of Business Administration (IBA) graduate Mir Raza Ali’s body, which was found last month with a gunshot wound to the chest in the bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The court issued the order on an application filed by Ali’s father, after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination. In its order, the court directed the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medico-legal board for the exhumation of Ali’s body “under intimation to this court at the earliest possible date and time”. The court order, issued after the ruling by Judicial Magistrate Hameedullah, stated that Ali’s father, Mir Hussain Ali Khan, had filed an application seeking the exhumation of his son’s body in accordance with law. He also requested the formation of a medico-legal board, comprising senior forensic experts and pathologists, under the Karachi police surgeon “to conduct a fresh and comprehensive” medico-legal examination and postmortem, as well as X-ray, DNA, forensic and chemical examination of the body to ascertain the actual cause of death. The court observed that the prosecutor had not raised any objection to allowing the application, and permitted the exhumation of Ali’s body. Moreover, the court office was directed to issue a letter to the Sindh health secretary and Karachi police surgeon for the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose. “The Ferozabad station house officer is also directed to make arrangements along with the investigating officer (IO) for such proceedings,” the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn read. The court had earlier reserved its decision on the application after the counsel for the applicant, Jibran Nasir, and the prosecutor presented their arguments. Nasir contended that police could not object to the exhumation. But, the judge observed that a notice would have to be issued to police. Nasir argued that the police surgeon and the medico-legal officer would have to conduct the exhumation, further stating that the police surgeon had identified loopholes in the postmortem report. “No X-ray was done; the cause of the death has not been determined,” he said. The judge then asked the prosecution how the court could issue an order for the body’s exhumation without issuing a notice to the IO. If the prosecution had no objection, the order would be issued, he added. The prosecutor replied that they had no objection to the exhumation. “This is a matter involving a human life,” he said. At that point, Nasir argued that issuing a notice to the IO would further delay the matter. The court then reserved its ruling on the application and later allowed the exhumation of Ali’s body. Controversy over autopsy Raza, an IBA graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. Police maintain that the investigation has revealed that Ali had been facing financial difficulties and had asked his friends for money the night he died. According to police, he had left his home in PECHS Block-2 and hired a taxi through an app. The taxi driver dropped him a short distance from the spot where his body was found, police said. While Ali’s family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide, claiming they have uncovered significant evidence that sheds light on the 25-year-old’s mental state. The case took a new turn when Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. She said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. While it was scientifically possible for a bullet to enter through the back and exit from the front, she stressed that her assessment was based only on the postmortem report and photographs, as she had not examined the body herself. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

items.title: Face aux tensions régionales, le Japon accélère l'intégration de l'IA dans son armée
items.description: Confronté à un environnement sécuritaire de plus en plus tendu en Indo-Pacifique, le Japon entend accélérer la modernisation de ses forces armées en misant sur l'intelligence artificielle. Tokyo envisage notamment de s'appuyer sur des technologies développées par les entreprises américaines Palantir et Anduril, tout en poursuivant le développement de solutions nationales afin de préserver sa souveraineté. Dans son Livre blanc annuel sur la défense, le gouvernement japonais met en garde contre la dégradation rapide de la situation sécuritaire dans la région, marquée par l'intensification des activités militaires de la Chine ainsi que par les menaces persistantes de la Corée du Nord et de la Russie. Le ministre japonais de la Défense, Shinjiro Koizumi, a évoqué un « sentiment d'urgence et de crise », estimant que le pays devait adapter rapidement ses capacités militaires aux nouveaux défis stratégiques. Selon le quotidien économique Nikkei, le Japon prévoit d'intégrer des systèmes d'intelligence artificielle au sein des centres de commandement des Forces d'autodéfense afin d'accélérer la prise de décision, d'améliorer l'analyse des données et de renforcer l'interopérabilité avec les forces américaines. Parmi les solutions étudiées figurent le Maven Smart System (MSS) de Palantir Technologies, déjà utilisé par l'armée américaine pour analyser les données du champ de bataille et assister l'identification de cibles, ainsi que la plateforme Lattice développée par Anduril, capable de connecter drones et capteurs pour offrir une vision globale du terrain et coordonner des opérations, même dans des environnements où les communications sont perturbées. Les autorités japonaises souhaitent déployer ces technologies au cours des cinq prochaines années afin d'améliorer les capacités de contre-attaque, la défense antimissile ainsi que le pilotage de drones. Les modalités précises de cette modernisation devraient être arrêtées d'ici la fin de l'année, dans le cadre de la révision des principaux documents de sécurité nationale. Ce projet soulève toutefois des questions de souveraineté. Les systèmes d'intelligence artificielle étant appelés à traiter des données classifiées, Tokyo souhaite limiter sa dépendance aux technologies étrangères. Le gouvernement japonais envisage ainsi de développer une architecture hybride combinant des solutions américaines avec un système de commandement conçu localement. La start-up japonaise Sakana AI apparaît comme l'un des acteurs clés de cette stratégie grâce à son logiciel Sakana Fugu, capable d'orchestrer plusieurs modèles d'intelligence artificielle selon les besoins opérationnels. En parallèle, le Japon prévoit de rapatrier sur son territoire ses infrastructures critiques, notamment les centres de données et les systèmes de traitement des informations sensibles, afin de renforcer la protection de ses données et de bâtir, à terme, un écosystème d'intelligence artificielle militaire plus autonome. The post Face aux tensions régionales, le Japon accélère l'intégration de l'IA dans son armée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
