UK appoints Vicky Seymour as deputy high commissioner in Abuja
items.description: By Favour Ulebor The United Kingdom Government has appointed Ms Vicky Seymour as the new Deputy High Commissioner in Abuja, succeeding Mrs Gill Lever OBE, who completed her posting in June 2026. The appointment was announced in a statement on Thursday, which noted that Seymour has assumed her duties in Abuja and will support efforts to strengthen the longstanding partnership between the UK and Nigeria across areas including economic growth, security, migration, development, international cooperation and people-to-people relations. According to the statement, Seymour brings more than 20 years of experience in diplomacy, international development and government service. Before her appointment, she served as Head of the East Africa Department at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), a position she held from 2023. She had also previously led the FCDO’s Trade Diplomacy Department and served as Development Director in Mozambique. The statement further said her career includes senior leadership roles in several African countries, including Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, as well as in Afghanistan. She has also held positions focused on climate issues, security and economic development. Prior to joining the UK civil service, Seymour worked in the not-for-profit sector, where she focused on migration-related issues. Speaking on her appointment, Seymour said, “I am delighted to be taking up the role of Deputy High Commissioner in Abuja. I look forward to getting to know this extraordinary country, meeting people from across Nigeria’s diverse communities, and building on the strong partnership that already exists between our two countries. Together, I hope we can continue creating opportunities for greater collaboration and links between our people in the years ahead.” The post UK appoints Vicky Seymour as deputy high commissioner in Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NAAE rejects proposed TSC review, warns against weakening NCAA funding
items.description: By Nnasom David The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) chapter of the National Association of Air Traffic Engineers (NAAE) has rejected a recent position by the association’s national leadership on the proposed review of the Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) sharing formula, warning that any reduction in the regulator’s allocation could undermine aviation safety oversight in Nigeria. The NCAA chapter, in a communiqué signed by its Chairman, Agunloye Fredrick O., said the position credited to the National President of NAAE did not represent the views of its members because the chapter was neither consulted nor carried along before the publication. The group said issues concerning the TSC sharing formula required broad consultation among stakeholders due to the importance of the charge to the operations of aviation agencies. “We therefore dissociate ourselves from the publication and respectfully state that it should not be interpreted as the collective position of all NAAE members across the aviation industry,” the communiqué stated. The Ticket Sales Charge is a statutory levy collected from airline passengers and shared among aviation agencies to support their respective mandates. The NCAA chapter argued that the Authority requires adequate funding from the charge to carry out its regulatory responsibilities, noting that the agency does not operate airports, provide air navigation services or generate significant commercial revenue. It said funds from the TSC support key regulatory functions, including airline certification and licensing, safety inspections, surveillance activities, economic regulation, consumer protection, enforcement of aviation regulations and implementation of International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards. The association warned that reducing NCAA’s share of the charge could lead to fewer safety inspections, delays in certification and approvals, reduced training opportunities for safety inspectors, inability to acquire specialised oversight equipment and possible challenges during international safety audits. According to the communiqué, weakened funding for the regulator could also affect Nigeria’s aviation safety rating and international confidence in the country’s oversight system. “Strong regulation remains the foundation of every safe aviation system. Effective regulation provides oversight over every operator, every airport, every air navigation service provider and every aviation organisation,” it said. While acknowledging the importance of adequate funding for the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), particularly in maintaining Communications, Navigation, Surveillance and Air Traffic Management infrastructure, the NCAA chapter said strengthening one agency should not undermine another institution’s statutory responsibilities. The group maintained that the TSC debate should not become a competition among aviation agencies but should focus on finding sustainable funding solutions that support all institutions within the sector. It called on stakeholders and the leadership of NAAE to prioritise consultation, dialogue and evidence-based engagement before taking public positions on national aviation policies. The association reaffirmed its commitment to aviation safety, regulatory excellence and cooperation among agencies for the development of Nigeria’s aviation industry. The post NAAE rejects proposed TSC review, warns against weakening NCAA funding appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ministère de la Femme, de la Famille et des Solidarités- Alerte ! Vacances scolaires en Guinée : protégeons nos filles contre l’excision
items.description: Les grandes vacances scolaires sont souvent synonymes de retrouvailles familiales, de voyages, de cérémonies et de moments de partage. Mais cette période peut aussi exposer certaines filles à des pratiques susceptibles de compromettre leur santé et leur bien-être, notamment l’excision. Les déplacements familiaux, les séjours dans certaines localités et les cérémonies organisées pendant cette période peuvent parfois exposer les filles à des situations à risque. C’est pourquoi une vigilance particulière est nécessaire afin de prévenir toute pratique susceptible de porter atteinte à leur intégrité et à leur avenir. L’excision est une pratique qui consiste à retirer une partie ou la totalité des organes génitaux externes d’une fille. Contrairement aux idées encore véhiculées dans certaines communautés, cette pratique ne repose sur aucune base religieuse ni morale et ne présente aucun avantage pour la santé. Elle ne prépare pas une fille à devenir une meilleure femme et ne contribue pas à son épanouissement. Au contraire, l’excision peut avoir des conséquences graves sur la santé physique et psychologique des filles et des femmes qui la subissent. Les dangers de l’excision sont notamment : • Des conséquences graves sur la santé physique : douleurs, saignements, infections, complications gynécologiques et risques lors de la grossesse et de l’accouchement. • Des conséquences psychologiques et émotionnelles : traumatismes, souffrances psychologiques, perte d’estime de soi et impacts durables sur le bien-être des filles et des femmes. • Une atteinte aux droits et à l’épanouissement des filles : l’excision constitue une violence qui porte atteinte à leur intégrité physique, leur dignité et leur droit de grandir dans un environnement protecteur. Face à ces réalités, le Ministère de la Femme, de la Famille et des Solidarités réaffirme son engagement à protéger les filles contre toutes les formes de violences, à promouvoir leur santé, leur dignité et leurs droits. Il invite les familles à mieux comprendre les dangers de l’excision et à faire des choix responsables qui garantissent la sécurité et l’avenir de leurs filles. La protection de nos filles nous concerne tous. Chaque parent, chaque famille et chaque acteur de la communauté a un rôle à jouer pour prévenir l’excision et créer un environnement favorable à leur épanouissement. Les responsables communautaires, les leaders religieux, les enseignants, les agents de santé, les associations et les médias sont également appelés à contribuer à la diffusion des messages de prévention et à l’accompagnement des familles. Aux parents, aux familles et à toutes les personnes engagées dans la protection des filles, voici quelques gestes essentiels : • Restons vigilants et à l’écoute des filles : dialoguons avec elles, prenons en compte leurs préoccupations et veillons à leur bien-être. • Informons-nous et sensibilisons notre entourage : partageons des messages de prévention sur les dangers de l’excision et contribuons à déconstruire les idées reçues qui entourent cette pratique. • Favorisons un dialogue familial et communautaire bienveillant : créons un climat de confiance permettant aux filles de s’exprimer librement et mobilisons les acteurs communautaires autour de leur protection. • Agissons face aux situations à risque : toute situation préoccupante ou tout projet d’excision doit être signalé aux services compétents de protection de l’enfant ou aux structures d’accompagnement disponibles afin de garantir une intervention adaptée. Pendant les vacances scolaires, restons attentifs aux filles qui nous entourent. Les écouter, les protéger et leur garantir un environnement sûr, c’est contribuer à leur permettre de grandir en bonne santé, de préserver leur dignité et de vivre pleinement leur avenir. items.title: Imran's sons express concerns about father's health in fresh interview with CNN
items.description: The sons of ex-prime minister Imran Khan, Kasim and Sulaiman, have reiterated concerns about their incarcerated father’s health in a fresh interview with CNN published on Thursday. Their interview comes as the PTI marked three years since Imran was imprisoned on Aug 5, 2023 for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts. After his eye ailment came to light in January, the PTI founder’s family and party leaders have repeatedly voiced concerns over a lack of access to him. In the CNN interview, Kasim and Sulaiman said they had “no updates because his (Imran’s) family, doctors [and] lawyers haven’t been allowed to see him for seven months”. “Been more in the dark than we’ve ever been through his incarceration,” Kasim said, noting the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) order for a phone call between them every two weeks. Speaking to CNN from London, the duo claimed that each time they speak to the media about their father, Pakistani authorities made it harder for them to see him by allegedly delaying their visas or bogging them down with other administrative issues. “We’re trying, we’d like to go, but nothing’s coming through,” Kasim said. “There’s no reason we shouldn’t be accepted for a visa.” While the government has previously said that Kasim and Sulaiman were “ welcome ” to visit Pakistan on their National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (Nicop), Imran’s sons said those cards have expired. “So we’re not able to go by those, and the visa has never come; there were technical difficulties,” Kasim said. CNN also quoted the information ministry as saying that Kasim and Sulaiman had Nicops, which meant they did not require visas to enter Pakistan. The ministry said their claims were “misleading and appear to convert an administrative process into an issue of political point-scoring”. The publication noted that the ministry did not address the duo’s claim that their Nicops had not been renewed. Asked if there was a chance their father could reach a “deal with the government, the sons thought it unlikely”, CNN reported. Sulaiman said Imran “wouldn’t [reach a deal that left] the other political prisoners in there … unless they were able to get some kind of resolution as well”. Kasim expressed a similar opinion, though he added it was “hard to say”. “They’re refusing to show us any kind of health report. So his health may have deteriorated significantly since then,” he said. Speaking on the charges against his father, Kasim termed them as “plain lies and deceit”. Asked about his message to the world, Kasim said “anyone with the power to take action” should take notice of the situation, insisting that the majority of the people voted for Imran in the elections and he was “behind bars for no good reason”. 3 years behind bars Imran was sent to jail on Aug 5, 2023 in the Toshakhana case. However, he is also serving a 14-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case , was convicted in another Toshakhana case in December 2025 and also faces pending trials in terrorism cases related to the May 9, 2023 riots . Imran’s PTI held rallies in major cities yesterday to demand his release, with the gatherings in Karachi and Lahore met with police action and arrests. Despite the IHC mandating meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Imran has not met his family or party leaders since his sister Uzma Khanum met him last December. His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January, for which the government has provided him treatment . The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations. Imran’s sisters and opposition leaders have demanded that the former premier be shifted to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, be treated in the presence of his personal physicians and allowed to meet his family.

items.title: I’ll resign from APC if Tinubu disrespects Catholic Church – Orji Kalu
items.description: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu has said he would quit the All Progressives Congress if President Bola Tinubu ever showed disrespect toward the opposition or the Catholic Church. The senator representing Abia North made the statement during Wednesday’s edition of Channels Television’s Politics Today, amid the ongoing controversy over Tinubu’s meeting with Catholic bishops as highlighted by John Cardinal Onaiyekan. Kalu, a former governor of Abia State, defended the President, insisting that Tinubu did not insult the Catholic bishops and therefore had nothing to apologise for. “Any day President Tinubu has disrespect for the opposition, or has disrespect for the Catholic Church, I’d resign from the APC. The President can never insult the Catholic bishop, knowing him. The President didn’t say anything that needs apology. If there is anything wrong the Presidency has done, he should apologise,” Kalu said. He described Tinubu as a longstanding friend of the Catholic Church and said there was nothing wrong with the bishops openly expressing concerns to the President. “Tinubu has a good relationship with the Catholic Church. Nothing wrong in what the Catholic bishops said. Tinubu is not an enemy to Catholic bishops, one of their best friends. Tinubu by no means insulted the bishops. I didn’t see it,” he said. Kalu also argued that comments made by Onaiyekan after the meeting should not automatically be treated as the official position of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria. “The discussion the Catholic bishops had with President Tinubu is not personal. They had cameras there, so it’s a public discussion. Onaiyekan did not go with other Catholic bishops. That might be his opinion,” he said. He added that the communiqué issued after the meeting was read by the President of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference, noting that individual cardinals and archbishops were entitled to their own opinions. The debate began after Onaiyekan told journalists that the bishops informed Tinubu that Nigeria was “bleeding” and that many citizens were struggling under severe economic hardship. According to Onaiyekan, Tinubu told the bishops that he disagreed with them about the state of the economy. items.title: Ceuta : un rapport pointe le rôle des réseaux sociaux dans l'afflux de migrants
items.description: Les tentatives massives de passage vers Ceuta des 30 et 31 juillet 2026 ont ete precedees de plusieurs semaines d'activite sur les reseaux sociaux. Un rapport fonde sur des techniques de renseignement en sources ouvertes, realise par l'analyste espagnol Jose María Gil Garre, retrace cette mobilisation numerique entre le 15 juin et le 2 août. Le document n'emane pas d'un organisme officiel espagnol et n'etablit aucune responsabilite penale ou politique. Il decrit toutefois la maniere dont une decision judiciaire a ete simplifiee, puis transformee en arguments en faveur des departs. Le phenomene s'est accelere apres une decision rendue le 8 juillet par le Tribunal supreme espagnol sur le traitement des migrants interceptes en mer. Sur internet, son contenu a ete presente de maniere trompeuse. Des publications affirmaient que les personnes arrivant a Ceuta par voie maritime ne pourraient plus etre renvoyees immediatement. Cette interpretation a progressivement installe l'idee que l'acces a Ceuta etait devenu plus simple et moins risque. a partir de ce recit, les messages ont change de nature : d'abord generaux et incitatifs, ils sont ensuite devenus plus visuels, puis directement operationnels. Des videos aux consignes de depart L'analyse distingue une chaîne numerique progressive. TikTok et Instagram attiraient l'attention, Facebook regroupait les informations pratiques et WhatsApp coordonnait les derniers deplacements. Sur TikTok, des videos montraient des traversees presentees comme reussies, des jeunes affirmant avoir atteint Ceuta et des portions du littoral decrites comme peu surveillees. Sans toujours fournir de consignes precises, ces contenus renforcaient l'idee que le passage etait realisable. Instagram prolongeait cette impression en relayant des temoignages et des images d'arrivees. Facebook servait davantage de reservoir d'informations. Au moins cinq groupes consacres aux passages vers Ceuta, reunissant plus de 250 000 membres au total, partageaient des cartes, des itineraires, des contacts et des conseils pratiques. a partir du 25 juillet, les echanges ont pris une dimension plus concrete. Des cartes indiquaient les points de depart, les distances approximatives et les parcours possibles a la nage depuis les cotes marocaines. Des palmes, des combinaisons, des bouees ou encore des kayaks etaient egalement proposes ou recommandes. WhatsApp intervenait dans la derniere etape. Les groupes de messagerie diffusaient les horaires, les lieux de rassemblement et des informations sur la surveillance de la frontiere. Des messages vocaux permettaient egalement de modifier rapidement les consignes selon la situation sur le terrain. Les 29 et 30 juillet, cette activite numerique a accompagne les deplacements signales vers la ville de Fnideq. Les videos entretenaient la mobilisation, Facebook centralisait les informations et WhatsApp transmettait les derniers rendez-vous. Le rapport ne releve cependant aucun commandement unique. Il decrit plutot un reseau decentralise, compose de profils, de groupes et de plateformes aux fonctions complementaires. Cette structure aurait permis a l'activite de se poursuivre, malgre la fermeture de certains groupes et la suppression de plusieurs comptes. Rabat pointe la desinformation et les reseaux de traite De son cote, Rabat attribue egalement cette crise a la desinformation numerique, tout en mettant en cause les reseaux de traite. Le directeur general du ministere marocain de l'Interieur, Rachid El Khalfi, a denonce « l'exploitation malveillante de l'espace numerique », la diffusion d'informations trompeuses et les interpretations erronees de decisions judiciaires. Selon les autorites marocaines, ces messages ont laisse croire qu'un passage vers Ceuta etait possible sans risque de renvoi immediat. Rabat estime qu'environ 40 000 personnes ont tente de rejoindre l'enclave, tandis que 1 135 tentatives ont ete enregistrees vers Melilla. Le bilan officiel marocain fait etat de 11 morts. Ce chiffre est conteste par l'Association marocaine des droits humains (AMDH) et le Conseil national des droits de l'Homme (CNDH), qui reclament davantage de transparence. Les autorites espagnoles font etat, pour leur part, de 72 morts parmi les quelques 60 000 personnes qui ont tente de rejoindre Ceuta. Les elements disponibles ne permettent pas d'expliquer l'ecart entre les differents bilans.

items.title: Le Président Tiani salue les résultats de la COLDEFF et demande la poursuite du recouvrement dans le respect de la dignité…
items.description: Le président de la République, chef de l’état, Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, a reçu en audience, le mercredi, le Bureau de la Commission de Lutte contre la Délinquance Économique, Financière et Fiscale (COLDEFF). La rencontre, qui s’est tenue dans la salle du Conseil, s’est déroulée en présence des membres du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie. Le Bureau de la COLDEFF a présenté au Chef de l’État le bilan de ses activités, portant essentiellement sur le recouvrement des avoirs de l’État. Les données exposées font état d’un progrès significatif : au 16 août 2025, les montants recouvrés s’élevaient à 63 808 497 269 F CFA en numéraire, auxquels s’ajoutaient plus de 5 milliards F CFA en biens immobiliers. Un an plus tard, au 5 août 2026, le total des recouvrements dépasse désormais 74 milliards F CFA, soit un gain de près de 12 milliards F CFA en numéraire sur la période, hors dation et hors biens immobiliers. Saluant le travail accompli, le Président Tiani a encouragé la COLDEFF à maintenir son action avec détermination et rigueur. Il a donné des instructions claires pour intensifier les efforts de recouvrement des avoirs dissipés, tout en insistant sur le respect de la dignité des personnes mises en cause. « L’objectif de la COLDEFF n’est pas d’envoyer les gens en prison. La sanction de la COLDEFF est la sanction pécuniaire », a-t-il rappelé, réaffirmant la philosophie de la Commission centrée sur la réparation financière des préjudices causés à l’État. Cette audience réaffirme la volonté des plus hautes autorités de renforcer la bonne gouvernance et la protection des ressources publiques, par des mécanismes de lutte contre la fraude et la délinquance économique qui privilégient le recouvrement et la réparation financière. Toutefois, à notre niveau, nous pensons que lorsque la gravité des faits l’exige, il serait important et opportun d’appliquer avec rigueur la loi pénale afin d’assurer une justice équitable au peuple nigérien et de décourager les instincts des voleurs de l’état. items.title: GMTF partners MDS-Lancet, Quest Medical Imaging to expand access to quality diagnostics
items.description: The Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF) has entered into a strategic partnership with MDS-Lancet Laboratories Ghana Limited and Quest Medical Imaging to improve access to quality diagnostic healthcare services across the country. The agreement seeks to combine GMTF’s mandate of supporting the prevention and treatment of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) with the expertise of MDS-Lancet Laboratories Ghana Limited and Quest Medical Imaging in delivering advanced medical diagnostic services. The partnership is expected to enhance access to timely, accurate and reliable diagnostic testing, supporting early detection of diseases and improving treatment outcomes for patients nationwide. Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Administrator of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, described the collaboration as a significant milestone in the Trust Fund’s efforts to establish partnerships that strengthen healthcare delivery. “Today marks a significant milestone as the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, MDS Lancet Laboratories Ghana Limited and Quest Medical Imaging formally establish a partnership that reflects our shared commitment to improving access to quality healthcare for the people of Ghana. Accurate and timely diagnostics are the cornerstone of effective treatment, and this collaboration represents an important investment in the health and wellbeing of Ghanaians,” she said. She expressed appreciation to the leadership of both organisations for their confidence in the partnership and reaffirmed GMTF’s commitment to working with key stakeholders to address the growing burden of non-communicable diseases. The Chief Executive Officer of MDS-Lancet Laboratories Ghana Limited, Dr Paul Sekyere-Nyantakyi, welcomed the partnership, noting that it aligns with the organisation’s objective of providing accessible and high-quality diagnostic services to support improved patient care. According to the partners, the collaboration will help strengthen Ghana’s healthcare system through innovation, technical expertise and coordinated efforts, while improving access to diagnostic services and supporting better clinical decision-making, particularly for patients managing chronic conditions. The agreement also reflects a shared commitment to building a long-term relationship anchored on trust, excellence and a common goal of improving healthcare outcomes. The Ghana Medical Trust Fund, MDS-Lancet Laboratories Ghana Limited and Quest Medical Imaging expressed confidence that the partnership will make a lasting contribution towards achieving more equitable and sustainable healthcare delivery in Ghana.

items.title: Bode George’s Abuja house funded by Rivers money, Wike’s aide insists
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has insisted that the Abuja property owned by former Peoples Democratic Party PDP Deputy National Chairman, Bode George, was acquired with funds traced to Rivers State. Olayinka, in a statement on Thursday, said the minister stood by his earlier claim on the matter, stressing that the issue was never about who sold the property or the agent involved, but the source of the money used to acquire it. “Wike was clear. He said Bode George’s Abuja house was acquired with funds from Rivers State, and he stands by this. Bode George said he bought the property from a private owner through an agent. That is not the issue. Wike’s statement was never about who the property was purchased from or through. Rather, what he said was that the money with which the property was acquired came from Rivers State, and this is the question Bode George must answer,” Olayinka said. The presidential aide’s statement was a response to recent media appearances by the former military governor whom he accused of lacking the moral standing to lecture Nigerians on corruption. Olayinka told Chief George to borrow some maturity from those he served with as Military Governor of the old Ondo State 38 years ago, urging him to rest rather than continue what he called an embarrassment to himself and the Yoruba race. “For someone who was Military Governor of the old Ondo State in 1988 (38 years ago), some level of decorum and maturity is expected. But it is becoming an embarrassment the way a man like Chief Bode George, who should be acting like an elder statesman, is jumping from one television station to the other to malign people who are young enough to be his children,” he said. He also challenged Bode George to account for the PDP’s poor political fortunes in Lagos State under his leadership, noting that the party had failed to win a single polling unit in the state since 1999. “Since 1999, he has not won his polling unit for the PDP. Unlike Lagos State, we have had PDP governors in Ogun, Ondo, Ekiti, Oyo and Osun States. Methinks rather than doing ‘cho cho cho’ all the time, Bode George needs to tell Nigerians why PDP has remained at the sideline in the politics of Lagos State since 1999,” Olayinka said. Citing Yoruba tradition, Olayinka argued that respect for elders was not automatic but conditional on the elder avoiding self-disrespect, and accused Bode George of failing to honour a string of public vows to leave Nigeria should President Bola Tinubu ascend to power. “In Yorubaland, it is a strict cultural and traditional rule to respect elders. However, this respect is not automatic, it is conditional and the major condition is that an elder must avoid disrespecting himself,” he said. He listed several occasions between 2015 and 2022 on which Bode George pledged to renounce his Nigerian citizenship or relocate abroad if Tinubu became president, including a March 2022 press briefing where he was quoted as saying he would “go to Ghana and be watching with binoculars from afar.” Olayinka said; “In 2015, ahead of the presidential election, Bode George promised to go on exile if APC emerged victorious in the presidential election. “In February 2020, he said he will disown Nigeria to take the citizenship of Togo or any other country if Tinubu is elected president. “On May 7, 2021, on Arise News, Bode George echoed his stand that he will cease to be a Nigerian should Tinubu get the presidency. “Also in 2021, while featuring on Arise News, Bode George said he will review and renounce his citizenship of Nigeria if Tinubu becomes president. “In January 2022, after Tinubu had announced his bid to contest for president, Bode George said he will move away from Nigeria. “At a press briefing on March 19, 2022, Bode George further reiterated that his promise to leave Nigeria if Tinubu emerged president was no joke. “He said then that ‘If by whatever chance he (Tinubu) gets to the villa, I won’t be part of this country. And I am not joking. I can go to Ghana and be watching with binoculars from afar.’ “Now, it is more than three years of Tinubu as President and he (Bode George) has failed to honour his own words. Should such an elder still be regarded as honourable?” The post Bode George’s Abuja house funded by Rivers money, Wike’s aide insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Troops foil bandit attack, prevent livestock rustling in Sokoto community
items.description: Troops of the 8 Division Garrison of the Nigerian Army have foiled a terrorist attack and chased away a gang of bandits attempting to rustle livestock in Asarara village in Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State. A credible security source from the area disclosed this to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Thursday in Sokoto. The source said the incident occurred on Wednesday when a gang of bandits attacked the community in an attempt to kidnap residents and rustle animals. “The gallant troops engaged the bandits in a fierce exchange of fire, which forced them to retreat in disarray, while some of the bandits escaped with gunshot wounds. “The quick response of the troops and continued vigilance saved the lives and property of villagers,” the source said. The source, who pleaded anonymity, said he had no authority to speak to the press, and added that the bandits had been pushed back to the Gwangi community along the riverside in the area. The credible source appreciated the cooperation of residents for sharing prompt information and urged them to sustain the effort. “Proactive measures have been put in place to protect lives and property. “The swift response, professionalism, and courage displayed by military personnel averted what could have been a tragic incident,” the source said. The source appealed for continued support from residents, while stressing the need for more vigilance in farming communities. items.title: Vassili Nebenzia : «Le régime de Kiev est impliqué dans des activités terroristes en Afrique»
items.description: Le representant permanent de la Russie aupres de l'Organisation des Nations unies (ONU), Vassili Nebenzia, a denonce l'implication de l'Ukraine dans des activites terroristes sur le continent africain, lors d'une reunion du Conseil de securite de l'ONU, le 5 août. Selon lui, cette implication concerne notamment « la livraison de drones et la formation directe de terroristes par des instructeurs militaires ukrainiens ». Il a estime que cette question devait faire l'objet d'une attention particuliere compte tenu de la situation securitaire dans plusieurs pays africains. Vassili Nebenzia a egalement declare que des armes occidentales livrees a l'Ukraine avaient ete retrouvees entre les mains de groupes armes, non seulement en Afrique, mais aussi en Amerique latine et au Moyen-Orient. Il a ajoute que des organismes de controle americains s'interrogeaient sur l'utilisation de l'aide militaire accordee a Kiev sous l'administration de Joe Biden. Le role des pays occidentaux mis en cause Au-dela des activites attribuees a Kiev, Vassili Nebenzia a egalement mis en cause le role des pays occidentaux, qui, selon lui, utiliseraient l'Ukraine pour defendre leurs interets sur le continent africain, en particulier dans la region du Sahel . Le diplomate a affirme que le soutien par apport des Ukrainiens a des groupes terroristes servirait des objectifs geopolitiques plus larges. Moscou considere ainsi que l'implication ukrainienne en Afrique ne peut etre separee de la politique menee par les allies occidentaux de Kiev. Ces accusations rejoignent plusieurs declarations formulees recemment par de hauts responsables russes. Le directeur du departement Afrique du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Anatoli Bachkine, avait notamment declare le 20 juillet que des specialistes ukrainiens participaient a la planification d'operations menees par des groupes terroristes en Afrique. Le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Sergueï Lavrov, ainsi que d'autres responsables de Moscou, ont egalement affirme que des combattants et des instructeurs ukrainiens etaient presents dans plusieurs pays du continent. Le Mali au centre des accusations Le Mali figure parmi les pays les plus directement concernes par ces declarations. Selon un article publie par le media russe Gazeta le 5 août 2026, un pilote de l'Africa Corps des forces russes a affirme que des operateurs ukrainiens de drones FPV participaient aux combats aux cotes de groupes armes dans le pays. Le militaire a indique que cette presence avait ete etablie grâce a des interceptions radio et aux temoignages de combattants captures. Ces elements viennent renforcer les accusations formulees par Moscou au sujet des activites de Kiev dans la region du Sahel. Pour les autorites russes, l'ensemble de ces informations temoigne d'une implication croissante de l'Ukraine aupres des groupes armes en Afrique. Elles soulevent egalement la question du controle des armes occidentales fournies a Kiev et de leur circulation vers d'autres zones de conflit.

items.title: Drainage des eaux pluviales à Nagrin : Le Secrétaire général du Ministère de la construction de la patrie évalue la situation sur le terrain
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 5 août 2026 )- Suite aux fortes précipitations survenues dans la nuit du 2 au 3 août 2026, ayant provoqué d'importantes accumulations d'eau et des inondations dans le quartier Nagrin, le secrétaire général du ministère de la construction de la patrie, le commandant Ollo PALENFO a effectué dans la matinée une visite d'inspection sur les lieux. Accompagné par la présidente de la délégation spéciale de l'arrondissement 7, camarade Marie Blanche YOUGBARÉ et des techniciens du ministère, le secrétaire général s'est rendu dans les zones les plus touchées du quartier. La délégation a pu observer les points critiques où le ruissellement des eaux s'est heurté à des obstacles majeurs, provoquant la submersion de plusieurs concessions et voies d'accès. A l'occasion, le commandant Palenfo s'est entretenu avec les riverains. » Nous sommes conscients des problèmes qu'il y'a dans la zone. C'est ce qui explique la présence des bornes balises qui deliminitent la zone inondable. Nous avons travaillé à résoudre en partie le problème et des solutions plus holistiques viendront après le compte-rendu fait à l'autorité ». Il a tout de même attiré leur attention sur certaines infrastructures qu'ils ont réalisées sur le lit du cours d'eau avant de leur souligner que l'objectif première de la réalisation de cette route est de résoudre d'abord le problème de mobilité des populations. Pour la PDS de l'arrondissement 7, ce n'est pas la voirie qui a causé le problème d'inondation dans la zone. Elle a plutôt résolu un temps soit peu les problèmes liés aux inondations au sein de l'arrondissement, d'où un appel lancé à la population à faire preuve de compréhension et à faire confiance aux plus hautes autorités pour solutionner le problème. items.title: Tinubu will deliver Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway – Umahi
items.description: The Minister of Works, Engr David Umahi, says President Bola Tinubu will deliver the 700-kilometer Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as scheduled. Umahi gave the assurance late Wednesday while inspecting the level of work at the Ondo section of the coastal highway in Ilaje Local Government Area of the state. The minister, who faulted several criticisms regarding the construction of the highway, said those criticising the project were “motivated by envy because they never believed the President could deliver it.” According to him, section one has already been completed, which is 7.47km from Victoria Island to Elepe village, while section two, about 50km stretching from Lagos to the Ogun border, is about 70 per cent completed. Umahi added that sections 3A and 3B, covering about 67 kilometres, are progressing, with approximately 30 per cent completed. The minister stated that section 4 covers about 82 kilometres, extending through Ogun into Ondo State, saying that the President was determined to ensure its completion. He explained that section 5, which is about 180 kilometres in Akwa Ibom, is likely the longest section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and work is ongoing there. “We have another 100-kilometre section beginning at the end of the Ondo section, which is currently at the design stage. What will remain afterwards are the sections through Rivers, Bayelsa and Delta States. “I also want to respond to some of the comments made by one of those who worked with the President when he was governor. I watched the interview of His Excellency Donald Duke. “He is a very brilliant man. What impressed me most was that he avoided insults. He was a perfect gentleman, and I am proud of him. “However, some of the issues he raised require clarification. When he said the Coastal Highway would never go beyond Epe, I respectfully disagree. “He also said the project was not a priority. Yet, this Coastal Highway was conceived years ago, but it could not be implemented because of funding constraints and other challenges. “Those attacking the Coastal Highway are, in my view, motivated by envy because they never believed this President could deliver it. “The man who tamed the Atlantic Ocean is capable of delivering this project. I call him a divine President,” he said. The minister urged stakeholders and leaders to continue to watch President Tinubu’s administration deliver the Coastal Highway. “I also saw where the secretary of Afenifere was accusing the Ministry of Works of diverting the Coastal Highway. Of note was when he said it was diverted upland because of people who own estates there; that is far from the truth. “The Coastal Highway was originally planned to follow the coastline because that was our preference. However, engineering is very dynamic. “When we designed this section of the Coastal Highway, it was intended to pass about two kilometres from the shoreline, but then the soil tests, which form the basis of engineering design, revealed a major challenge. “Along that route, we encountered very poor soil known in engineering as peat, extending more than 40 to 50 metres deep. “We encountered peat in Sections 1 and 2 within Lagos, but fortunately it was only about 20 metres deep there, making it manageable. “It is extremely difficult to manage peat deposits that are 50 metres deep because they have to be removed and replaced before construction can proceed. We also discovered that the sand we expected from the sea was not suitable,” he stated. Umahi praised the construction company for what he described as “diligent work” that was also impacting the community, with confidence in delivering a good job. The post Tinubu will deliver Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway – Umahi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPP demonstration meant to mar one-year helicopter crash anniversary – Solomon Owusu
items.description: The Director of Communications for the United Party, Solomon Owusu, has criticised the opposition New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) nationwide demonstration, alleging that the protest was deliberately organised to overshadow the first anniversary of a tragic incident that claimed the lives of 8 gallant men. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Thursday, 6 August, Mr Owusu argued that the NPP had “no business whatsoever” taking to the streets, insisting that the demonstration, themed “Democracy Under Attack,” was politically motivated rather than driven by genuine concerns over Ghana’s democratic governance. His remarks come as the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) stages nationwide protests under the theme “Democracy Under Attack,” arguing that recent developments threaten Ghana’s democratic governance. Rejecting the party’s justification for the demonstration, Mr Owusu questioned the basis of the NPP’s claims. “They have no business whatsoever being on the street. I say it from the heart of my heart. I think they decided to do this demonstration just to mar the one-year anniversary of our departed souls. That is all they are talking about,” he said. Mr Owusu dismissed assertions that individuals had been arrested merely for speaking their minds, arguing that the claims did not reflect the realities of the country’s democratic environment. “What did we see? That people have been arrested for speaking? Is that the truth? Is that the case? Is that what you believe in?” he questioned. He further pointed to demonstrations organised by the NPP while it was in government, arguing that the party had previously exercised its constitutional right to protest without interference. According to him, the party organised major demonstrations, including Save the Judiciary and another under the slogan ‘Yɛn Suro Ahunahuna’ (“We Are Not Afraid of Intimidation”), during which its members publicly declared that they feared no one. “They themselves told Ghanaians they were not afraid of anybody, and they embarked on demonstrations to show the whole world that they would not be intimidated,” he stated. Mr Owusu also accused the NPP of hypocrisy over concerns about political insults and intolerance, arguing that the party has historically engaged in some of the harshest political rhetoric in Ghana. Drawing on his experience as a former member of the NPP, he claimed the party had a long record of using derogatory language against political opponents. “Fortunately, I have been a member of the NPP before. There has not been any political party that has insulted more than the NPP, and it started long ago,” he said. He cited instances involving the late former President Jerry John Rawlings and John Evans Atta Mills, recalling that political figures associated with the NPP had previously used disparaging language against their opponents. Mr Owusu specifically referred to comments made in 2002 by Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko, who allegedly described Professor Mills as a “poodle” following the 2000 general election. “As recent as 2002, Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko referred to Professor Mills as a poodle. So what exactly are we discussing here?” he asked. Addressing the NPP’s concerns over the reported arrest of 21 individuals, Mr Owusu argued that the party had overlooked similar incidents during its own tenure in office. He referenced the 2024 Democracy Hub #OccupyJulorBiHouse protests, during which dozens of demonstrators were arrested, contending that the current criticism lacked consistency. “So, for this reason, they have no business whatsoever being on the streets,” he said. According to the NPP, the demonstration is intended to draw attention to issues including alleged restrictions on free expression, concerns over the treatment of opposition voices, and what it describes as threats to democratic institutions.

items.title: CAN féminine 2026 : le Mali et le Ghana se disputent le dernier billet des quarts
items.description: La phase de groupes de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine 2026 s'achève ce jeudi avec les deux dernières rencontres du groupe D. Si le Cameroun a déjà assuré sa qualification pour les quarts de finale, le Mali et le Ghana s'affronteront dans un duel décisif pour décrocher le dernier ticket. Les Maliennes et les Ghanéennes abordent cette rencontre avec le même bilan de trois points. Battu par le Cameroun après une victoire difficile contre le Cap-Vert, le Ghana n'a plus le droit à l'erreur. De son côté, le Mali, défait lors de son entrée en lice, s'est relancé grâce à un succès face au Cap-Vert et peut encore croire à une qualification. Cette confrontation s'annonce donc déterminante, les deux sélections devant s'imposer pour éviter de dépendre des autres critères de qualification. Dans l'autre match du groupe, le Cameroun, déjà qualifié et leader de la poule, affrontera le Cap-Vert. Les Lionnes Indomptables tenteront de conclure la phase de groupes par un troisième résultat positif afin de conserver leur dynamique avant les quarts de finale. Le Cap-Vert, déjà éliminé malgré des prestations encourageantes, cherchera quant à lui à quitter la compétition sur une bonne note en décrochant son premier point. Les deux rencontres débuteront simultanément à 21 heures, clôturant ainsi la phase de groupes de cette CAN féminine 2026. The post CAN féminine 2026 : le Mali et le Ghana se disputent le dernier billet des quarts appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: President Mahama concludes Jamaica visit with Seville Heritage Park tour
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama last Tuesday brought his four-day state visit to Jamaica to a close with a visit to Seville Heritage Park in St. Ann, where he toured the preserved Ghanaian Village Houses. The visit formed part of the President’s official engagements and highlighted the historical and cultural connections between Ghana and Jamaica. It also served to reaffirm Ghana’s commitment to strengthening relations with Caribbean nations in the areas of culture, trade, investment and diplomacy. Reception At the heritage park, President Mahama laid a wreath in honour of Africans who were transported across the Atlantic during the transatlantic slave trade. A Great House Reception was later held in his honour, and was attended by Jamaican government officials, cultural leaders, diplomats and members of the Ghanaian delegation. The President also toured the Great House, which was constructed in 1745 by the grandson of Captain Richard Hemmings. Captain Hemmings had participated in the English conquest of Jamaica in 1655 alongside Admiral William Penn and General Robert Venables before establishing the Seville Estate on approximately 2,500 acres of land. The Great House was originally designed as a fortified two-storey residence without a veranda. It overlooked the sugar plantations, sugar works, the village of enslaved Africans and the Caribbean coastline. Defensive guns were positioned around the building to protect the plantation owner and his household. Following hurricane damage after 1745, the upper floor was removed and a veranda was added to improve ventilation and provide shade. Several architectural features, including decorative architraves surrounding the doorways, have been preserved. The property was declared a National Monument by the Jamaica National Heritage Trust on May 13, 1999. Future cooperation Addressing guests at the Great House Reception, President Mahama said Ghana and Jamaica shared common ancestry, history and cultural traditions. He stated that both countries should focus on building a prosperous future through economic cooperation, tourism, education, investment and people-to-people exchanges. The President reiterated his call for the establishment of a direct air link between Ghana and Jamaica, stating that improved connectivity would enhance tourism, trade, business, academic collaboration and cultural exchange between West Africa and the Caribbean. One family Jamaica’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, Senator Kamina Johnson Smith, said Ghana and Jamaica were one family connected by shared ancestry and history. She emphasised the need to deepen cooperation and translate historical ties into stronger diplomatic and economic partnerships. Jamaica’s Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, Olivia “Babsy” Grange, expressed gratitude to President Mahama and the people of Ghana for the support extended to Jamaica following Hurricane Melissa. She called for greater collaboration in tourism and cultural development to drive economic growth. Later in the day, President Mahama attended a State Dinner hosted by the Governor-General of Jamaica, Sir Patrick Allen, and Lady Allen at the Ballroom of King’s House. The dinner marked the official conclusion of the President’s state visit.

items.title: 11 ans sans victoire : Gris Bordeaux obligé de stopper l’hémorragie face à Boy Diop 2
items.description: Gris Bordeaux (Fass) n’a plus goûté aux délices de la victoire depuis son succès face à Tyson (Ecurie Boul Faalé) en 2015. Voilà désormais onze ans que le 3ᵉ « Tigre » de Fass traverse une longue disette. Il est donc contraint de renouer avec le succès lors de son combat contre Boy Diop 2 (Yeumbeul Marin). Il est extrêmement rare de voir un grand champion de lutte rester onze années sans enregistrer la moindre victoire. C’est pourtant la situation dans laquelle se trouve Gris Bordeaux. Depuis son succès contre Tyson, le 3 mai 2015, le 3ᵉ « Tigre » de Fass traverse une interminable traversée du désert. Cette victoire s’expliquait notamment par sa meilleure condition physique, sa fraîcheur et une préparation plus aboutie que celle de son adversaire. Mais après ce brillant succès face à l’ancien chef de file de l’écurie Boul Faalé, le protégé de Moustapha Guèye est entré dans une spirale de revers. Cette série noire débute le 31 juillet 2016 avec une lourde défaite contre Modou Lô. A lire aussi : Gris Bordeaux: « Je souhaite terminer ma carrière en beauté » Dans l’espoir de se relancer, il est ensuite opposé à Balla Gaye 2, lui-même en quête de renaissance après avoir perdu sa couronne de « Roi des arènes » face à Bombardier en 2014, puis essuyé un autre revers contre Eumeu Sène en 2015. Le 31 mars 2018, Gris Bordeaux s’incline une nouvelle fois. Quatre ans plus tard, le 7 août 2022, il retrouve le « Lion de Guédiawaye » pour une revanche, mais subit encore la loi de son rival. Cette longue descente aux enfers se poursuit avec deux autres défaites, face à Ama Baldé, le 30 juin 2024, puis contre Zarco, le 12 janvier 2025. Le voilà désormais avec un bilan inquiétant : cinq revers consécutifs et onze années, sans victoire. La saison 2026-2027 apparaît donc comme celle de la dernière chance. Devant être opposé à Boy Diop 2, Gris Bordeaux n’a plus droit à l’erreur. Sur le papier, son futur adversaire ne possède ni l’expérience des grands rendez-vous ni le vécu du leader de Fass. Ce dernier conserve également un avantage en matière de gabarit et d’expérience au plus haut niveau. Mais ces atouts ne suffiront pas s’ils ne sont pas accompagnés d’une prestation à la hauteur de son statut. Gris Bordeaux devra imposer son style, exploiter toute son expérience et retrouver l’efficacité qui a longtemps fait sa réputation. Une nouvelle contre-performance plongerait davantage encore le mentor de Lac Rose dans une crise sportive sans précédent. Onze années sans victoire constituent un chiffre qui interpelle pour un lutteur de son calibre. Dans un sport où les résultats dictent la hiérarchie, une telle disette nourrit inévitablement les interrogations sur la fin de carrière du Fassois. Le combat contre Boy Diop 2 représente donc bien plus qu’un simple rendez-vous. Il s’agira, en effet, d’une occasion de mettre fin à une période de disette. Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: The August 6 tragedy and Ghana’s Galamsey fight: Any lessons learnt?
items.description: It was meant to be another chapter in Ghana’s war against galamsey. Instead, August 6, 2025, became one of the darkest days in the nation’s recent history. Eight of the country’s citizens, including senior government officials, the Defence and Environment ministers, tragically lost their lives in a helicopter crash when they were travelling to an event in Obuasi aimed at confronting illegal mining. One year after the tragic incident, what lessons has the country learnt in the quest to mitigate against illegal mining that continues to ravage natural resources? Their death shook the core of the nation. A routine mission ended in unimaginable loss. For weeks, the country brooded over the sudden demise of eight of its gallant citizens, including cabinet ministers. A helicopter carrying men committed to national duty never completed its journey. The defence minister, Dr Edward Omane Boamah, the environment minister, Murtala Mohammed, three other top government officials and three crew members never returned. The painful demise left behind grieving families, shattered dreams, and a nation searching for meaning in tragedy. Time has moved on. The pain has not. For many Ghanaians, the echoes of that tragic day still linger. The memory of those who perished continues to inspire solemn reflection on the national fight against illegal mining. The Departed 8 were on a national assignment in a renewed fight to eradicate illegal mining through the Responsible Community Mining and Skills Development Programme. The Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme (RCOMSDEP) is a national initiative that empowers mining cooperatives and small-scale miners through training, innovation, and responsible practices. The goal is to transform mining into a force for safe, inclusive, and environmentally responsible development. But a year after its launch, has the country won the Galamsey war at all? Convener for the Coalition of anti-Galamsey campaigners, Ken Ashigbey, is distraught that the blood of these individuals has not been avenged. “Dr Omane Boamah, and what I know that he stood for and the support he gave to the lands minister, unfortunately we have failed them. The best tribute to have given them was to make their blood count,” he said. While the government touts its achievements in the Galamsey fight, many rivers snaking through the country remain dirty and forest reserves dotted with open pits. Across Ghana, in the Western, Western North, Ashanti, Central, Eastern Bono and Ahafo regions, illegal mining is eating life away from the lands, water bodies and other natural resources. Illegal miners continue to operate with impunity – excavating the earth crust close to roads and in forest covers while local authorities watch on. A recent video which surfaced on social media showed some youth in one of the coastal communities fetching and washing sand along the beach in search of gold. An aerial view of the country’s water bodies reveals major rivers, once crystal clear, suffocating with heavy siltation and discoloured effluent from the mining activities. Aquatic life and biodiversity are at the mercy of humans’ unrelenting quest for wealth. “We have to honour their memory by doing what is right for our fight against illegal,” environmental journalist Erastus Asare Donkor noted. But perhaps the greatest tribute to these eight gallant souls will not be found in wreaths, monuments, or anniversary ceremonies. It will be found in rivers that run clear again… in forests that breathe once more… and in a nation that finally finds the resolve to protect the land that sustains us all. Their mission ended in the skies above Adansi. But the journey they began remains firmly on the ground—unfinished, and now entrusted to every Ghanaian. Until the scars of galamsey fade from our rivers and our forests, August 6 will remain more than a day of mourning. It will stand as a solemn reminder that the price of inaction can be painfully high. Rest in power, our fallen heroes. Damirifa due… Mmarima mma.

items.title: EFCC can freeze accounts for 72 hrs without court order – Spokesman
items.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has insisted that its temporary restriction on an Osun State Government bank account was lawful and backed by provisions of the EFCC Act and the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act. Speaking on Arise Television on Thursday, EFCC spokesperson and Director of Public Affairs, Wilson Uwujaren, rejected claims by the Osun State Government and the Nigerian Bar Association that the commission required a court order before placing the restriction. According to him, the decision followed what the agency described as suspicious transactions on the account over the past week. “As we indicated in the statement released by the Commission, we took that step to preserve the account of the Osun State Government. “We observed in the past one week that activities on that account looked suspicious, and based on the mandate of the Commission, we took the step of placing a restriction on that account to preserve it,” he said. Uwujaren clarified that the action affected only one account and did not amount to a freeze on all Osun State accounts. “That restriction order does not mean that all the accounts of Osun State have been frozen. No. It is just a targeted restriction on one account of the Osun State Government,” he said. He explained that the commission noticed multiple transfers from the account to several corporate entities within a short period, prompting the intervention. “The essence, like I said, is just to preserve that account because we observed suspicious activities on that account in terms of the transfer of funds to a number of entities within one week. “So we had to take that decision to place a restriction on that account, not minding the fact that there is an election process in place,” he said. The EFCC spokesman argued that the agency would have been criticised if it had failed to act while public funds were allegedly being moved. “We have the responsibility under the law to do so because if we don’t take that step and, for instance, funds are looted from the account of the Osun State Government, I’m sure the Nigerian public will also ask, ‘Where was the EFCC when those funds were being moved?’” he said. Uwujaren maintained that the state government still had access to other accounts and could continue to carry out its operations, including salary payments. “It does not stop the Osun State Government from running the government of the state because they have access to other funds in the other accounts that they have. “In any case, the payment of salaries and other expenditures by the state government happens just once in a month. What we have done is not a blanket freezing of the account. “It’s just a targeted freezing. Once we are satisfied that activities on that account are no longer suspicious, it will be lifted,” he said. On the legal basis for the restriction, he pointed to specific statutory provisions empowering the commission to temporarily restrict access to an account. “A number of people have asked whether the Commission has the power to do so under the law. I can assure you that we have the power to place a temporary restriction on an account. “Section 34 of the EFCC Act and Section 7, Subsection 6 of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act 2022 give us that authority to take that step,” he said. He added that the restriction could remain in place for up to 72 hours before the commission would need to seek judicial backing if it wished to extend it. “The restriction order can last within 72 hours before we can come with a court order if we need to provide a court order,” he said. The EFCC had earlier announced that it had been investigating the Osun State Government since March 2026 over the alleged fraudulent management of about N11bn in Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and Federation Account Allocation Committee allocations. The commission said some officials, including the Accountant General, had already been questioned. The post EFCC can freeze accounts for 72 hrs without court order – Spokesman appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‎Police intercept 866 parcels of suspected cocaine hidden in bags of gari, 3 suspects in custody
items.description: ‎The Police in Tema have intercepted 866 parcels of a white powdered substance suspected to be cocaine. They were concealed in sacks of gari. The seizure followed an intelligence-led operation conducted by the Police at about 8 pm on Wednesday, August 5, 2026. ‎Three suspects, including a Dutch national and two Ghanaians, have been arrested in connection with the consignment.‎ Sources close to the operation told Graphic Online’s Benjamin Xornam Glover that the suspects were picked up while supervising a group of men loading sacks of gari and ‘konkonte’ into a 40-foot container for export at a warehouse within the Tema Port enclave. ‎The suspects, together with the truck and the intercepted parcels, are currently in police custody for further investigations.

items.title: Accident de bus de Constantine : le bilan s’alourdit
items.description: Nouvelle tragédie sur les routes algériennes. Six personnes ont perdu la vie et 19 autres ont été blessées dans un nouvel accident d’autobus à Constantine ce jeudi 6 août peu après 05 h 00 du matin, selon un nouveau bilan provisoire de la Protection civile. Un précédent bilan faisait état de trois morts et 19 blessés. Le drame s’est produit sur la RN 79 à Ben Ziad entre Constantine et Mila quand un bus a dérapé et a fini sa course dans un ravin peu profond. Cet accident, dont les raisons n’ont pas été précisées, survient moins d’une semaine après deux drames routiers impliquant des autocars. Accidents de bus en Algérie : un bilan très lourd Le premier a eu lieu à Boumerdès vendredi 31 juillet quand un bus a sauté dans un ravin, faisant 28 morts et 41 blessés. Le second s’est produit à Timimoun samedi 1ᵉʳ août et a fait 4 morts et 43 blessés. En moins d’une semaine, 38 personnes ont perdu la vie et 103 autres ont été blessées dans trois accidents de bus survenus à Boumerdès, Timimoun et Constantine. Malgré le durcissement des sanctions contre les chauffards dans le nouveau code de la route, le terrorisme routier continue d’endeuiller les familles algériennes. L’article Accident de bus de Constantine : le bilan s’alourdit est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Protection de l’enfance : Le manuel sur les pratiques endogènes de protection de l’enfance validé à Wahala
items.description: Notsè, 5 août (ATOP) – Les acteurs communautaires et les personnes ressources de la commune Haho 4 ont validé le manuel sur les pratiques et mécanismes endogènes de protection de l’enfance, le mardi 4 août à Wahala. L’initiative est portée par le Collectif des centres de développement des enfants et des jeunes (CDEJ) de Haho-nord, en partenariat avec l’ONG Compassion International Togo. Elle s’inscrit dans une dynamique de valorisation des pratiques positives des communautés en matière de protection de l’enfance. Le projet vise également à renforcer le dialogue familial, l’accompagnement scolaire des enfants et des jeunes, la solidarité communautaire ainsi que la collaboration entre les communautés, les services techniques de l’État et les collectivités territoriales. Composé de 32 pages, le manuel présente les concepts liés aux pratiques et mécanismes endogènes de protection de l’enfance, les objectifs de l’approche endogène ainsi que les principales pratiques traditionnelles favorisant la protection des enfants. Il met notamment en avant les légendes, les proverbes, les dialogues et conseils, les écoles d’apprentissage, les prières de protection ainsi que le rôle des chefs traditionnels et des leaders communautaires dans la prévention des risques. Le document explique également l’importance de préserver ces pratiques, propose des stratégies pour leur valorisation et décrit le fonctionnement des comités villageois de protection de l’enfant. Il est enrichi d’illustrations mettant en évidence les différents mécanismes endogènes de protection. Le pasteur Alpha Augustin Tchaa, du CDEJ Essowéréou, a souligné que ce manuel constitue un outil de référence pour renforcer la participation des familles, des chefs traditionnels, des leaders religieux, des enseignants et des communautés à la protection des enfants. Il a invité les participants à promouvoir les valeurs d’écoute, de respect et de solidarité. La responsable du Centre social de Wahala, Mme Kola Hadalo, a appelé les acteurs communautaires et les personnes ressources à préserver les pratiques positives afin de garantir un environnement protecteur et favorable au développement intégral des enfants. Elle a rappelé l’engagement du gouvernement en faveur du bien-être des enfants et de la protection de leurs droits. La cérémonie a été marquée par des prestations artistiques de jeunes mettant en valeur les pratiques et mécanismes endogènes de protection de l’enfance. ATOP/YM/AO/KYA

items.title: US has ‘massive amounts’ – Trump dismisses reports of munitions shortages
items.description: President Donald Trump said on Thursday the United States has a vast supply of munitions and threatened those who suggested otherwise with jail terms as his frustration with the Iran war boiled over. The Republican leader lashed out on his Truth Social platform at media reports about the dwindling weapons stockpile, saying that the United States has “massive amounts of ‘munitions’ especially of certain types,” without giving further detail. “Additionally, large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed. Defense companies are building the largest number of plants and factories in our country’s history,” he said. The Washington Post reported that Trump demanded answers about the munitions shortages from Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth last Friday, when they attended a cabinet meeting at the Camp David presidential retreat. Trump told Hegseth that he thought the munitions issue “had been fixed,” the Post reported, citing two unidentified sources familiar with the exchange. Trump railed against the media reports, threatening on Thursday that “the ‘leakers’ of these treasonous statements are being hunted down” and “Long term jail sentences will be sought!” CNN also reported that shortages of long-range guided missiles and air-defense interceptors had affected Trump’s strategy in the conflict with Iran, with the US military having “nearly exhausted 80%” of its stock of THAAD interceptors. The Post also said that the shortages led Trump to call off fresh strikes against Iran, despite having threatened to hit the Islamic republic “very hard”. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt branded coverage of the exchange with Hegseth “FAKE NEWS!” “I was at Camp David with President Trump and Secretary Hegseth. This literally never happened,” she wrote on X. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the reports about Trump’s clash with Hegseth and the weapons shortages were “equally fictional.” Iran’s foreign ministry has denied there are any negotiations underway with Washington, even as Trump said Tehran was keen for a deal. AFP The post US has ‘massive amounts’ – Trump dismisses reports of munitions shortages appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Samsung dévoile une mémoire 3D destinée aux futurs accélérateurs d’IA
items.description: À la conférence FMS 2026, Samsung a présenté les concepts zHBM et zNAND-O ainsi qu’une mémoire NAND de plus de 400 couches. Les performances annoncées restent des objectifs de feuille de route, mais elles illustrent la bataille pour rapprocher mémoire et processeurs afin de réduire les transferts de données et la consommation électrique. Samsung Electronics a profité de la conférence Future of Memory and Storage, en Californie, pour montrer sa prochaine génération de composants destinés aux systèmes d’intelligence artificielle. Le fabricant sud-coréen a présenté environ trente technologies de mémoire et de stockage, avec deux concepts au centre de sa démonstration : zHBM pour les accélérateurs d’IA et zNAND-O pour les traitements rapides au plus près des utilisateurs. La mémoire à haute bande passante, ou HBM, est aujourd’hui placée à côté des processeurs graphiques et autres accélérateurs. Le concept zHBM prévoit de l’empiler verticalement directement au-dessus du processeur. En raccourcissant le trajet des données, Samsung vise une bande passante plus élevée et une meilleure efficacité énergétique pour l’entraînement et l’exécution de grands modèles. L’entreprise avance des écarts spectaculaires : une interface zHBM pourrait atteindre environ huit fois les performances de HBM5, plus de dix fois sa densité, trois fois son efficacité énergétique et une résistance thermique réduite de plus de moitié. Il s’agit d’estimations de conception communiquées par Samsung, sans produit commercial, date de disponibilité, prix ni test indépendant publiés pour ce concept. Le groupe a également dévoilé zNAND-O, développé en versions de quatre et huit couches pour les usages d’IA en périphérie, lorsque les données doivent être traitées rapidement dans un appareil ou un site local. Sa V10 BV-NAND franchit pour sa part le seuil de 400 couches. Samsung affirme que le collage de tranches augmente la densité d’environ 58 % par rapport à la génération V9, avec des gains attendus en lecture, écriture et consommation. Cette feuille de route accompagne des produits plus proches du marché, notamment HBM4E, HBM5, la mémoire LPDDR5X-PIM capable d’effectuer certains calculs en interne, et des SSD d’entreprise. Le mouvement répond à une contrainte centrale des centres de données d’IA : déplacer sans cesse de grandes quantités d’informations entre stockage, mémoire et processeurs ralentit les calculs et augmente la facture énergétique. Le rapprochement physique de la mémoire et du calcul pose aussi des difficultés. L’empilement accroît la densité de chaleur dans un espace réduit, exige des techniques de collage très précises et rend la réparation des composants plus complexe. Le rendement industriel, la compatibilité avec les architectures des fabricants d’accélérateurs et le coût du conditionnement pèseront donc autant que la vitesse théorique. Les chiffres présentés à FMS décrivent la direction technique choisie par Samsung, pas les performances d’un serveur disponible à l’achat. Leur portée dépendra de la fabrication à grande échelle, du refroidissement, de l’intégration avec les accélérateurs et des validations réalisées par les clients. Les prochains jalons commerciaux permettront de mesurer l’écart entre le prototype et les systèmes effectivement déployés. Cet article vous est proposé en collaboration avec Aïobi . Contact : team@aiobi.world . L’article Samsung dévoile une mémoire 3D destinée aux futurs accélérateurs d’IA est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: NCoS launches probe after inmate’s viral TikTok live stream in Ogun
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Nigerian Correctional Service NCoS has removed the Officer-in-Charge of the Ibara Medium Custodial Centre, Abeokuta, Ogun State, along with two other principal officers, pending investigations into the unauthorised use of a mobile phone by a death row inmate who went live on TikTok from custody. The Service, in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, CSC Jane Osuji, said the Controller General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, ordered the removal of the affected officers to ensure a transparent and impartial investigative process. The statement said the Service had noted with grave concern the media reports and public reactions trailing the viral live stream, describing the incident as a serious breach of custodial security and a violation of the Nigerian Correctional Service Act, 2019, the Service Standing Orders and other extant regulations governing custodial operations. According to the statement, preliminary findings confirmed that the inmate was in unlawful possession of a prohibited mobile phone, which he used to access social media while in lawful custody. “Preliminary findings confirmed that the inmate was in unlawful possession of a prohibited mobile phone, which he used to access social media while in lawful custody,” the statement read. The Service said the phone has since been recovered following a search operation and secured as an exhibit for further investigation, while the inmate has been transferred to another facility where he is being held under enhanced security pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations. It added that the probe had also identified security gaps that may have contributed to the breach. Osuji said the removal of the officers was without prejudice to the final outcome of the investigation and was intended to demonstrate the Service’s commitment to accountability and institutional integrity. The Service used the opportunity to highlight ongoing security reforms embarked upon by the Controller General since his assumption of office, aimed at eliminating security vulnerabilities and preventing the introduction of prohibited items into custodial centres, noting that the incident had reinforced the need for their full implementation. “The preliminary findings from this incident has further reinforced the need for these reforms and has directed their full implementation and intensified compliance across all Commands and Custodial Centres,” the statement said. While the inmate’s culpability has been established, the NCoS said investigations were ongoing into the possible involvement, negligence or complicity of any officer, inmate or external collaborator connected to the breach. “The Service wishes to assure Nigerians that anyone found to have facilitated, aided, condoned or failed in their responsibilities in connection with this incident will face appropriate disciplinary and administrative sanctions in accordance with extant regulations,” the statement said. The Service commended the vigilance of members of the public and the media in bringing the matter to national attention, while appealing against speculation as investigations continue. “The Service appeals against speculation while investigations continue and assures Nigerians that it remains resolute in its constitutional mandate of ensuring the safe, secure and humane custody of all persons legally committed into its care through continuous reforms, professionalism and accountability,” the statement said. The post NCoS launches probe after inmate’s viral TikTok live stream in Ogun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Commune de Mont-Rolland : Mame Astou Mbaye, le combat pour l’eau à Sambaye Karang
items.description: Soutien de famille et technicienne agricole sans emploi, Mame Astou Mbaye mène un combat au quotidien : doter son village de Sambaye Karang (commune de Mont-Rolland) d’eau pour l’agriculture, l’élevage et les besoins domestiques. Diplômée en agrobusiness, elle multiplie les démarches auprès des autorités et des partenaires. Son rêve : créer une entreprise agricole pour retenir la jeunesse de Mont-Rolland. TIVAOUANE – Il est 14 h 30. Vêtue d’une robe traditionnelle multicolore qui épouse sa taille moyenne, Mame Astou Mbaye porte un foulard noir noué avec soin. Le tissu couvre sa tête et descend jusqu’aux hanches, apportant sobriété et dignité à l’ensemble coloré. Elle s’affaire aux derniers réglages de sa cuisine. Et dire que cette dame a une Licence en Agrobusiness. Après son bac, en 2020, des problèmes techniques l’ont empêchée de s’inscrire à l’université via la plateforme numérique Campusen. Elle s’est alors formée en agrobusiness. Faute de moyens pour le Master, Mame Astou est rentrée au village pour un stage rural. Son ambition : devenir entrepreneuse agricole, créer des emplois et lutter contre l’exode rural des jeunes. En attendant, elle aide sa mère, malade, dans les travaux domestiques qu’elle partage avec sa petite sœur, élève en classe de Première. « Sans eau, on ne peut rien faire » Mame Astou Mbaye est inscrite au Pôle emploi. Elle postule sur les plateformes horticoles et a rencontré des structures d’accompagnement de porteurs de projets. Une demande de financement a aussi été déposée pour que le précieux liquide coule à Sambaye Karang. « Forer coûte trop cher », lui a-t-on répondu. Pourtant, à quelques mètres, l’entreprise Pfo, en charge de l’Autoroute Dakar–Tivaouane–Saint-Louis, a réalisé un forage pour ses travaux. L’eau y coule à flots jour et nuit. Selon les informations recueillies par Mame Astou, Pfo serait prête à céder le forage après les travaux. Mais, seule la mairie pourra en assurer les frais d’entretien. A lire aussi : Autoroute Dakar-Tivaouane-Saint-louis : des populations de Mont-Rolland isolées par le tracé À Sambaye Karang, commune de Mont-Rolland, département de Tivaouane, l’eau est partout désirée. « Les femmes dans leurs foyers, les maraîchers dans leurs périmètres, les abreuvoirs du bétail, tous souffrent péniblement du manque d’eau. Les projets agricoles qui devaient servir d’échappatoire pour l’emploi des jeunes deviennent des épouvantails et sont quasiment tous abandonnés », témoigne la dame. Le réseau de la Sen’Eau s’arrête à l’autre bout du village. Pas de forage, pas de robinet. Les habitants ont tenté une cotisation pour prolonger les tuyaux. Trop cher. Le projet a été abandonné. Le bassin agricole, réalisé dans le cadre du Projet de valorisation des eaux pour le développement de chaînes de valeur (Proval-Cv), en 2021, est lui aussi à l’abandon. Résultat : de nombreux jeunes ont quitté l’agriculture et l’élevage pour chercher du travail dans le chantier de l’autoroute ou à Dakar. Malgré les blocages, Mame Astou Mbaye ne baisse pas les bras. Elle multiplie les appels aux autorités territoriales et étatiques, mais aussi aux partenaires techniques et financiers. « Sans eau, on ne peut rien faire », lance-t-elle. Son message aux jeunes de Sambaye Karang et de Mont-Rolland est clair : « Restez. Il y a du potentiel ici. On peut vivre de la terre si on a de l’eau ». Pour elle, régler le problème de la disponibilité de cette ressource, c’est donner une chance à l’agriculture locale et à toute une génération. Pour l’heure, elle attend et espère voir le bout du tunnel. « Il faut que les autorités nous aident à fixer la jeunesse. Et cela passe par la disponibilité de l’eau, essentielle au développement de l’agriculture et de l’élevage, mais aussi l’allégement des travaux ménagers », souligne-t-elle. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)
