items.title: Oppong Nkrumah demands full disclosure of BoG financing for gold purchase programme
items.description: The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Economy Committee, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, has called on the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to disclose the full amount of monetary financing provided to support the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), following reports of substantial losses linked to the initiative. His call comes after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) disclosed that the central bank’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme recorded losses exceeding **US$1.7 billion** in 2025, despite playing a significant role in boosting Ghana’s foreign exchange reserves. Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, August 5, Mr Oppong Nkrumah argued that while attention had largely focused on the reported losses, there was a need for greater transparency regarding the total amount of money the central bank injected into the programme. He maintained that the public deserved a complete picture of the financial arrangements behind the initiative, particularly the overall value of monetary financing extended to the Ghana Gold Board. The former Minister for Works and Housing further suggested that the financing arrangement could have implications for the wider economy, including the Bank of Ghana’s ongoing liquidity sterilisation measures aimed at reducing excess money in circulation. He also expressed concern over what he described as a lack of full disclosure surrounding the programme, indicating that the Minority Caucus and the New Patriotic Party (NPP) would continue scrutinising the available data. “The other question that we will need to get into eventually is the 1.7 only the loss. What was the gross monetary financing that the Bank of Ghana availed to the Gold Board to be used for this?… In the coming days the Minority and the NPP, as we dig through the numbers some more, we’ll update the nation on what we are finding,” Mr Oppong Nkrumah said. According to the IMF’s 2026 Article IV Consultation and proposed Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI) report, the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme became a major source of foreign exchange inflows and reserve accumulation for the Bank of Ghana, although it also generated losses exceeding US$1.7 billion during the 2025 financial year.

items.title: GNAT urges calm over BECE results, asks dissatisfied candidates to petition WAEC
items.description: The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) has called on parents, candidates and other education stakeholders to remain calm following the release of the 2026 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) results. It urges those with concerns to seek clarification through the appropriate channels rather than making allegations against the West African Examinations Council (WAEC). The Association said while concerns over the results were understandable, they should be addressed through formal petitions to WAEC rather than public speculation or unverified claims. GNAT also appealed to WAEC to provide a comprehensive explanation of the processes it followed in determining the examination results to improve public confidence and understanding. “For us to have a better understanding of the results, I think WAEC will have to explain the processes they normally go through, or the processes that they went through in arriving at this particular conclusion,” the Association said. The teacher union further cautioned against placing excessive pressure on candidates, warning that portraying examinations as a matter of life and death could have serious emotional and psychological consequences for children. “Examination is gradually becoming like a do-or-die affair, and I think that we must be careful. Look, if these things are not managed, these children might not be able to manage their emotions. This can even lead to some of them committing suicide, some of them having health complications and all that,” it said. It therefore urged parents, commentators and education stakeholders to be measured in their reactions whenever examination results are released, stressing that children are often affected by the emotions displayed by adults. “So, as parents, stakeholders, commentators and all the people within this particular space, when the results come, let us be measured,” it added. The General Secretary of GNAT, Thomas Tanko Musah, made the remarks in an interview with TV3 on Wednesday, August 5, in which he encouraged dissatisfied candidates and parents to submit their concerns directly to WAEC rather than resorting to public accusations. He also observed that, in some cases, adults appear more distressed than the candidates themselves, warning that such reactions could negatively influence the emotional well-being of children. “Some people are even more anxious, more aggressive than the children. When the children see you behaving that way, the kind of energy you unleash will negatively affect them. So, we have to be measured in our pronouncements,” he advised.

items.title: Seth Terkper calls for greater use of diaspora remittances to drive Ghana’s development
items.description: Presidential Advisor on the Economy and former Finance Minister, Seth Terkper, has urged Ghana to adopt a more strategic approach to diaspora remittances, arguing that the funds should play a greater role in driving national development and long-term economic transformation. He noted that remittances from Ghanaians living abroad have become an increasingly important source of financing, particularly as Ghana and many other African countries face declining access to concessional loans and grants amid changing global financing conditions. Speaking at the launch of Region 17 under the theme, “Harnessing the Power of the Diaspora to Transform Ghana’s Future,” Mr Terkper said countries transitioning to higher-income status must increasingly depend on domestic resource mobilisation and alternative financing mechanisms to sustain development. He stressed the need to move beyond viewing remittances solely as financial support for families, urging policymakers to assess how diaspora inflows can be harnessed more effectively to stimulate economic growth. According to him, remittances already contribute significantly to sectors such as housing, entrepreneurship, investment and skills transfer, and could have an even greater impact if supported by the right policies. Mr Terkper also observed that the evolving global economic landscape requires Ghana to strengthen its domestic financing capacity, explaining that countries with growing economies are expected to rely less on external assistance and develop sustainable sources of development financing. He acknowledged that Ghana’s recent debt crisis and sovereign default had undermined investor confidence, emphasising the need for consistent economic management and credible policies to rebuild trust among both local and diaspora investors. “We need to diagnose the nature of remittances and how they can benefit Ghana’s development,” Mr Terkper said. The former Finance Minister further pointed to the experience of the so-called “African Lions”, noting that several African economies have demonstrated that sustained economic growth is achievable through sound policies and effective mobilisation of domestic and diaspora resources, even in a challenging global environment.

items.title: UK-based Ghana gov’t-sponsored students to undergo mandatory oath, scholarship validation exercise
items.description: The Ghana High Commission in the United Kingdom has announced a mandatory Oath of Affirmation and Scholarship Validation Exercise for all Ghana Government-sponsored students studying in the UK, following a directive from the Ghana Scholarships Authority (GSA). According to a statement issued by the High Commission’s Education Office, the month-long exercise will take place from Thursday, August 13, to Friday, September 4, 2026, in line with Section 31 of the Ghana Scholarships Authority Act, 2025 (Act 1149) and Section 11 of the Oaths Act, 1972 (NRCD 6). The High Commission explained that under the new law, all beneficiaries of government scholarships pursuing studies outside Ghana are required to personally swear an Oath of Affirmation before a designated officer at a Ghana diplomatic mission. The exercise, it said, forms part of efforts to strengthen accountability, improve oversight of government-sponsored scholarships and ensure beneficiaries honour their obligations under the scholarship scheme. Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Sabah Zita Benson, said students who fail to complete the validation and oath-taking process risk losing access to future scholarship benefits. “We have received second payment quarter, which we will start disbursing soon. But in accordance with the new Act, we are going to validate all students; they will take an oath that they will return to Ghana to serve (breach of the oath will lead to a refund of all monies spent on the student plus interest). Students who fail to comply with validation and oath taking will not be considered going forward,” she said. The High Commission further announced that validation sessions would be organised at selected locations across the UK to make the exercise accessible to students, with details of the venues and appointment schedules to be communicated directly to beneficiaries. The statement also reminded students that participation is compulsory under the Ghana Scholarships Authority Act, warning that failure to comply could attract sanctions, including delays in the payment of tuition fees.

items.title: IMF-reported DGPP losses were necessary for economic recovery – Sagnarigu MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Sagnarigu, Attah Issah, has defended the costs associated with the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), insisting that the losses highlighted by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) were part of the sacrifices required to restore Ghana’s macroeconomic stability. He argued that the programme should not be assessed solely on the financial losses recorded but also on its wider economic impact, including rebuilding the country’s foreign exchange reserves, strengthening the cedi and reducing inflation. Mr Issah explained that government recognised from the outset that stabilising the economy would come at a cost. “We were very clear from day one that there was a cost attached to fiscal stabilisation. There is also a cost to economic growth and development,” he said. He further maintained that the initiative aligned with the Bank of Ghana’s statutory responsibilities. “The Bank of Ghana has two primary mandates. One is to ensure price stability, and the other is to ensure macroeconomic growth and development. Government of Ghana, through the gold purchase programme, believes that those two mandates were met,” he stated. The lawmaker also dismissed suggestions that the programme’s benefits were superficial, arguing that falling inflation had delivered tangible gains for ordinary Ghanaians. “If your inflation at a point was about 54% or 33.8%, now you are having about 5%. That is a savings in your nominal income,” he said. Mr Issah made the remarks on Citi FM on Wednesday, August 5, while responding to an IMF assessment that the expansion of the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme resulted in losses exceeding $1.7 billion in 2025, equivalent to about 1.5% of Ghana’s gross domestic product. The Fund noted that although the programme became the Bank of Ghana’s largest source of foreign exchange inflows and reserve accumulation, the associated costs further weakened the central bank’s already negative equity position. He also defended the exchange rate incentives and premiums offered under the programme, describing them as deliberate policy measures designed to channel gold through official systems and curb smuggling. “The position should therefore not be reduced to just a line, Ghana lost money by buying gold, or something like, oh, the domestic gold purchase programme has landed the country into more debt,” he said. “We deliberately inflicted this loss on ourselves so that we save smuggling,” he added.

items.title: Ex-Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib's home attacked after joining Hasina's first public media event since ouster
items.description: Windows were smashed and petrol bombs hurled at former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan’s residence after he joined ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s first public media interaction since her 2024 removal from power, in which she vowed to return in December. Police said a group of people attacked Shakib’s ancestral home in Magura town, about 170 km (105 miles) southwest of the capital Dhaka on Wednesday, causing a fire on the upper floor of the residence. The property was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported. The attack came hours after Shakib, a former Awami League lawmaker, joined a virtual event organised by the Foreign Correspondents Club of South Asia in New Delhi. During the audio address, Hasina reiterated that she would return to Bangladesh, where she has been sentenced to death. Shakib, who was elected to parliament as an Awami League candidate in January 2024, has remained outside Bangladesh since the student-led uprising that toppled Hasinas government. He faces multiple investigations, including over allegations of murder, embezzlement, fraud and money laundering. “I will return to my people,” Hasina said. “I know that they may put me in jail or they may kill me, but still I have to go back.” The event, held on the second anniversary of her ouster, was Hasina’s first public interaction with the media since she fled Bangladesh in 2024. Hasina also said the ban on the Awami League, the party she led for more than four decades, should be lifted after it was barred from political activity following her ouster. Bangladesh’s foreign ministry condemned Hasina’s media appearance, describing it as an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and warning that allowing her to address the media from India could harm bilateral relations. Hasina, 78, has been living in New Delhi since August 2024. Bangladesh has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is being examined under its legal procedures. In November 2025, the country’s war crimes tribunal sentenced her to death in absentia over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 student-led uprising, charges she has dismissed as politically motivated.

NPP’s ‘Democracy Under Attack’ demonstration comes off today
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) will today, Thursday, August 6, stage its planned nationwide demonstration dubbed “Democracy Under Attack”, as the party raises concerns over what it describes as threats to Ghana’s democratic governance. The protest is scheduled to begin at 6:00 a.m. at the Supreme Court and end at the Jubilee House, according to promotional materials released by the party. Organisers are mobilising supporters under the hashtags #DemocracyUnderAttack, #SaveGhanaNow and #SayNoToStateCapture. The NPP has said the demonstration is intended to draw attention to issues including alleged restrictions on free expression, concerns over the treatment of opposition voices and what it describes as threats to democratic institutions. In a Facebook post, spokesperson for former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and NPP communications team member, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said the protest is aimed at resisting what he described as attempts to suppress dissent and undermine democratic values. “There is always the temptation by people in power to suppress the voices and rights of the people. But there is an inherent self-purge with democracy. Try as you may, you can never suppress the will of the people,” he wrote. Mr Aboagye further alleged that issues such as what he described as “rampant arrests of opposition voices”, the detention of some individuals over alleged insults, the arrest of TikTok users and media practitioners, the use of bail conditions, and concerns about the relationship between the Executive and the Judiciary pose a threat to Ghana’s democracy. He called for equal application of the law and urged authorities to avoid what he termed selective justice. “Let’s stop the selective justice now before it becomes a cycle. Power is like ice…. Live and let’s live… that’s the beauty of democracy,” he added. The NPP maintains that the demonstration is to defend civil liberties, the rule of law and democratic accountability. The government, however, has rejected claims of targeting political opponents, insisting that state institutions operate independently and that law enforcement actions are guided by due process.

items.title: GAF observes maiden Omane Boamah memorial lecture
items.description: The Ghana Armed Forces on Tuesday observed the maiden annual memorial public lecture in honour of the late Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah at the Burma Camp in Accra. Dr Omane Boamah and seven other public officials lost their lives in a military helicopter crash at Adansi Akrofuom in the Ashanti Region on August 6th, 2025, while on a national assignment. Among the dignitaries that grace the maiden annual memorial public lecture were Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, Dr Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Presidency and Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson, the Finance Minister and Acting Defence Minister. Also in attendance were service chiefs and old students from the Pope John Senior High School and Junior Seminary, Koforidua where the late Defence Minister schooled. The maiden public lecture, which was chaired by Nana Dr Emmanuel Adu-Sarkodee, the President of the Ghana Employers’ Association and Akwamu Manwerehene, had two main speakers. Reverend Father Dr Ebenezer Akesseh, the Parish Priest of Christ the King Parish of the Catholic Church, Accra, delivered the first lecture on the topic “Selfless Leadership in Public Service: Lessons from the Life and Legacy of the late Dr Omane Boamah”. Whereas Professor Kwasi Appeaning Addo, a former Director of the Institute of Environment and Sanitation Studies, Department of Marine and Fisheries Science, University of Ghana, delivered the second lecture on the topic “Accra Beyond the Floods: Rethinking Enforcement, Urban Planning and Community Resilience”. Rev. Dr Akesseh in his presentation described public service as a vocation and a divine calling to serve humanity rather than a profession pursued for personal gain. He reiterated that the late Dr Omane Boamah exemplified servant leadership by dedicating his talents, medical expertise and political career to the service of Ghana, adding that Dr Omane Boamah consistently placed the needs of others above his own interests. Rev. Dr Akesseh cited an instance where the late minister interrupted his journey to personally assist a woman in distress and ensured she received urgent medical care, demonstrating that compassion must always be accompanied by action. He said Dr Omane Boamah viewed leadership as a moral responsibility rooted in integrity, humility and accountability; declaring that throughout his career, the late Dr Boamah earned the trust of his colleagues and the public by remaining transparent, rejecting corruption and making decisions based on national interest rather than personal or political advantage. Prof. Addo in his presentation made a call to action for the Accra Beyond the Floods Equation, saying in honouring the legacy of the late Defence Minister, a climate resilient Accra could be realised by combining disciplined urban order with progressive engineering. This would secure the capital against flood disaster, building on its early foundational work, by leading national environmental investigations and tree planting campaigns, the vision to transition Accra from reactive crisis management to a highly regulated sustainable city, he said. He stressed that the proposed Accra flood resilience strategy could integrate natural infrastructure; AI driven enforcement and community led action to transition into a secure and sustainable capital. Prof. Addo said the transformation of Ghana’s capital from a flood prone city to a climate resilient one, could not be achieved through isolated efforts, but required a unified front where policy, tradition, advocacy and civic duty intersected to secure the city’s future. “The mandate for each stakeholder group is clear and immediate. To our policy makers, please lead with courage and integrity and enforce without fear or favor. Utilise the digital planning and GIS mapping to permanently lock out unauthorized construction in our towers,” he said. He urged the nation’s traditional leaders to protect natural purpose by acting as strong custodians of their lands, refusing the sale of wetlands and flood plains to developers, to ensure social accountability, ensuring that ecological zoning laws were respected at every local level. Prof. Addo encouraged civil society and the media to champion truth and equity, as well as maintain continuous independence oversight on the prosecution of corrupt planning officials. He also urged them to drive public education by keeping climate adaptation and waste management sensitisation at the forefront of public discourse. “To our citizens, stop the practice of damping solid and plastic waste into their dreams. Take active charge of your neighborhood’s cleanliness,” calling on people to volunteer as community-led early warning and disaster response teams, refusing the purchase of land in flood plains. He appealed to them to act as whistle blowers on illegal development that threatened their community’s safety; declaring that this was their collective action. Prof. Addo stated that “either we continue down the path of a chaotic expansion and recurrent disaster, or we can choose the path of structural discipline, environmental harmony and systemic progress,” calling on all to collaborate to build a proud order.

items.title: REGSEC to begin fresh demolitions at Laboma, Agbogbloshie to curb flooding
items.description: The Greater Accra Regional Security Council (REGSEC) is set to begin another phase of demolition exercises next week at Laboma and Agbogbloshie, targeting structures built on waterways as part of ongoing efforts to reduce flooding in Accra. The exercise follows recent clean-up campaigns, desilting of drains and earlier demolitions carried out after the devastating June 29 floods that affected several parts of the capital. Speaking after touring a number of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), the Greater Accra Regional Minister, Linda Ocloo, said the government remains determined to reclaim waterways and remove illegal structures contributing to persistent flooding. She explained that the exercise forms part of a broader strategy to restore buffer zones, improve drainage infrastructure and minimise the risk of future floods in the city. According to the Minister, authorities have identified several unauthorised structures that will have to be removed to allow for the restoration of waterways and improve the free flow of stormwater. “We have noticed that a lot of the buildings must come down and so we will do a major demolition over there, hopefully next week. We want to create the buffer like we said. We can see that the refuse was caused by the squatters over there. Once we clear the place, we wouldn’t have issues there,” Ms Ocloo said. She reaffirmed the government’s commitment to strictly enforcing planning regulations and removing structures that obstruct waterways as part of long-term measures to address flooding in the Greater Accra Region.

items.title: New US policy gives officials more power to reject immigration filings
items.description: WASHINGTON: Immigrants seeking work permits, green cards, or changes of status could face a greater risk of having their applications denied under a new US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) policy that took effect on August 5. The policy, announced by USCIS on Wednesday, gives immigration officials broader discretion to deny incomplete applications without first allowing applicants an opportunity to submit missing documents or other required evidence. The new policy applies to a wide range of applications handled by USCIS, including those for green cards, work permits, US citizenship, travel documents, and other immigration-related approvals. Under the revised guidance, applicants must prove they qualify for the immigration status or approval they are seeking and submit all required supporting documents when they file their application. If they fail to do so, USCIS officers may deny the application without first issuing a request for evidence (RFE) or a notice of intent to deny (NOID), both of which previously allowed applicants to correct mistakes or provide missing documents. USCIS said the change restores officers’ discretion under long-standing Department of Homeland Security regulations and reverses a Biden-era policy that generally encouraged officers to request additional evidence before denying an incomplete application. According to the agency, the previous policy allowed some people to file incomplete or “placeholder” applications to obtain temporary immigration advantages, such as work authorisation while waiting to submit the required evidence. It said the new policy will help reduce frivolous filings, improve efficiency, and shorten processing times for applicants who submit complete applications. For many South Asian immigrants, the change could have important practical consequences, as they account for a large number of family-sponsored and employment-based immigration applications. Many also apply for work permits, adjustment of status to permanent residence, naturalisation, and other immigration services provided by USCIS. Immigration lawyers say these applications often require extensive documentation. Under the new policy, forgetting to include a required document or failing to demonstrate eligibility at the time of filing is more likely to result in an immediate denial. However, the policy does not change who qualifies for a green card, work permit, citizenship or any other immigration status. The updated policy applies to immigration applications that were pending or filed on or after Aug 5 unless a specific law or USCIS regulation provides otherwise.

items.title: Social media, drug abuse fuelling student indiscipline – Deputy Education Minister
items.description: The Deputy Minister for Education, Dr Clement Apaak, has identified social media, the misuse of mobile phones and the growing abuse of narcotics and other unapproved substances as major factors driving indiscipline among students. His remarks come in the wake of an incident at Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, where students allegedly attacked the school’s headmaster over claims that a baby’s body had been buried on the school premises. Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, August 5, Dr Apaak said student misconduct was being fuelled by a combination of influences, including unrestricted exposure to inappropriate online content and increasing peer pressure. He explained that many young people are constantly exposed to disturbing behaviour on social media platforms, which can create the false impression that such actions carry little or no consequences. “Some of the issues that came up, and I believe some to be true, are the negative influence of social media and the abuse of the modern cell phone,” he said. According to the Deputy Minister, students are increasingly consuming content that normalises unacceptable behaviour, making them more likely to imitate what they see. “Students are able to see all manner of behaviours, no matter how condemnable and abhorrent, both from within the jurisdiction and beyond. And somehow they begin to get a feeling that they can also act in such manners and get away with it,” he stated. Dr Apaak also expressed concern over the increasing use of narcotics and unauthorised substances among young people, describing it as a growing challenge that extends beyond senior high schools. “We also have the incessant danger of the use of narcotics and other unapproved medical substances. This is a very serious issue that is also plaguing our youth,” he said. He noted that the problem affects students across different levels of the education system, including junior high schools and tertiary institutions, and warned that some products sold as energy drinks may contain harmful mixtures capable of influencing behaviour. “You see them holding these energy drinks, and you might think that it is just an energy drink. But that is a potent concoction of a combination of all kinds of substances,” he added.

items.title: Four Peshawar High Court additional judges cease to function as president delays their service confirmation
items.description: PESHAWAR: Four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court have ceased to function as the president of Pakistan has yet to give assent to the confirmation of their services as recommended by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP). The four judges, including Justice Farah Jamshed, Justice Inamullah Khan, Justice Sabitullah Khan and Justice Aurangzeb, were appointed as additional judges for a period of one year and they had taken oath of their offices on Feb 4, 2025. On the JCP’s recommendations early this year, their service terms as additional judges were extended for six months. The time ended on Aug 4. In a meeting on July 20, the JCP recommended confirmation of the services of the said four judges under Article 175(A) of the Constitution. Article 175(A)(8) declares: “The Commission, by the majority of its total membership, shall nominate one person for each vacancy of a Judge in the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, a High Court or the Federal Shariat Court, as the case may be, to the Prime Minister who shall forward the same to the President for appointment.” However, no deadline has been set for the president to give assent to the recommendations received from the prime minister. Official sources said that the Peshawar High Court was also in contact with the law ministry on the situation arising from the delay in the presidential nod to the JDC recommendations. They said no case had been assigned to any of these four judges since Aug 3. An official insisted that judicial work couldn’t be assigned to those judges unless the relevant notification was issued by the government. PHC Bar Association president Ameenur Rehman Yousafzai has called upon the president to give assent to the recommendations to pave the way for issuance of the relevant notification by the federal government so as to end the impasse. He told reporters that in light of the Constitution and superior court judgements, the President couldn’t withhold the summary and it was binding on him to give assent to it. Mr Yousafzai said that it was the constitutional powers of the JCP to recommend service confirmation of judges after due consideration of the relevant data forms, antecedents, and evaluation of the material placed before it. He said that the PHC was already short of judges and delaying the matter would affect the day-to-day affairs of the high court and would also result in an increasing backlog of pending cases. The four judges were initially appointed as additional judges along with six others, who have already been confirmed as the regular high court judges in Feb this year. Justice Jamshed was the lone woman judge in the PHC. Both Justice Jamshed and Justice Inamullah Khan were senior judicial officers prior to their elevation to the bench. They belong to Mansehra and Bannu districts, respectively. Once the relevant notification is issued of their service confirmation as regular judges, the retirement of Justice Jamshed and Justice Inamullah will take place in Jan 2032 and Sept 2029, respectively. Both of them had joined the judicial service in1994 as civil judges. They were promoted as additional district and sessions judges in 2007 and subsequently as district and sessions judges in 2011. In over three-decade long judicial careers, they held key positions. Justice Jamshed was also the first woman director general of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Judicial Academy. Justice Inamullah also served as the additional registrar of the PHC’s Dera Ismail Khan Bench. The other two judges, including Justice Sabitullah and Justice Aurangzeb, were prominent lawyers enjoying respect in the legal fraternity. After service confirmation, they will retire in Dec 2033 and Dec 2039, respectively. Published in Dawn, August 6th, 2026

items.title: IMF urges BoG to end quasi-fiscal activitiess after GH¢22bn DGPP losses
items.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to end quasi-fiscal activities following losses recorded under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). The Fund said the DGPP recorded losses of GHS22 billion in 2025, equivalent to about 1.5 per cent of Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), weakening the central bank’s financial position. The IMF said the losses, together with other factors, increased the BoG’s negative equity position to 6.7 per cent of GDP by the end of 2025. It said safeguarding the independence and credibility of the central bank required the permanent cessation of quasi-fiscal operations and the full transfer of the DGPP to GoldBod. The DGPP was introduced to strengthen Ghana’s gold and foreign exchange reserves through the purchase of gold from local miners. Although the programme contributed to higher reserves, the Fund said it also imposed significant financial costs on the central bank. In July 2026, the Government, the BoG and GoldBod signed an agreement transferring all DGPP activities from the central bank to GoldBod. Under the arrangement, GoldBod will assume responsibility for purchasing gold and meeting all operational costs, while the BoG will focus on its core mandate. The IMF welcomed the transfer, stating that it would eliminate future financial risks from the central bank’s balance sheet and enhance transparency in the management of the programme. The Fund also called for the recapitalisation of the central bank, noting that a strong financial position was essential to maintaining price stability and confidence in the economy. An independent audit of the DGPP is underway, with its findings expected later this year.

items.title: La rougeole explose aux États-Unis de Donald Trump
items.description: « La médecine est une science sociale, et la politique n’est rien de moins que de la médecine à très grande échelle », écrivait Rudolf Virchow Die medicinische Reform , n° 2, 10 juillet 1848, p. 2. Trad. fr. de l'auteur. Sur ce mot d'ordre, voir Erwin H. Ackerknecht, Rudolf Virchow : Doctor, Statesman, Anthropologist , University of Wisconsin Press, 1953.'> 1 . C’est sous ce prisme que se lit la résurgence de la rougeole aux États-Unis. Avec 285 cas en 2024, 2 289 en 2025, soit des chiffres inédits depuis 1992, et déjà plus de 2 300 à l'été 2026, nous assistons à un pic jamais observé depuis 1991 « Measles Cases and Outbreaks » , CDC, données consultées en août 2026. Voir aussi « US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year’s total » , ABC News, 24 juillet 2026 ; « US measles cases reach 35-year high » , CNN , 24 juillet 2026.'> 2 . Cette flambée coïncide avec la prise de fonction de Robert F. Kennedy Jr. au poste de secrétaire à la Santé, en février 2025. Les éléments nécessaires à ce retour de la maladie étaient déjà présents, documentés, et faisaient l’objet de nombreux appels à l'action. Ainsi de part son silence et son refus d’agir, son rôle, tout comme celui de l’administration Trump dans cette poursuite du retour de la maladie, ne fait aucun doute. Les États-Unis, premier pays à avoir officiellement « éliminé » la rougeole en 2000, sont désormais jugés « très susceptibles » de perdre ce statut à l'automne 2026, si les chaînes de transmission se prolongent au-delà de douze mois. Ils rejoindraient ainsi une tendance déjà amorcée en 2019 par le Royaume-Uni, la Grèce, la République tchèque et l'Albanie, des pays développés où la rougeole est de nouveau endémique en raison d'une couverture vaccinale insuffisante « US ‘highly likely’ to lose measles elimination status this fall, analysis warns » , CIDRAP (University of Minnesota), juillet 2026 ; « Will the USA lose its measles elimination status ? » , The Lancet, 2026.'> 3 . À l'inverse d'autres pathologies infectieuses, la rougeole est un virus peu létal, mais elle n'est en aucun cas anodine. Ainsi, avec une létalité de l’ordre d’un décès pour mille cas, soit trois morts en 2025 et aucun décès recensé à ce jour en 2026, c'est sans doute ce qui nourrit un faux sentiment de non-dangerosité, qui constitue l'un des principaux obstacles aux politiques vaccinales « Measles » , fiche d’information, CDC, « Measles Cases and Outbreaks » , op. cit.'> 4 . Il s'agit pourtant de l'un des agents pathogènes les plus contagieux connus. Son taux de reproduction (R0) est estimé entre 12 et 18, ce qui signifie qu'une personne infectée en contamine en moyenne quinze autres, un chiffre qui est encore plus élevé au sein de communautés peu vaccinées « The basic reproduction number (R0) of measles : a systematic review » , The Lancet Infectious Diseases, 2017.'> 5 . À titre de comparaison, le taux de reproduction du Covid-19 était estimé à 2,5 ou 3 pour la souche initiale de 2020, et à 8 ou 10 pour le variant Omicron, le plus contagieux. De plus, la morbidité, elle, est loin d’être négligeable. Avec un taux d’hospitalisation d’autour de 9 % en 2025/2026, une épidémie qui se propage rapidement peut entraîner l'hospitalisation de plusieurs centaines de personnes, parfois en soins intensifs. Une surcharge qui pèserait sur un système de santé déjà sous tension « Measles Cases and Outbreaks » , op. cit. ; « Measles Hospitalizations Fell This Year Even as Case Counts Hit a 35-Year High » , Medical Daily, 2026.'> 6 . Les nourrissons de 6 à 12 mois forment « l'angle mort » de la protection. Trop âgés pour bénéficier des anticorps maternels, trop jeunes pour être vaccinés, ils dépendent entièrement de l'immunité collective et sont les premiers touchés quand celle-ci diminue « Measles » , op. cit.'> 7 . Pour comprendre le risque que représente une personne atteinte de la rougeole pour la santé publique, il faut connaître la notion d'« amnésie immunitaire ». La principale raison de s'alarmer tient ainsi à un phénomène mis en évidence par deux études parues dans Science Measles virus infection diminishes preexisting antibodies that offer protection from other pathogens », Science , vol. 366, n° 6465, 1er novembre 2019, p. 599-606, et V. N. Petrova et al., « Incomplete genetic reconstitution of B cell pools contributes to prolonged immunosuppression after measles », Science Immunology , vol. 4, n° 41, 1er novembre 2019. Ces travaux confirment sur le plan mécanistique l'hypothèse épidémiologique formulée dans M. J. Mina et al., « Long-term measles-induced immunomodulation increases overall childhood infectious disease mortality », Science , vol. 348, n° 6235, 8 mai 2015.'> 8 : le virus infecte les cellules du système immunitaire via la protéine de surface CD150 — « comme le SARS-CoV-2 utilise ACE2 » pour pénétrer les cellules pulmonaires texte intégral .'> 9 . En détruisant les lymphocytes « mémoire », il efface une partie de l'immunité acquise. On pourrait dire que la rougeole arrache des pages au carnet de vaccination biologique de l'organisme : le système immunitaire tient normalement à jour la liste des microbes déjà rencontrés pour pouvoir réagir rapidement en cas d'une nouvelle attaque. Privé de cette mémoire, l'individu doit « réapprendre » à se défendre contre des infections qu'il maîtrisait déjà, ce qui entraîne une surexposition aux maladies et une surmortalité dans les deux à trois ans qui suivent l'infection. Les auteurs de l’étude évoquent prudemment un « mini effet VIH », tout en soulignant que les différences avec ce dernier l’emportent largement sur les similitudes « Measles virus infection diminishes preexisting antibodies that offer protection from other pathogens » , Science, vol. 366, n° 6465, 1er novembre 2019, p. 599-606, doi:10.1126/science.aay6485. Voir aussi V. N. Petrova et al. et la synthèse « Measles increases the risk of other infections » , Nature Reviews Microbiology, 2019.'> 10 . Cumulée aux hospitalisations et à la désorganisation économique et psychologique qu’elles entraînent, cette surmortalité indirecte fait de l’épidémie actuelle une « véritable bombe à retardement » pour le système de santé américain. D'autant plus que les États-Unis comptaient plus de 500 000 cas déclarés par an dans les années 1950, et que la résurgence de 1989-1991 avait culminé autour de 27 000 cas en 1990 séries historiques MMWR ; « Measles cases in the U.S. break a 33-year record » , Los Angeles Times , 24 juillet 2026.'> 11 . Avant d'être nommé secrétaire à la Santé par Donald Trump, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. avait relayé le récit scientifiquement discrédité d'un lien entre vaccins et autisme, affirmé qu'« il n'existe pas de vaccins sûrs et efficaces » et conseillé aux parents de ne pas faire vacciner leurs enfants « RFK Jr. disparaged vaccines dozens of times in recent years, misled on race » , The Washington Post , 28 janvier 2025. Sur le retrait des études fondant le lien vaccins-autisme, voir BMJ 2026, doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-595295 .'> 12 . Confirmé de justesse par le Sénat (52 voix contre 48), il a vu le Parti républicain se diviser : le sénateur Mitch McConnell, seul républicain à avoir voté contre, a précisément fait ce choix à cause de ses positions sur la politique vaccinale. Le sénateur et médecin Bill Cassidy ne l’a soutenu qu’à condition de « le tenir à l’œil » « Senate confirms RFK Jr. as Health secretary ; McConnell lone GOP dissenter » , The Hill, 13 février 2025 ; « Bill Cassidy, lifelong vaccination advocate, on voting for RFK Jr. » , ABC News, 2025. Sur la fracture du parti républicain, voir Forbes , 16 novembre 2021, et Politico , 23 septembre 2023.'> 13 . Sous la pression du Congrès, RFK Jr. a alors opéré un virage à 180 degrés, niant ses propos passés, notamment son affirmation selon laquelle « il n’existe pas de vaccins sûrs et efficaces » « Fact-checking RFK Jr.’s confirmation hearing » , CNN , 1er février 2025.'> 14 . On pourrait ainsi dire que sa ligne actuelle est celle d'un « antivax modéré, passif-agressif ». Sur le site des CDC, il fait afficher que « deux doses offrent la meilleure protection possible » contre la rougeole « About Measles » .'> 15 , tout en retirant la mention selon laquelle les vaccins ne causent pas l'autisme. Cette mention a été remplacée, fin 2025, par une formulation laissant entendre que ce lien n'a pas été exclu « The CDC revives debunked « link » between childhood vaccines and autism » , NPR , 20 novembre 2025 ; Aaron Pellish, « RFK Jr. vaccines autism CDC » , Politico , 21 novembre 2025 ; CDC, « Autism and Vaccines » .'> 16 . Ce double langage répond à une équation politique. Il s'agit de ménager la conviction de Donald Trump quant au lien entre vaccins et autisme, sans provoquer la fronde des élus républicains sensibles à l'argument médical. Sa proximité affichée avec le quarterback antivax Aaron Rodgers, qu'il envisageait comme colistier lors de la campagne de 2024, illustrait déjà cette stratégie « RFK Jr. praises Aaron Rodgers amid VP speculation » , ABC News, 2024. Ben Morse, « RFK Jr. is considering Aaron Rodgers for a 2024 running mate » , CNN, 22 mai 2024. Sur le statut vaccinal de Rodgers en 2021, Chris Bengel, « Aaron Rodgers admits he misled public by saying he was ‘immunized’ » , CBS Sports , novembre 2021.'> 17 . Cette stratégie de l'inaction peut être mieux comprise en la comparant à la crise de la rougeole du début des années 1990. Lors de l’épidémie de 1989-1991, qui culmina à quelque 27 000 cas en 1990, le secrétaire à la Santé de George H. W. Bush, le Dr Louis Sullivan, avait mobilisé trois leviers : l’achat massif de vaccins à prix négociés et leur distribution gratuite sur l’ensemble du territoire, l’obligation vaccinale stricte pour les soignants et une campagne de communication univoque « Louis Wade Sullivan (1989-1993) » , « Six areas lead national early immunization drive » , PubMed, 1992.'> 18 . Face à la flambée de 2026, RFK Jr. n'utilise aucun levier fédéral : sa seule réponse est une recommandation vaccinale maintenue sur le site des CDC, accompagnée de déclarations ambiguës. Il substitue ainsi la liberté de choix individuelle à l'action publique. L'inaction de RFK Jr. s'apparente à une hostilité vaccinale qui ne dit pas son nom, et qui est d'autant plus efficace qu'elle n'offre aucune prise directe à ses contradicteurs. Le virus de la rougeole ne touche pas des individus isolés, mais des communautés. Alors que la moyenne nationale de couverture vaccinale cache de fortes disparités locales, c'est à cette échelle que le problème se pose. Dans les années 1990, la non-vaccination était principalement due à des obstacles matériels (coût, accès). En 2025-2026, elle résulte de choix délibérés, souvent d'ordre politique ou religieux. RFK Jr. lui-même l'a reconnu sur CNN : « Les communautés touchées sont presque toutes des communautés religieuses qui, tout simplement, ne se vaccinent pas » « RFK Jr., Fauci and medical misinformation » , CNN , 2 août 2026.'> 19 . Or, ces populations ont tendance à vivre ensemble, ce qui fait chuter la couverture locale bien en deçà du seuil d'immunité collective. Chaque communauté devient ainsi une sorte de réserve de combustible, il ne lui manque qu'une étincelle pour s'enflammer. Celle-ci vient presque toujours de l'extérieur : un membre de la communauté, contaminé lors d'un court déplacement, souvent professionnel, réimporte le virus dans un milieu à la fois très peu vacciné et très dense en contacts. De là, une propagation en chaîne, de cluster en cluster, d'une communauté à une autre. Sur les quelque 2 300 cas actuels, environ 1 300 sont liés à des chaînes de transmission qui n'ont jamais été interrompues depuis 2025. Cette situation devrait se poursuivre tant que le gouvernement fédéral n'agira pas. L’article La rougeole explose aux États-Unis de Donald Trump est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Pakistan launches effort to trace missing boxer Qudratullah after Commonwealth Gam­es in Glasgow
items.description: PAKISTAN boxer Qudratullah LAHORE: Pakistan auth­orities have launched a high-level effort to trace boxer Qudratullah, who failed to return home with the national contingent at the Commonwealth Gam­es in Glasgow, well-informed sources told Dawn on Wednesday. The disappearance of the 20-year-old boxer, who competed in the men’s 60kg category, is being treated as a high-profile case, the sources said. “Until around 2:00am in Glasgow, when the contingent was due to leave for Pakistan the following morning, every member of the contingent was present at one place,” a member of the Pakistan contingent told Dawn on condition of anonymity. “Later in the night, as the Games organisers had provided separate accommodation for each athlete, everyone returned to their respective rooms. Qudratullah also went to his room,” the source added. “The passports and air tickets of all contingent mem­bers, including Qudra­tullah, were in the custody of the head of the contingent. Despite taking all the preventive measures that the contingent management could, Qudratullah still managed to disappear. It is extremely unfortunate and has tarnished the country’s image,” the official said. Government agencies are making serious efforts to trace the boxer, the source said, adding: “The authorities are trying to determine Qudratullah’s whereabouts. If he intends to apply for asylum, it may not be possible under the circumstances.” Sources said that since British authorities issued six-month visas to all members of the Pakistani contingent, they may not treat the case as urgent until the visa validity nears its expiry. Qudratullah, who is associated with the department of Pakistan Army, lost to Northern Ireland’s Jude Gallagher in the men’s 60kg category during the Games. Pakistan returned from Glasgow with only one medal — a bronze won by boxer Fatima Zahra in the women’s 60kg category. This is not the first such incident involving Paki­stani athletes. During the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, two Pakistani boxers failed to return home with the national contingent. In 2024, boxer Zohaib Rasheed went missing in Italy while representing Pakistan at an Olympic qualifying event. Despite repeated atte­mpts, no official of the Pakistan Boxing Fede­ration could be contacted for comment. Published in Dawn, August 6th, 2026
